Accounts: retrieval by login, with entity storage (example 28): [findOneBy(critères)] returns the single entity that matches the criteria, or [null]; addition and deletion.

docs.title: 11.11. The Business Layer
docs.text: The business layer brings together business rules and transactions (Example 28). It is described by an interface, implemented by two classes: [MetierService], the business layer itself, and [ApplicationModel], the web layer cache (discussed later).

docs.title: 11.11.1. src/Metier/Dates.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Metier/Dates.php: today’s date. It is used for RÈGLES, DE, and GESTION (no
// past appointments; only one appointment per patient at VENIR): it resides
// in the business layer. The web layer reuses it.

namespace App\Metier;

use DateTimeImmutable;

class Dates
{
     // today at midnight, in the application’s time zone (see src/Kernel.php)
    public static function aujourdhui(): DateTimeImmutable
    {
        return new DateTimeImmutable('today');
    }
}

The current date at midnight (['today']), in the application’s time zone (see [src/Kernel.php]). It is used for business rules (no past reservations, only one upcoming appointment): it resides in the business layer. A static method ([static]) is called without creating an object: [Dates::aujourdhui()].

docs.title: 11.11.2. src/Metier/MetierException.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Metier/MetierException.php: the exception thrown by the business layer when a
// RÈGLE DE GESTION is violated (username already taken, doctor who still has
// appointment, slot already reserved...). It does not contain text, but a
// CLÉ translation string (e.g., "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"): it is the web layer that
// will translate it into French or English when the page is displayed (see translations).
//
// A MetierException is not an error: it is a normal response ("this login
// is already taken”), displayed to the user. Any other exception is a true
// error, which results in a 500 error page.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Metier;

use RuntimeException;
use Throwable;

class MetierException extends RuntimeException
{
    public function __construct(
         // message translation key
        public readonly string $cle,
         // any parameters for the message ({minutes}...)
        public readonly array $parametres = [],
        ?Throwable $previous = null,
    ) {
        parent::__construct($cle, 0, $previous);
    }
}

The exception thrown when a business rule is violated. It does not carry text, but rather a translation key ([ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN]) and its parameters: the web layer will translate it into the page’s language (Example 22). The business layer knows nothing about the interface languages. [RuntimeException] is a subclass of [PHP]. The constructor properties [public readonly] are declared and initialized by the constructor promotion (Example 03); [parent::__construct($cle, 0, $previous)] calls the constructor of [RuntimeException], passing the message, the code, and the previous exception (the one that caused this one—a database error, for example: it appears in the log along with the new one).

docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Metier/Metier.php: the CONTRAT from the business layer: read operations, calendar,
// appointments, doctor and client management.
//
// A INTERFACE describes the methods a class must have, without specifying how
// they are written. MetierService (the business layer) and ApplicationModel (the cache
// of the web layer) both implement it; PHP checks, when loading
// the class, that no methods are missing.
//
// ?Type: a result that may be absent (null: a doctor who does not exist...).
// list<Medecin> (in a comment /** */): an array of doctors, indexed 0, 1, 2...
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Metier;

use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Creneau;
use App\Entity\Medecin;
use App\Entity\Rv;
use DateTimeImmutable;

interface Metier
{
     // ------------------------------------------------ readings
     /** @return list<Client> */
    public function getAllClients(): array;

     /** @return list<Doctor> */
    public function getAllMedecins(): array;

     /** @return list<Time Slot> */
    public function getAllCreneaux(int $idMedecin): array;

     /** @return list<Appointment> */
    public function getRvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour): array;

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client;

    public function getMedecinById(int $id): ?Medecin;

    public function getRvById(int $id): ?Rv;

    public function getCreneauById(int $id): ?Creneau;

    public function getAgendaMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour): ?AgendaMedecinJour;

     // the client (patient) whose user account is [$idUser]
    public function getClientByUserId(int $idUser): ?Client;

     // a client’s appointments—current or future—with time slot and doctor
     /** @return list<Rv> */
    public function getRvAVenirClient(int $idClient): array;

     // ------------------------------------------------ appointments (ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER)
     // triggers a MetierException if:
       // - the day has passed ("ERRORS.PAST_DATE");
       // - the patient already has an upcoming appointment ("ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT");
       // - the time slot is already booked for that day ("ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED").
    public function ajouterRv(DateTimeImmutable $jour, Creneau $creneau, Client $client): Rv;

    public function supprimerRv(Rv $rv): void;

     // ------------------------------------------------ doctors (ADMIN)
     // creates a user account for the doctor ET (role DOCTOR)
    public function ajouterMedecin(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin;

     // modifies the doctor ET's user account
    public function modifierMedecin(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin;

     // deletes the doctor, his time slots, and his account (ET) — rejected if he has appointments
    public function supprimerMedecin(int $id): void;

     // ------------------------------------------------ clients
     // (ADMIN; ajouterClient is also used to register a patient,
     // modifierClient and supprimerClient for the patient to create their own account)
     //creates the client ET and their user account (role USER)
    public function ajouterClient(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client;

    public function modifierClient(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client;

     // deletes the client, their account ET, and all their appointments (past and future)
    public function supprimerClient(int $id): void;
}

The business layer contract: an interface (example 06), the list of methods, without their code. Read operations return entities or arrays of entities (the comment [@return list<Client>] specifies their content); [?Client]: a client, or [null] if it does not exist. The comments specify the rules for each write operation and the keys of the [MetierException] entities it may raise.

docs.text:
<?php
// src/Metier/Descripteur.php: everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client for the
// management rules (see MetierService). Doctors and clients follow the
// same rules: the common code is written UNE times and configured by a descriptor.

namespace App\Metier;

use App\Dao\PersonneDao;
use App\Entity\Role;
use Closure;

readonly class Descripteur
{
    public function __construct(
        public PersonneDao $dao,
        public Role $role,              // DOCTOR or USER
         // the entity class, to create a person: Medecin::class or Client::class
        public string $classe,
        public string $cleIntrouvable,  // message if the person does not exist
        public string $cleExisteDeja,   // message if the same first and last names already exist
         // optional (null): if present, deletion is REFUSÉE as long as the
         // person has appointments (compterRv(id) > 0), with the message cleAvecRv
        public ?Closure $compterRv,
        public ?string $cleAvecRv,
         // optional: what to delete for the person (the rows that
         // via a foreign key); receives their ID
        public ?Closure $avantSuppression,
    ) {
    }
}

Doctors and clients follow the same management rules, with a few minor differences: the DAO, the account role, the class of the entity to be created, the error messages, and the deletion rule. This descriptor consolidates these details; the common code reads them. Two properties are functions ([?Closure]: a function, or [null]): the appointment count, which prevents deletion (doctors only), and the deletion of references to the person.

docs.title: 11.11.6. src/Metier/MetierService.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Metier/MetierService.php: the business layer implementation.
//
// The management of doctors and clients follows three business rules:
//
//    1. A person (doctor or client) and their user account are TOUJOURS
//       as a pair: they are created, modified, and deleted together, within the same
//       TRANSACTION—either everything succeeds, or nothing is written;
//    2. The login is unique throughout the application, and two doctors (or two
//       customers) cannot have the same first and last names;
//    3. Deletion:
//       - A MÉDECIN with appointments cannot be deleted (their patients
//         would lose their appointments without being notified): you must first
//         cancel. Its time slots disappear along with it;
//       - a CLIENT, on the other hand, disappears along with TOUS its appointments (past and future) -
//         whether the deletion is initiated by the ADMIN or by the patient themselves.
//
// And two rules for scheduling appointments, regardless of the role of the person
// making the appointment (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient themselves):
//    4. No appointments in the past;
//    5. A patient can have only one upcoming appointment at a time.
//
// Doctors and patients follow exactly the same rules: the common code is
// is written UNE times (private methods xxxPersonne), and configured by a descriptor
// that specifies what type of person is involved.
//
// The TRANSACTIONS files are opened using the transaction method (end-of-file),
// which also translates errors reported by the database into MetierException.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Metier;

use App\Dao\ClientDao;
use App\Dao\CreneauDao;
use App\Dao\MedecinDao;
use App\Dao\RvDao;
use App\Dao\UserDao;
use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Domain\CreneauMedecinJour;
use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Creneau;
use App\Entity\Medecin;
use App\Entity\Personne;
use App\Entity\Role;
use App\Entity\Rv;
use App\Entity\User;
use Closure;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use Doctrine\DBAL\Exception\UniqueConstraintViolationException;
use Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface;
use Doctrine\ORM\OptimisticLockException;
use Symfony\Component\PasswordHasher\Hasher\PasswordHasherFactoryInterface;
use Symfony\Component\PasswordHasher\PasswordHasherInterface;

class MetierService implements Metier
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Database errors -> MetierException
    //
     // When a constraint UNIQUE rejects a write operation, Doctrine raises a
     // UniqueConstraintViolationException, whose message is that of MySQL. It
     // cites the NOM from the constraint:
        // Duplicate entry 'Marie-PELISSIER' for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom'
     // (MySQL prefixes the name with the table name, MariaDB does not). This is why
     // that the script SQL NOMME has all these constraints.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private const MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES = [
        'unq_users_login' => 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN',
        'unq_medecins_prenom_nom' => 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
        'unq_clients_prenom_nom' => 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
        'unq1_rv' => 'ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED',
    ];

    private const CONTRAINTE = "/for key '(?:[^'.]*\\.)?([^']+)'/";

    private Descripteur $medecin;

    private Descripteur $client;

     // password hashing (bcrypt, see config/packages/security.yaml)
    private PasswordHasherInterface $hacheur;

     // all dependencies are provided by the Symfony service container
     // (dependency injection, see Example 06)
    public function __construct(
        private EntityManagerInterface $em,
        private MedecinDao $medecins,
        private ClientDao $clients,
        private CreneauDao $creneaux,
        private RvDao $rvs,
        private UserDao $users,
        PasswordHasherFactoryInterface $hacheurs,
    ) {
        $this->hacheur = $hacheurs->getPasswordHasher(User::class);

        $this->medecin = new Descripteur(
            dao: $medecins,
            role: Role::DOCTOR,
            classe: Medecin::class,
            cleIntrouvable: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND',
            cleExisteDeja: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
             // $rvs->compterParMedecin(...): the method itself, as a closure
             // (so-called “first-class callable” syntax)
            compterRv: $rvs->compterParMedecin(...),
            cleAvecRv: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS',
             // A walk-in clinic may still have time slots:
             // they no longer make sense without it, so they are removed along with it (otherwise the
             // foreign key creneaux.id_medecin would prevent the deletion)
            avantSuppression: $creneaux->supprimerParMedecin(...));

        $this->client = new Descripteur(
            dao: $clients,
            role: Role::USER,
            classe: Client::class,
            cleIntrouvable: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND',
            cleExisteDeja: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
             // no compterRv: deleting a client is never denied;
             // their appointments (past and future) are deleted along with them (otherwise
             // the foreign key rv.id_client would prevent deletion)
            compterRv: null,
            cleAvecRv: null,
            avantSuppression: $rvs->supprimerParClient(...));
    }

    // =======================================================================
     // readings
    // =======================================================================

    public function getAllClients(): array
    {
        return $this->clients->lister();
    }

    public function getAllMedecins(): array
    {
        return $this->medecins->lister();
    }

    public function getAllCreneaux(int $idMedecin): array
    {
        return $this->creneaux->listerParMedecin($idMedecin);
    }

    public function getRvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour): array
    {
        return $this->rvs->rvMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
    }

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client
    {
        return $this->clients->lire($id);
    }

    public function getMedecinById(int $id): ?Medecin
    {
        return $this->medecins->lire($id);
    }

    public function getRvById(int $id): ?Rv
    {
        return $this->rvs->lire($id);
    }

    public function getCreneauById(int $id): ?Creneau
    {
        return $this->creneaux->lire($id);
    }

    public function getClientByUserId(int $idUser): ?Client
    {
        return $this->clients->lireParUser($idUser);
    }

    public function getRvAVenirClient(int $idClient): array
    {
        return $this->rvs->rvAVenirClient($idClient, Dates::aujourdhui());
    }

     // a doctor’s schedule on a given day: their time slots, and for each one the
     // appointment scheduled for that day (null if the slot is free)
    public function getAgendaMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour): ?AgendaMedecinJour
    {
        $medecin = $this->getMedecinById($idMedecin);
        if ($medecin === null) {
            return null;
        }
         // slot number -> appointment scheduled for that slot
        $reservations = [];
        foreach ($this->getRvMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour) as $rv) {
            $reservations[$rv->getCreneau()->getId()] = $rv;
        }
         // array_map: applies the function to each time slot and returns the results table
        $creneauxMedecinJour = array_map(
            fn (Creneau $creneau) => new CreneauMedecinJour($creneau, $reservations[$creneau->getId()] ?? null),
            $this->getAllCreneaux($idMedecin));
        return new AgendaMedecinJour($medecin, $jour, $creneauxMedecinJour);
    }

    // =======================================================================
     // appointment
    // =======================================================================

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // scheduling an appointment in a transaction:
        // 1. no past appointments;
        // 2. on VERROUILLE the patient’s line (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE): if the same
           // patient books two time slots at the same time (two tabs, double
           // click...), the second transaction waits for the first one to finish—and sees
           // the appointment it has just created;
        // 3. only one upcoming appointment per patient;
        // 4. Finally, the insertion. If the time slot has just been booked by a AUTRE patient,
           // it is the constraint SQL unq1_rv (day, id_creneau) that rejects
           // the insertion—translated to MetierException by transaction().
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function ajouterRv(DateTimeImmutable $jour, Creneau $creneau, Client $client): Rv
    {
        return $this->transaction(function () use ($jour, $creneau, $client) {
            $aujourdhui = Dates::aujourdhui();
            if ($jour < $aujourdhui) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PAST_DATE');
            }
            $idPatient = $this->clients->verrouiller($client->getId())
                ?? throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND');
            if ($this->rvs->compterAVenirClient($idPatient, $aujourdhui) > 0) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT');
            }
            $rv = new Rv($jour, $creneau, $client);
            $this->rvs->ajouter($rv);
            return $rv;
        });
    }

    public function supprimerRv(Rv $rv): void
    {
        $this->transaction(fn () => $this->rvs->supprimer($rv));
    }

    // =======================================================================
     // doctors and clients—public methods delegate to
     // shared private methods, with the correct descriptor
    // =======================================================================

    public function ajouterMedecin(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        return $this->ajouterPersonne($this->medecin, $donnees);
    }

    public function modifierMedecin(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        return $this->modifierPersonne($this->medecin, $id, $donnees);
    }

    public function supprimerMedecin(int $id): void
    {
        $this->supprimerPersonne($this->medecin, $id);
    }

    public function ajouterClient(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        return $this->ajouterPersonne($this->client, $donnees);
    }

    public function modifierClient(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        return $this->modifierPersonne($this->client, $id, $donnees);
    }

     // the client, their account ET all their appointments (ADMIN, or the patient themselves
     // from “Manage My Account”: same method, same rule)
    public function supprimerClient(int $id): void
    {
        $this->supprimerPersonne($this->client, $id);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // creation: the user account ET and the person (who references it), in UNE
     // transaction. Doctrine first inserts the account, then the person, whose key
     // foreign key [user] receives the ID that the database has just generated for the account.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function ajouterPersonne(Descripteur $d, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne
    {
        $nom = mb_strtoupper(trim($donnees->nom));
        $prenom = trim($donnees->prenom);
         // Rules for the dbrdvmedecins2 database: login = first name in lowercase, password
         // password = login—unless the ADMIN (or the patient) has entered others
        $login = mb_strtolower($donnees->login ?: $nom);
        $password = $donnees->password ?: $login;

        return $this->transaction(function () use ($d, $donnees, $nom, $prenom, $login, $password) {
            $this->verifierPersonneUnique($d, $prenom, $nom, null);
            $this->verifierLoginLibre($login);
             // hash: the bcrypt hash of the password
            $user = new User($login, $this->hacheur->hash($password), "$prenom $nom", $d->role);
            $this->users->ajouter($user);
             // new $d->class(...): an instance of the class whose name is in the
             // property [classe] of the descriptor (Doctor or Client)
            $personne = new ($d->classe)($donnees->titre, $nom, $prenom, $user);
            $d->dao->ajouter($personne);
            return $personne;
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // modification: the person ET their account (the displayed name "first name NOM" must
     // match; the username and password change only if they were entered).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function modifierPersonne(Descripteur $d, int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne
    {
        return $this->transaction(function () use ($d, $id, $donnees) {
            $personne = $d->dao->lire($id) ?? throw new MetierException($d->cleIntrouvable);

             // optimistic lock: if the version in the database is no longer the same as the
             // form, someone has modified this record in the meantime—the operation is rejected
             // rather than silently overwriting their changes
            if ($donnees->version !== null && $donnees->version !== $personne->getVersion()) {
                throw new MetierException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE');
            }

            $nom = mb_strtoupper(trim($donnees->nom));
            $prenom = trim($donnees->prenom);
            $this->verifierPersonneUnique($d, $prenom, $nom, $id);
            $personne->modifier($donnees->titre, $nom, $prenom);

             // their account: the displayed name, and, if entered, the username and
             // password
            $compte = $personne->getCompte();
            $compte->setNom("$prenom $nom");
            $login = $donnees->login ? mb_strtolower($donnees->login) : null;
            if ($login !== null && $login !== $compte->getLogin()) {
                $this->verifierLoginLibre($login);
                $compte->setLogin($login);
            }
            if ($donnees->password) {
                $compte->setPassword($this->hacheur->hash($donnees->password));
            }
             // nothing else to do: at the end of the transaction, Doctrine sends the
             // UPDATE of the modified rows, along with their optimistic locks
                // UPDATE ... SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ?
             // If the record has been modified APRÈS as described above, no line
             // is modified, and Doctrine raises a OptimisticLockException
            return $personne;
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // deletion, in UNE the transaction, in the order dictated by the foreign keys
     // foreign keys:
        // 1. possible rejection if there are still available appointments (with a doctor);
        // 2. which identifies the person (a doctor’s time slots, a
           // client), immediately;
        // 3. the person (who references their account), then their account: Doctrine
           // deletes them in this order at the end of the transaction.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function supprimerPersonne(Descripteur $d, int $id): void
    {
        $this->transaction(function () use ($d, $id) {
            $personne = $d->dao->lire($id) ?? throw new MetierException($d->cleIntrouvable);
            if ($d->compterRv !== null && ($d->compterRv)($id) > 0) {
                throw new MetierException($d->cleAvecRv);
            }
            if ($d->avantSuppression !== null) {
                ($d->avantSuppression)($id);
            }
            $d->dao->supprimer($personne);
            $this->users->supprimer($personne->getCompte());
        });
    }

     // rejects first and last names already used by a AUTRE person of the same type
     // ($idCourant: the person being edited, who obviously has the right
     // to keep their own first and last names; null for a new record)
    private function verifierPersonneUnique(Descripteur $d, string $prenom, string $nom, ?int $idCourant): void
    {
        $homonyme = $d->dao->homonyme($prenom, $nom);
        if ($homonyme !== null && $homonyme->getId() !== $idCourant) {
            throw new MetierException($d->cleExisteDeja);
        }
    }

    private function verifierLoginLibre(string $login): void
    {
        if ($this->users->lireParLogin($login) !== null) {
            throw new MetierException('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN');
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // executes [$travail] within a transaction (wrapInTransaction, see Example 28):
     // if the function completes normally, Doctrine sends the
     // pending updates (flush), then commits the transaction (COMMIT); if an
     // exception occurs (including MetierException), ROLLBACK: nothing is written.
    //
     // The "free login" and "unique first name + last name" checks are performed AVANT
     // the entry, to provide a clear message. But two ADMIN entries could
     // register the same login (or the same doctor) at the same time: in this case
     // — though rare — a uniqueness constraint SQL prevents the second write.
     // Similarly, two simultaneous modifications to the same record are resolved by the
     // optimistic lock. We therefore intercept these errors AUTOUR in the transaction,
     // and convert them to MetierException. Any other error is a true
     // anomaly: we let it propagate.
     // After an exception, Doctrine FERME calls the entity manager: the
     // in progress must no longer write anything (the controllers redirect, or
     // re-display a form).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function transaction(Closure $travail): mixed
    {
        try {
            return $this->em->wrapInTransaction($travail);
        } catch (UniqueConstraintViolationException $e) {
            if (preg_match(self::CONTRAINTE, $e->getMessage(), $m)
                && isset(self::MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES[$m[1]])) {
                throw new MetierException(self::MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES[$m[1]], previous: $e);
            }
            throw $e;
        } catch (OptimisticLockException $e) {
            throw new MetierException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE', previous: $e);
        }
    }
}

The most important file in the application. We’ll go through it by topic.

docs.title: 11.11.6.1. Dependencies and descriptors
docs.text: Lines 86–124: The constructor receives from the container the entity manager (for transactions), the five DAO instances, and the hash service factory ([PasswordHasherFactoryInterface]), which is asked to provide the one for accounts: [getPasswordHasher(User::class)] provides the service that applies the algorithm chosen for class [User] in [security.yaml] ([bcrypt], 10 iterations). Next come the two descriptors. Named arguments ([dao: $medecins], example 01) make the call readable. [$rvs->compterParMedecin(...)] (with three dots in parentheses) has no significance: it is the syntax of [PHP] 8.1 that creates, from a method, a [Closure]—a function that will be called later ([($d->compterRv)($id)], line 359). A doctor is removed along with their time slots ([supprimerParMedecin]), but not if they have appointments; a client is removed along with all their appointments ([supprimerParClient]).

docs.title: 11.11.6.2. Read operations and the calendar
docs.text: The read operations (lines 130–178) delegate to the DAO layer. A doctor’s schedule (lines 182–198) is calculated: the doctor, their time slots, and the appointments for that day. Appointments are stored in an array indexed by slot number: [$reservations[$creneau->getId()] ?? null] returns the appointment for a slot, or [null] if the slot is free. [array_map] converts each time slot to [CreneauMedecinJour].

docs.title: 11.11.6.3. Scheduling an Appointment
docs.text:
Lines 216–232: four steps, in a single transaction.

  • No past appointments: The [DateTimeImmutable] entries match the usual operators ([<], [>=]...);
  • the patient’s record is locked ([verrouiller], [SELECT ... FOR UPDATE]). Why? The rule “only one upcoming appointment per patient” is verified by a count (third step), then the insertion takes place (fourth step). If the same patient books two time slots at the same time (two tabs, a double-click), both transactions could count zero appointments and then each insert its own: the rule would be violated. With the lock, the second transaction waits for the first one to finish, then counts... one appointment. [?? throw new MetierException(...)]: if the client no longer exists, [verrouiller] returns [null], and the operator [??] evaluates its second operand, which raises the exception (since [PHP] 8, [throw] is an expression);
  • counting upcoming appointments;
  • insertion, at the end of the transaction. If the time slot has just been taken by another patient, the database constraint [unq1_rv] rejects the insertion: the method [transaction] translates this error into [MetierException].

docs.title: 11.11.6.4. Managing Doctors and Clients
docs.text:
The public methods (lines 244–274) call the shared private methods, using the correct descriptor.

  • Lines 281–302: creation. The last name is capitalized ([mb_strtoupper]: the version of [strtoupper] that supports accented letters), and the first name and last name are stripped of unnecessary spaces ([trim]). By default, the login is the last name in lowercase, and the password is the login (as per the rules for demo accounts): [$a ?: $b] is equivalent to [$a] if it is “true” (neither [null] nor an empty string), and [$b] otherwise. In the transaction: the validations (first and last names can be any value, login can be any value), then the account, whose password is hashed ([hash]), then the person, who references the account. [new ($d->classe)(...)] creates an object of the class whose name is in the [classe] property of the descriptor (parentheses are required around an expression). [Doctrine] will insert the account before the person: it knows the relationships between the entities and deduces the order of the [INSERT] objects. [use (...)]: An ordinary anonymous function ([function () use ($d, ...)]) cannot see the variables of the method that contains it; [use] passes them to it (an arrow function, [fn () =>], sees them on its own, but can only contain an expression);
  • Lines 308–344: the update, with two optimistic locks. The first is a comparison (lines 316–318): the form’s version (hidden field, Example 28) must match that of the record in the database; otherwise, someone modified the record between the time the form was displayed and the time it was submitted. The second is that of [Doctrine]: the [UPDATE] records sent at the end of the transaction carry the condition [WHERE version = ?], which detects a change that occurred between reading and writing ([OptimisticLockException]). The account follows: its displayed name (“first name NOM”) is always updated; its login and password are updated only if they were entered; its own optimistic lock also protects the row in the [users] table. There is nothing to “save”: the entity being read is tracked by the entity manager, which will write its changes. At the end of the transaction, [Doctrine] stores the new versions of the entities: the caller receives the updated person;
  • lines 355–368: deletion, in the order dictated by the foreign keys: first, the records referencing the person (time slots or appointments), immediately followed by [DELETE] from DAO; then the person, then their account, which [Doctrine] deletes in that order at the end of the transaction. The reverse order would be rejected by the database: a row that is still referenced by a foreign key cannot be deleted;
  • lines 373–387: the person being modified is allowed to retain their own first and last names; [$idCourant] is equivalent to [null] for a creation.

docs.title: 11.11.6.5. Database Transactions and Errors
docs.text:
Lines 406–419: All postings use this method. [wrapInTransaction] executes the function within a transaction (Example 28): [flush], then [COMMIT] if it completes normally, and [ROLLBACK] if an exception occurs—including a [MetierException]: a rule violation in the middle of an operation leaves no trace. The “login available” and “first and last names available” checks are performed before writing, to provide a clear message. However, two administrators could attempt to register the same login at the same time: each finds it available, and the second [INSERT] is rejected by the constraint [unq_users_login]. [Doctrine] then raises a [UniqueConstraintViolationException] (example 28), whose message is that of [MySQL]; it contains the name of the violated constraint:

SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry 'dupont' for key 'users.unq_users_login'

The regular expression on line 75 extracts this name ([MySQL] 8 prefixes it with the table name, [users.unq_users_login], but not [MariaDB]: the part [(?:[^'.]*\.)?] accepts both forms), and the table in lines 68–73 provides the message key. Another constraint violation is a true anomaly: it is retried ([throw $e]) and will result in a 500 error page. Finally, the conflict detected by the optimistic lock on [Doctrine] ([OptimisticLockException]) becomes the same [MetierException] as the one detected by the version comparison.

Recall a consequence of [wrapInTransaction] (Example 28): after an exception, the entity manager is closed and can no longer write during the current request. The controllers take this into account: after a [MetierException], they redirect or re-display a form without writing anything else.

docs.title: 11.12. Authentication
docs.text: The [src/Securite] folder includes examples 25 through 27, featuring database users and a few additional security measures. Let’s review the principle (Example 25): the [principal] firewall for [config/packages/security.yaml] is stateless ([stateless]); for each request, an authenticator of our own design reads the token JWT from the cookie [rdvmedecins_jwt] and identifies the user; the rules [access_control] then determine access to the pages.

docs.title: 11.12.1. src/Security/UtilisateurConnecte.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Securite/UtilisateurConnecte.php: the logged-in user, as described
// by its token JWT (see Example 25). UserInterface: the interface that Symfony expects from
// authenticated users ($this->getUser() in a controller, #[CurrentUser],
// app.user and is_granted() in a view...).
//
// The claims of our tokens (see AuthService::cookieJeton):
//    su  b : the user account ID (convention JWT: "subject"), as plain text
//    login: the login
//    na  me: the display name ("Marie PELISSIER"), for the navigation bar
//    rol e: ADMIN, DOCTOR, or USER
//    iat, exp: token creation and expiration dates
//
// This object does not come from the database: it is reconstructed with each request,
// from the token, whose signature guarantees its content.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Securite;

use App\Entity\Role;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Core\User\UserInterface;

readonly class UtilisateurConnecte implements UserInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $userId,
        public string $login,
        public string $nom,
        public Role $role,
    ) {
    }

     // the user described by the claims of a token that has already been verified; null if a claim
     // is missing or does not have the expected format. Role::tryFrom: null for an unknown role
    public static function de(array $claims): ?self
    {
        $role = Role::tryFrom((string) ($claims['role'] ?? ''));
        if (! isset($claims['sub'], $claims['login'], $claims['nom']) || $role === null
            || ! ctype_digit((string) $claims['sub'])) {
            return null;
        }
        return new self((int) $claims['sub'], (string) $claims['login'], (string) $claims['nom'], $role);
    }

    public function estAdmin(): bool
    {
        return $this->role === Role::ADMIN;
    }

    public function estPatient(): bool
    {
        return $this->role === Role::USER;
    }

     // ---- the UserInterface interface: the user’s identifier (their login),
     // and their roles as defined by Symfony (ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_DOCTOR, or ROLE_USER; see
     // the Role enumeration), which are verified by the rules access_control in
     // config/packages/security.yaml
    public function getUserIdentifier(): string
    {
        return $this->login;
    }

    public function getRoles(): array
    {
        return [$this->role->roleSymfony()];
    }
}

The logged-in user, as described by their token: their account ID, username, name, and role. Like [Utilisateur] in Example 25, it implements the [UserInterface] interface, which [Symfony] expects from authenticated users. This object does not come from the database: it is reconstructed with each request, based on the token, whose signature guarantees its content. The application therefore does not read the account from the database with each request. The class is [readonly] (Example 08): its public properties cannot be modified after construction.

  • Lines 36–44: the user is described by the claims (claims) of a token that has already been verified, or [null] if one of the claims is missing or does not have the expected format. A properly signed token should never be malformed; however, the secret key could be shared with another application, which might generate different tokens: it costs nothing to be cautious. [Role::tryFrom] returns the role, or [null] for an unknown value; [ctype_digit] verifies that a string consists only of digits;
  • lines 46–54: two questions that views and controllers often ask;
  • Lines 60–68: the [UserInterface] interface. The user’s identifier is their login; their roles, as defined by [Symfony], are limited to a single role, [ROLE_ADMIN], [ROLE_DOCTOR] or [ROLE_USER], calculated by the enumeration [Role]. These are the ones checked by the rules [access_control], the attribute [#[IsGranted]], and the function [is_granted] of the views. (The [eraseCredentials] method, which cleared the plaintext password after login, has been removed from the interface with [Symfony] 8.)

docs.title: 11.12.2. src/Security/AuthService.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Security/AuthService.php: authentication logic:
//    - validate       () : verifies a username/password pair;
//    - cookieJeton(   ) : generates the JWT token for a validated user, and the
//                         cookie that carries it;
//    - user() :    the user described by a token.
//
// Where does the JWT token travel? In a COOKIE (see Example 25): a browser
// that displays ordinary HTML pages presents it on its own, with every
// request. The settings in this cookie are important for security:
//    - HttpOnly: the page’s JavaScript cannot read the cookie (an injected script
//      injected script could not steal the token);
//    - SameSite=Lax: the browser does not send the cookie with a PAS value originating from a
//      another site (first line of defense against the so-called CSRF attack; the second is
//      the anti-CSRF token for forms);
//    - Secure: in production (HTTPS), the cookie is never transmitted in plain text;
//    - Lifetime: the cookie is deleted when the token expires.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Securite;

use App\Dao\UserDao;
use App\Entity\User;
use Firebase\JWT\JWT;
use Firebase\JWT\Key;
use RuntimeException;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Cookie;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\PasswordHasher\Hasher\PasswordHasherFactoryInterface;
use Throwable;

class AuthService
{
     // the name of the cookie that carries the token
    public const COOKIE = 'rdvmedecins_jwt';

     // the settings in the .env file: #[Autowire(env: ...)] (see Example 25)
    public function __construct(
        private UserDao $users,
        private PasswordHasherFactoryInterface $hacheurs,
         #[Autowire(env: 'JWT_SECRET')] private string $secret,
         #[Autowire(env: 'int:JWT_DUREE_MINUTES')] private int $duree,
         #[Autowire(env: 'bool:COOKIE_SECURE')] private bool $cookieSecure,
    ) {
         // HMAC-SHA256 requires a key of at least 256 bits: this is clearly stated,
         // rather than letting the library fail later
        if (strlen($this->secret) < 32) {
            throw new RuntimeException('JWT_SECRET doit comporter au moins 32 caractères (cf. .env).');
        }
    }

     // null if the login does not exist or if the password is incorrect. verify hashes the
     // the entered password with the “salt” contained in the stored hash, then
     // compares the two results
    public function valider(string $login, string $password): ?User
    {
        $user = $this->users->lireParLogin($login);
        if ($user === null
            || ! $this->hacheurs->getPasswordHasher(User::class)->verify($user->getPassword(), $password)) {
            return null;
        }
        return $user;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the token JWT from [$user], in the cookie that carries it. The token is SIGNÉ
     // (HMAC-SHA256) using the secret key: the browser can read it (it is not
     // encrypted), but it cannot modify it—any modification would render the signature
     // invalid.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function cookieJeton(User $user): Cookie
    {
        $maintenant = time();
        $claims = [
            'sub' => (string) $user->getId(),
            'login' => $user->getLogin(),
            'nom' => $user->getNom(),
            'role' => $user->getRole()->value,
            'iat' => $maintenant,
            'exp' => $maintenant + $this->duree * 60,
        ];
        $jeton = JWT::encode($claims, $this->secret, 'HS256');
        return Cookie::create(self::COOKIE, $jeton)
            ->withExpires($maintenant + $this->duree * 60)
            ->withSecure($this->cookieSecure)
            ->withHttpOnly(true)
            ->withSameSite(Cookie::SAMESITE_LAX);
    }

     // deletes the token cookie: the response contains an empty cookie with the same name that has already expired
    public static function effacerCookie(Response $reponse): Response
    {
        $reponse->headers->clearCookie(self::COOKIE);
        return $reponse;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the user identified by a token; null if the token has expired, is forged, or
     // malformed. JWT::decode verifies the signature; ET verifies the expiration date (claim exp).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function utilisateur(string $jeton): ?UtilisateurConnecte
    {
        try {
             // decode returns an object; (array) converts it to an associative array
            $claims = (array) JWT::decode($jeton, new Key($this->secret, 'HS256'));
        } catch (Throwable) {
            return null;
        }
        return UtilisateurConnecte::de($claims);
    }
}
  • line 37: the name of the token cookie, a class constant, read by [AuthService::COOKIE];
  • lines 40–52: the service receives the DAO layer for accounts; the hash service factory (the one corresponding to the [User] class, bcrypt, is declared in [security.yaml]), and three settings from the [.env] file, via the [#[Autowire(env: ...)]] attribute (Example 25). The prefixes [int:] and [bool:] convert the text of the environment variable. If a key is too short, this is reported as soon as the service is started, with a clear message (see “Common Problems”);
  • Lines 57–65: Verification of a username and password (Example 25), with the account retrieved from the database by the DAO layer. Note that this service uses the DAO layer directly, without going through the business layer: password verification is not a business rule;
  • Lines 73–90: the user’s token and the cookie that carries it. The statements are the same as in Example 25, with the account ID ([sub], a string, as required by the standard) and the username. [Cookie::create] creates a cookie, which the [with...] methods supplement (each returns a new cookie: the object is immutable): its expiration date (that of the token), [Secure] (in production, on HTTPS), [HttpOnly], and [SameSite=Lax] (see the comment on lines 9–18);
  • lines 93–97: Deleting the cookie. [clearCookie(nom)] adds a cookie with the same name to the response—empty and already expired—so the browser deletes it. The method is static: it requires no configuration, and the classes that call it do not need to receive the service;
  • lines 103–112: token verification (example 25).

docs.title: 11.12.3. src/Securite/JetonAuthenticator.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Securite/JetonAuthenticator.php: the AUTHENTIFICATEUR of the firewall (see
// config/packages/security.yaml and Example 25): for each request, it determines which
// the user is, based on the JWT token in the [rdvmedecins_jwt] cookie.
//
// It does not reject anything on its own: a missing or invalid token allows the visitor
// ANONYME. It is the rules access_control that subsequently deny access to the protected pages
// protected pages; an anonymous visitor who is denied access is then redirected to the POINT D'ENTRÉE (the
// "start" method), which redirects them to the login page.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Securite;

use App\Web\Flash;
use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ResponseEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Generator\UrlGeneratorInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Core\Authentication\Token\TokenInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Core\Exception\AuthenticationException;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Core\Exception\CustomUserMessageAuthenticationException;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Http\Authenticator\AbstractAuthenticator;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Http\Authenticator\Passport\Badge\UserBadge;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Http\Authenticator\Passport\Passport;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Http\Authenticator\Passport\SelfValidatingPassport;
use Symfony\Component\Security\Http\EntryPoint\AuthenticationEntryPointInterface;

class JetonAuthenticator extends AbstractAuthenticator implements AuthenticationEntryPointInterface
{
     // the request attribute indicating an invalid token, to be cleared
    private const JETON_INVALIDE = '_jeton_invalide';

    public function __construct(
        private AuthService $auth,
        private Flash $flash,
        private UrlGeneratorInterface $urls,
    ) {
    }

     // the authenticator only takes effect if the request includes the token cookie
    public function supports(Request $request): ?bool
    {
        return $request->cookies->getString(AuthService::COOKIE) !== '';
    }

     // the token, verified by AuthService, describes the user: the passport
     // validates itself, and the badge directly identifies this user (without the
     // searching the database; see Example 25)
    public function authenticate(Request $request): Passport
    {
        $utilisateur = $this->auth->utilisateur($request->cookies->getString(AuthService::COOKIE))
            ?? throw new CustomUserMessageAuthenticationException('jeton invalide');
        return new SelfValidatingPassport(new UserBadge($utilisateur->login, fn () => $utilisateur));
    }

    public function onAuthenticationSuccess(Request $request, TokenInterface $token, string $firewallName): ?Response
    {
        return null;
    }

     // an invalid token (expired, forged): the visitor remains anonymous (null), and the
     // cookie will be removed from the response, regardless of its content (see effacerJetonInvalide)
    public function onAuthenticationFailure(Request $request, AuthenticationException $exception): ?Response
    {
        $request->attributes->set(self::JETON_INVALIDE, true);
        return null;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POINT from ENTRÉE: an anonymous visitor requests a protected page. Redirect to
     // to the login page. If they had a token cookie, it means their token is
     // no longer valid (expired, tampered with): their session has expired, and they are notified
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function start(Request $request, ?AuthenticationException $authException = null): Response
    {
        if ($request->cookies->has(AuthService::COOKIE)) {
            $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
        }
        return new RedirectResponse($this->urls->generate('login'));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // a listener for kernel.response (see Example 24), written in the same class:
     // it deletes the cookie for an invalid token from all responses
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::RESPONSE)]
    public function effacerJetonInvalide(ResponseEvent $evenement): void
    {
        if ($evenement->getRequest()->attributes->get(self::JETON_INVALIDE)) {
            AuthService::effacerCookie($evenement->getResponse());
        }
    }
}

The authenticator from Example 25, declared in [security.yaml] ([custom_authenticators]). It also serves as the firewall’s entry point: it implements the [AuthenticationEntryPointInterface] interface, and [Symfony] selects it automatically, since it is the firewall’s only authenticator.

  • lines 45–48: [supports] determines whether the authenticator should intervene: only if the request contains the token cookie. Without a cookie, the visitor is anonymous, and no further action is taken;
  • lines 53–58: [authenticate] verifies the token. An invalid token triggers a [AuthenticationException] (its subclass, [CustomUserMessageAuthenticationException], carries a free message). Otherwise, a self-validating passport ([SelfValidatingPassport]: there is no password to verify; the token’s signature serves as the password), whose user is constructed from the token without looking it up in the database;
  • lines 60–63: after a successful authentication, [null]: the request continues on to the requested action;
  • lines 67–71: after a failure (expired or forged token), [null] as well: the visitor remains anonymous. The rules [access_control] will redirect the visitor to the login page if they request a protected page, but they can view public pages (including the login page itself!). The only indication is in a request attribute stating that the cookie should be deleted;
  • lines 78–84: the entry point, called by the firewall when an anonymous visitor requests a protected page: a redirect to the login page. If the request contained a token cookie, it means that token is no longer valid: the message “Your session has expired; please log in again” is displayed (a pop-up message, discussed later);
  • Lines 90–96: A listener for event [kernel.response] (Example 24), defined within the same class: the [#[AsEventListener]] attribute is applied to a method, and the authenticator—a service like any other—also becomes a listener. It deletes the cookie for an invalid token, regardless of the response: the login page, a public page, or a redirect from the entry point. An invalid cookie serves no purpose and would corrupt the message of the next request.

docs.title: 11.12.4. src/Security/SessionInvalide.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Securite/SessionInvalide.php: the token is valid, but the account it
// no longer exists: it has been deleted since the login (either by the patient
// themselves in another tab, or by the ADMIN). This case is treated as a
// expired session: the listener PageErreur clears the cookie and redirects to the
// login page.

namespace App\Securite;

use RuntimeException;

class SessionInvalide extends RuntimeException
{
}

A scenario not covered in Example 25: the token is valid, but the account it refers to no longer exists. A patient has deleted their account in one tab, but the token is still present in another tab; or the administrator has deleted the account of a logged-in patient. The token’s signature provides no indication of the account’s existence; it is only when the application searches for the patient associated with the account ([Outils::patientConnecte], discussed later) that it discovers the account no longer exists. It then throws this exception, which the listener [PageErreur] (discussed later) treats as an expired session. The class is empty: only its type matters, which the listener recognizes ([instanceof]).

docs.title: 11.12.5. src/Securite/CaptchaService.php, Captcha.php, and DessinCaptcha.php
docs.text:
[DessinCaptcha.php] and [Captcha.php] are from Example 27. The service is almost the same:

<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Securite/CaptchaService.php: a CAPTCHA ("test to distinguish a human from a
// robot") generated by the server itself, without an external service (see example 27).
//
// How it works:
//    1. `generer()` generates a random text, turns it into an image, and stores the correct
//       response DANS LE CACHE from the server under a random identifier;
//    2. The page displays the image and places the identifier in a hidden field on the
//       form (the response itself never leaves the server);
//    3. verify(id, input) compares the input to the expected response, then OUBLIE
//       this CAPTCHA: each image is used only once; a bot cannot reuse
//       a response that has already been found.
//
// Why the cache? An application PHP does not keep RIEN in memory from one request to
// : each request starts from scratch. Anything that needs to persist beyond a single request
// is therefore stored in the cache (in this case, files in var/cache), shared by all
// requests, and even across multiple servers using a cache like Redis.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Securite;

use Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Lock\LockFactory;

class CaptchaService
{
     // image validity period, in seconds: 10 minutes to fill out the form
    private const DUREE_VIE = 600;

    public function __construct(private CacheItemPoolInterface $cache, private LockFactory $verrous)
    {
    }

    public function generer(): Captcha
    {
        $texte = DessinCaptcha::texteAleatoire(5);    // 5 characters
        $id = bin2hex(random_bytes(12));              // an unguessable identifier
         // the cache will automatically forget the answer after 10 minutes
        $element = $this->cache->getItem("captcha.$id");
        $this->cache->save($element->set($texte)->expiresAfter(self::DUREE_VIE));
        return new Captcha($id, DessinCaptcha::svg($texte));
    }

     // true if [$saisie] is the correct answer to the captcha [$id] (regardless of
     // case). The CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases.
    public function verifier(?string $id, ?string $saisie): bool
    {
         // The identifier comes from the browser: hexadecimal digits, or nothing
        if ($id === null || ! ctype_xdigit($id) || $saisie === null) {
            return false;
        }
         // if two requests have the same CAPTCHA at the same time, only one
         // receives the lock (acquire(false): without waiting)—the other fails
        $verrou = $this->verrous->createLock("captcha.$id");
        if (! $verrou->acquire(false)) {
            return false;
        }
        try {
            $element = $this->cache->getItem("captcha.$id");
            $this->cache->deleteItem("captcha.$id");
        } finally {
            $verrou->release();
        }
        return $element->isHit() && strcasecmp($element->get(), trim($saisie)) === 0;
    }
}
  • lines 35–43: a 5-character string generated at random, a random identifier ([random_bytes], a cryptographic generator, whose bytes are written in hexadecimal as [bin2hex]), and the correct answer stored in the cache (example 20) for 10 minutes ([expiresAfter], in seconds);
  • lines 47–66: a difference from Example 27. The answer is read, then removed from the cache. Between the reading and the removal, a second request presenting the same CAPTCHA could also read it: two attempts for a single solved image. A lock (Example 20), specific to this CAPTCHA, therefore protects both the reading and the removal. [acquire(false)] acquires it immediately: it returns [false] if another request already holds it, and that request, which loses the race, fails. The block [finally] releases the lock in all cases. The comparison ignores uppercase letters ([strcasecmp] returns 0 for two strings that are case-insensitive matches) and spaces around the input ([trim]).

docs.title: 11.12.6. src/Security/LimiteurTentatives.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Securite/LimiteurTentatives.php: second line of defense against bots (the first
// is the CAPTCHA): we track attempts, and once a threshold is exceeded, we block
// for a while (see example 27).
//
//    - login: after LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS failed attempts (incorrect captcha or incorrect
//      (password) for the same login from the same address IP; this pair is
//      blocked until the end of a LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES-minute window, counted
//      from the first failed attempt. The same IP address is also blocked if it accumulates
//      LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS_IP failed attempts across all logins (a bot attempting
//      thousands of different logins);
//    - account creation: no more than INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE accounts created per
//      per hour from the same IP address IP.
//
// Caution in the classroom: all computers often connect to the Internet via the
// MÊME address IP. This is why the connection block first targets the
// pair (IP, login)—a student who enters the wrong password does not block their
// neighbors—and why the thresholds are adjustable (.env file).
//
// The counters are those of the three limiters in the RateLimiter component, declared
// in config/packages/framework.yaml, and stored in the cache.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Securite;

use Symfony\Component\RateLimiter\LimiterInterface;
use Symfony\Component\RateLimiter\RateLimiterFactoryInterface;

class LimiteurTentatives
{
     // the factories for the limiters [login], [login_ip], and [inscription]: the name
     // of the parameter refers to the limiter (see Example 27)
    public function __construct(
        private RateLimiterFactoryInterface $loginLimiter,
        private RateLimiterFactoryInterface $loginIpLimiter,
        private RateLimiterFactoryInterface $inscriptionLimiter,
    ) {
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- connection

     // number of remaining minutes of blocking (0 = the attempt is allowed)
    public function minutesBlocageLogin(string $ip, string $login): int
    {
        return max(self::minutesRestantes($this->limiteurLogin($ip, $login)),
            self::minutesRestantes($this->loginIpLimiter->create($ip)));
    }

     // consume(): one more failure; the first opens a window of
     // LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES minutes, at the end of which the counter resets to zero
    public function echecLogin(string $ip, string $login): void
    {
        $this->limiteurLogin($ip, $login)->consume();
        $this->loginIpLimiter->create($ip)->consume();
    }

     // A successful connection resets the login counter to zero CE
    public function reussiteLogin(string $ip, string $login): void
    {
        $this->limiteurLogin($ip, $login)->reset();
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

    public function minutesBlocageInscription(string $ip): int
    {
        return self::minutesRestantes($this->inscriptionLimiter->create($ip));
    }

    public function inscriptionReussie(string $ip): void
    {
        $this->inscriptionLimiter->create($ip)->consume();
    }

     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- common mechanics

     // the torque limiter (IP, login): create(key) returns a limiter that has its
     // own counter, under this key
    private function limiteurLogin(string $ip, string $login): LimiterInterface
    {
        return $this->loginLimiter->create("$ip|".mb_strtolower(trim($login)));
    }

     // `consume(0)` queries the limiter without consuming anything: no more "tokens"?
     // getRetryAfter: the end date of the current window; the seconds that
     // remain until then are rounded up to the nearest minute SUPÉRIEURE: 30 s → “1 minute”
    private static function minutesRestantes(LimiterInterface $limiteur): int
    {
        $etat = $limiteur->consume(0);
        if ($etat->getRemainingTokens() > 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        return max(1, (int) ceil(($etat->getRetryAfter()->getTimestamp() - time()) / 60));
    }
}

The second line of defense against bots, after the CAPTCHA: we count the attempts, and once a threshold is exceeded, we block access. Example 27 presented the [RateLimiter] component of [Symfony]. The three limiters are declared in [config/packages/framework.yaml] (policy [fixed_window]: a fixed-duration window, opened by the first token consumed); the service receives their factories, identified by the parameter names (lines 34–38): [$loginLimiter] for the limiter [login], [$loginIpLimiter] for [login_ip], [$inscriptionLimiter] for [inscription]. A factory uses its method [create(clé)] to create a limiter that has its own counter under this key. Two rules:

  • the connection (lines 44–62): each failure (incorrect CAPTCHA or password) is counted twice: for the pair (address IP, login), and for the address IP alone. The pair is blocked after 5 failed attempts (setting [LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS]), and the address IP after 25 (setting [LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS_IP]), across all logins: It’s the bot trying thousands of different logins. Why not block the address IP first? In a classroom (or at a company), all machines often access the Internet through the same address, IP: a student who enters the wrong password shouldn’t block their neighbors. [consume()] consumes a token (counts as a failed attempt); the first attempt opens a 15-minute window (setting [LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES]), at the end of which the counter resets to zero. A successful connection resets the counter for that user ([reset]);
  • account creation (lines 66–74): no more than 10 accounts per hour per address IP (setting [INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE]);
  • lines 80–83: the key for a torque limiter. The login is in lowercase: [Admin] and [admin] are considered the same (as with the database; see its collation);
  • Lines 88–95: [consume(0)] queries the limiter without consuming any tokens (example 27): there are tokens remaining, so the attempt is allowed; otherwise, [getRetryAfter] returns the end date of the current window, and the number of seconds remaining until then is rounded up to the next minute ([ceil]): there are 30 seconds left, so “1 minute” is displayed. The message displayed depends on this: “Too many failed attempts. Please try again in 15 minutes.”

The limiters’ counters are stored in the cache: they are shared by all requests and survive a server restart. The command [php bin/console cache:pool:clear cache.rate_limiter] resets them all to zero (useful during development, when you’ve gotten yourself stuck); [php bin/console cache:clear], which clears the entire [var/cache] directory, does the same.

docs.title: 11.12.7. src/Securite/PasseInscription.php and PasseInscriptionExige.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Securite/PasseInscription.php: the "pass" for account creation.
//
// To open the “Create a Customer Account” page, you must first have copied the
// captcha from the authentication page (see InscriptionController, POST
// /registration/access). The server then issues a token:
//    - a random identifier, stored in a cookie named HttpOnly;
//    - valid for 15 minutes (enough time to fill out the form, even if you have to
//      several times after data entry errors);
//    - Expires as soon as an account is created: UN captcha solved = UN account at most.
//      A bot cannot create accounts in bulk.
//
// Without a valid passcode, GET and POST /registration redirect to the
// authentication page (see the attribute #[PasseInscriptionExige] and the listener
// VerifierPasseInscription): typing the URL /registration directly does not allow
// to bypass the CAPTCHA.
//
// Like CAPTCHAs, passcodes are stored in the cache.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Securite;

use Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Cookie;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class PasseInscription
{
    public const COOKIE = 'rdvmedecins_inscription';

     // The cookie is sent by the browser only to addresses ending in /registration...
    private const CHEMIN = '/inscription';

     // lifetime of a token, in minutes
    private const DUREE_VIE = 15;

    public function __construct(
        private CacheItemPoolInterface $cache,
         #[Autowire(env: 'bool:COOKIE_SECURE')] private bool $cookieSecure,
    ) {
    }

     // issues a new pass; returns the cookie carrying it
    public function emettre(): Cookie
    {
        $id = bin2hex(random_bytes(12));
        $element = $this->cache->getItem("passe.$id");
        $this->cache->save($element->set(true)->expiresAfter(self::DUREE_VIE * 60));
        return Cookie::create(self::COOKIE, $id)
            ->withExpires(time() + self::DUREE_VIE * 60)
            ->withPath(self::CHEMIN)
            ->withSecure($this->cookieSecure)
            ->withHttpOnly(true)
            ->withSameSite(Cookie::SAMESITE_LAX);
    }

     // true if [$id] is an existing, unexpired pass; hasItem: does the
     // Does the cache contain this item?
    public function estValide(?string $id): bool
    {
        return $id !== null && ctype_xdigit($id) && $this->cache->hasItem("passe.$id");
    }

     // The pass has been used: we forget about it...
    public function consommer(?string $id): void
    {
        if ($id !== null && ctype_xdigit($id)) {
            $this->cache->deleteItem("passe.$id");
        }
    }

     // ... and its cookie is overwritten by a cookie with the same name and path that has already expired
    public static function effacerCookie(Response $reponse): Response
    {
        $reponse->headers->clearCookie(self::COOKIE, self::CHEMIN);
        return $reponse;
    }
}

Creating a customer account is protected by the CAPTCHA on the login page. But the account creation form is on a different page ([/inscription]): how can the system know, when the form is requested, that the CAPTCHA was solved just before? Through a token: when the CAPTCHA is solved, the server generates a random identifier, stores it in the cache for 15 minutes, and sends it to the browser in a cookie. The form is only displayed—and the account is only created—with a valid token; the token is consumed when the account is created. A solved CAPTCHA thus allows you to create an account, and typing the address [/inscription] directly leads nowhere.

  • Lines 46–57: The cookie has the path [/inscription] ([withPath]): the browser sends it only to addresses that begin with this path. It contains only a random identifier—impossible to guess—and only the server’s cache knows whether it is valid: the cookie does not need to be signed;
  • lines 61–64: [hasItem] indicates whether the cache contains an (unexpired) entry under this key;
  • lines 75–79: To delete a cookie, you must specify the same name and the same path: to the browser, two cookies with the same name but different paths are two distinct cookies.
<?php
// src/Securite/PasseInscriptionExige.php: a ATTRIBUT PHP of our own invention (see
// Example 24), applied to actions that require a creation token
// account (see PasseInscription and the listener VerifierPasseInscription).

namespace App\Securite;

use Attribute;

#[Attribute(Attribute::TARGET_METHOD)]
class PasseInscriptionExige
{
}

An attribute [PHP] of our own invention, like the [#[Chronometre]] in Example 24, is applied to actions that require a pass. It is read by the listener [VerifierPasseInscription].

docs.title: 11.13. The listeners: src/EventListener
docs.text: Three kernel event listeners (Example 24), stored in the [src/EventListener] folder, as is customary. The [#[AsEventListener]] attribute, set on the class, specifies the event and priority; the method called is then [__invoke].

docs.title: 11.13.1. src/EventListener/FixerLangue.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/EventListener/FixerLangue.php: the language of the request (see Example 22):
// the language of the cookie [rdvmedecins_langue]; if it is a supported language, French; otherwise, another language.
//
// Priority 40: the listener bypasses AVANT Symfony’s routing (priority 32). It
// Thus, it processes TOUTES requests—even those that do not result in any
// route (404, 405 pages, etc.): their error pages are in the correct language. For the
// same reason, it also sets the translator’s language itself—a task that would otherwise be handled by
// a Symfony listener (priority 15) would otherwise have to
// from intervening.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\EventListener;

use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\RequestEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;
use Symfony\Contracts\Translation\LocaleAwareInterface;

#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::REQUEST, priority: 40)]
class FixerLangue
{
     // the cookie that stores the selected language (see LangueController)
    public const COOKIE = 'rdvmedecins_langue';

     // supported languages (translations folder); the first one is the default language
    public const LANGUES = ['fr', 'en'];

     // LocaleAwareInterface: a service that has a language, in this case the translator
    public function __construct(private LocaleAwareInterface $traducteur)
    {
    }

    public function __invoke(RequestEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $requete = $evenement->getRequest();
        $langue = $requete->cookies->get(self::COOKIE);
        $langue = in_array($langue, self::LANGUES, true) ? $langue : self::LANGUES[0];
        $requete->setLocale($langue);
        $this->traducteur->setLocale($langue);
    }
}

The request language (Example 22): the language of the cookie, if it is a supported language; otherwise, the default language (French). A difference from Example 22: priority 40 (line 21), which is higher than the routing priority (32). The listener in Example 22 (priority 20) ran after the routing; for a URL that does not match any route, the routing throws an exception before the listener, and the 404 page would have been in French even for an English-speaking user. For the same reason, the listener itself sets the translator’s language (line 41), which is typically done by a listener for [Symfony] ([LocaleAwareListener]), which is also placed after the routing. [LocaleAwareInterface] is the interface for services that have a language; the translator is one of them, and it is this translator that [Symfony] injects here.

docs.title: 11.13.2. src/EventListener/VerifierPasseInscription.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/EventListener/VerifierPasseInscription.php: actions marked with
// the #[PasseInscriptionExige] attribute (GET and POST /registration) require a
// valid pass (see src/Securite/PasseInscription.php); otherwise, redirect to
// the authentication page, along with a message. Entering the URL
// /registration does not allow you to bypass the CAPTCHA.
//
// A listener for kernel.controller (see Example 24): the action is selected, but
// it has not yet been called. To reject it, the REMPLACE (setController) is replaced by a
// function that returns a redirect.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\EventListener;

use App\Securite\PasseInscription;
use App\Securite\PasseInscriptionExige;
use App\Web\Flash;
use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ControllerEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Generator\UrlGeneratorInterface;

#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::CONTROLLER)]
class VerifierPasseInscription
{
    public function __construct(
        private PasseInscription $passes,
        private Flash $flash,
        private UrlGeneratorInterface $urls,
    ) {
    }

    public function __invoke(ControllerEvent $evenement): void
    {
        if ($evenement->getAttributes(PasseInscriptionExige::class) === []) {
            return;
        }
        if (! $this->passes->estValide($evenement->getRequest()->cookies->get(PasseInscription::COOKIE))) {
            $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
            $url = $this->urls->generate('login');
            $evenement->setController(fn () => new RedirectResponse($url));
        }
    }
}

A listener for [kernel.controller] (example 24): the action is selected but not yet called.

  • lines 37–39: [getAttributes(classe)] returns the attributes of this class carried by the action: an empty list; the action does not require a token; the listener does nothing;
  • lines 40–44: no valid token: a message is displayed, and the action is replaced ([setController]) by a function that redirects to the login page. The kernel calls this function instead of the action. URL is calculated outside the arrow function, which therefore requires only one variable.

The listener receives its services through its constructor: a listener is a service, created by the container, just like controllers.

docs.title: 11.13.3. src/EventListener/PageErreur.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/EventListener/PageErreur.php: how errors become pages HTML
// (see example 24). Three cases:
//    1. a SessionInvalide (account deleted since login) -> redirect to the
//       login page, as with an expired session;
//    2. an error HTTP: invalid request (400), insufficient role (403),
//       unknown (404), unsupported method (405), missing anti-CSRF token, or
//       invalid (419)... -> the error page, with the original code;
//    3. any other exception (a true anomaly): Symfony has already logged it in
//       the log, along with its call stack; in production (APP_ENV=prod),
//       the user sees the 500 error page—never the call stack; in
//       development, the Symfony debug page.
//
// Priority -10: after the Symfony listener that logs the exception
// (0) and after the security listener (1), which converts an access denial into
// a redirect to the login page (anonymous visitor) or a 403 error
// (authenticated user); before the one that generates the Symfony error page
// (-128).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\EventListener;

use App\Securite\AuthService;
use App\Securite\SessionInvalide;
use App\Web\Flash;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ExceptionEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Generator\UrlGeneratorInterface;
use Twig\Environment;

#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::EXCEPTION, priority: -10)]
class PageErreur
{
    public function __construct(
        private Environment $twig,
        private Flash $flash,
        private UrlGeneratorInterface $urls,
         // debug mode (APP_ENV=dev): the container parameter kernel.debug
         #[Autowire('%kernel.debug%')] private bool $debug,
    ) {
    }

    public function __invoke(ExceptionEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $e = $evenement->getThrowable();

        if ($e instanceof SessionInvalide) {
            $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
            $evenement->setResponse(AuthService::effacerCookie(new RedirectResponse($this->urls->generate('login'))));
            return;
        }

        if ($e instanceof HttpExceptionInterface) {
            $evenement->setResponse($this->page($e->getStatusCode()));
            return;
        }

         // a real anomaly: during development, the Symfony debug page
        if (! $this->debug) {
            $evenement->setResponse($this->page(500));
        }
    }

     // the error page, with the error code HTTP and its message
    private function page(int $code): Response
    {
        $message = match ($code) {
            400 => 'ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST',
