            403 => 'ERRORS.FORBIDDEN',
            404, 405 => 'ERRORS.NOT_FOUND',
            419 => 'ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED',
            default => 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
        };
        return new Response($this->twig->render('erreur.html.twig', ['titrePage' => 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE',
            'code' => $code, 'message' => $message]), $code);
    }
}

How Errors Become Pages HTML: This is the listener [PageErreur] from Example 24, expanded. It listens for the event [kernel.exception], with priority -10 (line 37): after the [Symfony] listener, which logs the exception (priority 0), and after the security component’s listener (priority 1), which converts an access denial either into a call to the entry point (anonymous visitor) or into a 403 error (authenticated user with an inappropriate role); before the handler that generates the error page, [Symfony] (-128). Three cases:

  • lines 53–57: a [SessionInvalide] (the account has been deleted): the “session expired” message, deletion of the token cookie, and the login page;
  • lines 59–62: a HTTP error: [HttpExceptionInterface] is the exception handler for exceptions with the code HTTP ([NotFoundHttpException], [AccessDeniedHttpException], [HttpException(419)]...), which is thrown by [getStatusCode]. The error page is displayed, showing this code;
  • lines 65–67: another exception is a true error. In development ([kernel.debug], example 24), the listener does nothing: the debug page for [Symfony], showing the call stack, will be displayed. In production, the 500 error page: the user never sees the call stack, which the log has already captured;
  • lines 71–82: the error page, view [erreur.html.twig], showing the message code and key. [match] ([PHP] 8) selects a value based on another, using strict equality; [404, 405 =>] covers two cases; [default] handles all others. Code 405 (Method Not Allowed: a GET on an address that only accepts POST) is displayed as a "page not found" error.

docs.title: 11.14.1. src/Controller/AuthController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/AuthController.php: the routes PUBLIQUES for the connection:
//    GE T         / redirects to the role’s home page (or to /login)
//    GE T /log  in displays the login form (with its CAPTCHA)
//    POST /logi  n checks attempt limit, CAPTCHA, username/password
//    POST /logou t logs out
//
// Protection against bots, in this order:
//    1. Too many recent failed attempts for this login from this address IP?
//       -> immediate rejection, without even checking the password;
//    2. Incorrect CAPTCHA answer? -> Denied (counted as a failed attempt);
//    3. Only then is the password verified.
// The password for an attempt rejected in steps 1 or 2 is not verified:
// A bot therefore cannot learn anything by persisting.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Role;
use App\Securite\AuthService;
use App\Securite\CaptchaService;
use App\Securite\LimiteurTentatives;
use App\Securite\UtilisateurConnecte;
use App\Web\Controleur;
use App\Web\Message;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class AuthController extends Controleur
{
    public function __construct(
        private AuthService $auth,
        private CaptchaService $captchas,
        private LimiteurTentatives $limiteur,
    ) {
    }

     // The home page for each role, immediately after logging in: the name of its route
    public static function pageAccueil(Role $role): string
    {
        return $role === Role::USER ? 'espace' : 'agenda';
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /
     // The route is public: the user, if there is one, is known
     // ($this->getUser()), but nothing is required.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/', name: 'accueil', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function accueil(): Response
    {
        $utilisateur = $this->getUser();
        return $this->redirectToRoute($utilisateur instanceof UtilisateurConnecte
            ? self::pageAccueil($utilisateur->role) : 'login');
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the "login" field
     // (used immediately after creating an account; see InscriptionController)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/login', name: 'login', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function formulaire(Request $request): Response
    {
         // Already logged in (token still valid): Go directly to the home page
        $utilisateur = $this->getUser();
        if ($utilisateur instanceof UtilisateurConnecte) {
            return $this->redirectToRoute(self::pageAccueil($utilisateur->role));
        }
         // mb_substr: 30 characters maximum
        return $this->page(mb_substr($request->query->getString('login'), 0, 30), null);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /login
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/login', name: 'connexion', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function connexion(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->verifierCsrf($request);
        $login = $request->request->getString('login');
        $password = $request->request->getString('password');
        $ip = (string) $request->getClientIp();

         // 1. Too many recent failures?
        $minutes = $this->limiteur->minutesBlocageLogin($ip, $login);
        if ($minutes > 0) {
            return $this->page($login, new Message('ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', ['minutes' => $minutes]));
        }

         // 2. The CAPTCHA
        if (! $this->captchas->verifier($request->request->getString('captchaId'),
            $request->request->getString('captcha'))) {
            $this->limiteur->echecLogin($ip, $login);
            return $this->page($login, new Message('ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA'));
        }

         // 3. The password
        $user = $login !== '' && $password !== '' ? $this->auth->valider($login, $password) : null;
        if ($user === null) {
            $this->limiteur->echecLogin($ip, $login);
            return $this->page($login, new Message('LOGIN.ERROR'));
        }

        $this->limiteur->reussiteLogin($ip, $login);
        $reponse = $this->redirectToRoute(self::pageAccueil($user->getRole()));
        $reponse->headers->setCookie($this->auth->cookieJeton($user));
        return $reponse;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /logout: Clear the token cookie, then go to the login page.
     // POST only: a simple link (GET), placed on another site, cannot
     // log the user out without their knowledge.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/logout', name: 'logout', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function deconnexion(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->verifierCsrf($request);
        return AuthService::effacerCookie($this->redirectToRoute('login'));
    }

     // the form, always with a NOUVEAU CAPTCHA (each image is used only once
     // time); the entered username is displayed again, but never the password. An error:
     // code 422, as for an invalid form (see example 19)
    private function page(string $login, ?Message $erreur): Response
    {
        return $this->render('login.html.twig', ['titrePage' => 'LOGIN.TITLE', 'erreur' => $erreur,
            'login' => $login, 'captcha' => $this->captchas->generer()],
            new Response(status: $erreur ? 422 : 200));
    }
}

The login controller, which is based on Example 27. It inherits from the application’s [Controleur] class (discussed later), which itself is a subclass of [AbstractController].

  • lines 41–44: the home page for each role, along with its route name: “My Space” for a patient, and the calendar for others;
  • lines 51–57: The address [/] links to the role’s home page or to the login page. The route is public (rule [access_control] of [security.yaml]): [getUser()] returns the user established by the authenticator, if there is one, without requiring anything. [redirectToRoute] (example 04) creates a redirect to a named route;
  • lines 63–73: a user who is already logged in goes directly to their home page. The optional parameter [login] of URL pre-fills the field (after account creation); [mb_substr] truncates it to 30 characters;
  • Lines 78–110: the login process, in the order shown in Example 27: the anti-CSRF token (discussed later), any blocking measures, the CAPTCHA, and the password. A password is never verified for an attempt rejected by the limiter or the CAPTCHA: a bot learns nothing by persisting. [getClientIp] returns the client’s address IP. If the attempt fails, the page is rendered directly (no redirection): the re-displayed form always has a new CAPTCHA and the entered login. The error is an object [Message] (see below), consisting of a key and its parameters, displayed at the bottom of the page. If successful, the login counter is reset to zero, and the browser is redirected to the role’s home page, with the token cookie ([headers->setCookie]);
  • lines 117–122: Logout deletes the token cookie (example 25). It only accepts POST, along with the anti-CSRF token: a simple link placed on another site cannot log the user out without their knowledge;
  • lines 127–132: the login page. The third parameter of [render] is the response to be populated: an error is returned with code 422 (Unprocessable Content), as with an invalid form (example 19). [new Response(status: ...)] uses a named argument ([PHP] 8): the first two parameters of the constructor retain their default values.

The login page receives the variable [titrePage], the translation key for the page title: all actions pass it to their view for the template (see below).

docs.title: 11.15. The Web Layer: Shared Services
docs.text: The [src/Web] folder contains the elements shared by the controllers.

docs.title: 11.15.1. src/Web/ApplicationModel.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/ApplicationModel.php: the cache/facade of the business layer (the equivalent
// to the [ApplicationModel] class in other versions of the application): the
// the lists of doctors and clients are retrieved from the database once, then served from
// the cache.
//
// Why use Symfony's CACHE, rather than simply a property of this object? Because
// a PHP application does not retain anything in memory from one request to the next: this
// object is a shared service, but a service only exists for the duration of a UNE request.
// The cache, on the other hand, is shared by all requests (see examples 20 and 23).
//
// These lists can be CHANGER (the ADMIN adds, modifies, or deletes doctors and
// clients): each write operation therefore goes through this facade, which OUBLIE the relevant list
// immediately afterward; the next query that needs it reads it from the database. This is
// the whole point of an entry point UNIQUE to the business layer: the rule
// "write => cache update" is only written here.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Creneau;
use App\Entity\Medecin;
use App\Entity\Rv;
use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;
use App\Metier\Metier;
use App\Metier\MetierService;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use Symfony\Contracts\Cache\CacheInterface;

// same contract as the business layer
class ApplicationModel implements Metier
{
    private const MEDECINS = 'rdvmedecins.medecins';

    private const CLIENTS = 'rdvmedecins.clients';

     // CacheInterface: the application cache (the cache.app service), as seen by
     // Symfony’s “contracts” interface, which is simpler than that of PSR-6
    public function __construct(private MetierService $metier, private CacheInterface $cache)
    {
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ retrievals from the cache

     // get(key, function): the value from the cache if it exists; otherwise, the function
     // is called, and its result is stored in the cache (with no time limit) before
     // it is rendered. Entities are stored there in serialized form (see serialize): each
     // query that reads them obtains copies, which Doctrine does not track
    public function getAllMedecins(): array
    {
        return $this->cache->get(self::MEDECINS, fn () => $this->metier->getAllMedecins());
    }

    public function getAllClients(): array
    {
        return $this->cache->get(self::CLIENTS, fn () => $this->metier->getAllClients());
    }

     // the doctor whose user account is [$idUser]—is used to preselect,
     // for a logged-in doctor, their own calendar. array_find: the first element
     // in the table that checks the condition (null if there is none)
    public function getMedecinByUserId(int $idUser): ?Medecin
    {
        return array_find($this->getAllMedecins(), fn (Medecin $m) => $m->getCompte()->getId() === $idUser);
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    public function getAllCreneaux(int $idMedecin): array
    {
        return $this->metier->getAllCreneaux($idMedecin);
    }

    public function getRvMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour): array
    {
        return $this->metier->getRvMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
    }

    public function getClientById(int $id): ?Client
    {
        return $this->metier->getClientById($id);
    }

    public function getMedecinById(int $id): ?Medecin
    {
        return $this->metier->getMedecinById($id);
    }

    public function getRvById(int $id): ?Rv
    {
        return $this->metier->getRvById($id);
    }

    public function getCreneauById(int $id): ?Creneau
    {
        return $this->metier->getCreneauById($id);
    }

    public function getAgendaMedecinJour(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour): ?AgendaMedecinJour
    {
        return $this->metier->getAgendaMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
    }

     // no cache here: the most recent data is what counts (a patient who
     // has just modified or deleted their account)
    public function getClientByUserId(int $idUser): ?Client
    {
        return $this->metier->getClientByUserId($idUser);
    }

    public function getRvAVenirClient(int $idClient): array
    {
        return $this->metier->getRvAVenirClient($idClient);
    }

    public function ajouterRv(DateTimeImmutable $jour, Creneau $creneau, Client $client): Rv
    {
        return $this->metier->ajouterRv($jour, $creneau, $client);
    }

    public function supprimerRv(Rv $rv): void
    {
        $this->metier->supprimerRv($rv);
    }

     // ------------------------------------------------ entries => cache ignored
     // (delete: the item is removed from the cache)

    public function ajouterMedecin(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        $medecin = $this->metier->ajouterMedecin($donnees);
        $this->cache->delete(self::MEDECINS);
        return $medecin;
    }

    public function modifierMedecin(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Medecin
    {
        $medecin = $this->metier->modifierMedecin($id, $donnees);
        $this->cache->delete(self::MEDECINS);
        return $medecin;
    }

    public function supprimerMedecin(int $id): void
    {
        $this->metier->supprimerMedecin($id);
        $this->cache->delete(self::MEDECINS);
    }

    public function ajouterClient(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        $client = $this->metier->ajouterClient($donnees);
        $this->cache->delete(self::CLIENTS);
        return $client;
    }

    public function modifierClient(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Client
    {
        $client = $this->metier->modifierClient($id, $donnees);
        $this->cache->delete(self::CLIENTS);
        return $client;
    }

    public function supprimerClient(int $id): void
    {
        $this->metier->supprimerClient($id);
        $this->cache->delete(self::CLIENTS);
    }
}

All versions of the application have a class named [ApplicationModel]: a single entry point from the web layer to the business layer, which keeps the lists of doctors and clients in memory. These lists are accessed by almost all pages (the drop-down list of doctors in the calendar, the list of patients in the booking window, and the administration pages) and rarely change.

What changes in [PHP] is the meaning of “in memory.” An application such as [Java], [C#], or [Python] remains in memory between requests; the [Flask] version stored these lists in the properties of a single object created at startup. An application [PHP] is recreated with each request (Example 01): the object [ApplicationModel] is indeed a shared service, but it exists only for the duration of a single request (Example 23). The lists are therefore stored in the cache of [Symfony] (example 20), which is shared by all requests.

  • Line 34: The class implements the [Metier] interface, just like [MetierService]: the controllers call the same methods, regardless of which class serves them;
  • Line 42: This time, the cache is received via the [CacheInterface] interface of the “contracts” for [Symfony] (the same [cache.app] service), which is simpler than the PSR-6 interface in the examples;
  • Lines 52–60: [get(clé, fonction)] returns the value stored under this key; if it does not exist, it calls the function (which reads the list from the database), stores its result in the cache indefinitely, and returns it. The first query that needs the list reads it directly from the database; subsequent queries find it in the cache. The cache stores the array of entities in a serialized form (example 20) and reconstructs it upon reading, along with the loaded relationships (each person’s account). The reconstructed entities are copies that the [Doctrine] entity manager does not track: they are used for display, never for writing (the business layer always re-reads from the database what it modifies);
  • lines 65–68: the physician associated with an account, retrieved from the cache list by [array_find] (example 06);
  • Lines 72–127: The other methods of the [Metier] contract simply delegate to the business layer. An account’s client ([getClientByUserId]) is always retrieved from the database, not from the cache: the most recent data takes precedence (a patient who has just modified or deleted their account);
  • Lines 132–170: the updates. Each update made by a doctor or a client does not save the relevant list ([delete]): the next query that needs it will retrieve it from the database. This is the whole point of a single entry point: the rule “a write updates the cache” is implemented only here. If the write fails (e.g., a [MetierException]), the list is not overwritten—it hasn’t changed. An application that writes to the database via a different path (another program, another version of the application using the same database) would leave the cache out of date: [php bin/console cache:pool:clear cache.app] would clear it.

docs.title: 11.15.2. src/Web/Message.php and Flash.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Web/Message.php: a message to be translated: its key and its parameters.
// Views display it as {{ message.cle|trans(message.parametres) }}.

namespace App\Web;

readonly class Message
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $cle,
        public array $parametres = [],
    ) {
    }
}

A message to be translated: a key and its parameters. Errors in the business layer ([MetierException]) and those in the controllers become [Message], which the views translate into the page’s language.

<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/Flash.php: “flash” messages—a message to be displayed UNE times on the
// SUIVANTE page (see Example 20). This is the natural complement to the
// "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern used by all forms in the application: a
// successful POST does not generate a page; it redirects (302) to a GET page; the
// message, however, must survive the redirect.
//
// Symfony stores them in the SESSION (files in the var/sessions directory, see
// config/packages/framework.yaml).
//
// A message does not contain text, but rather a CLÉ translation and its parameters
// (a Message object): it is translated at the time of display, into the language of
// the page (see templates/fragments). Two lists: successes (displayed at the top of
// the page) and errors (displayed at the bottom).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;

class Flash
{
     // the request stack, to reach the session for the current request
    public function __construct(private RequestStack $requetes)
    {
    }

    public function succes(string $cle, array $parametres = []): void
    {
        $this->ajouter('succes', $cle, $parametres);
    }

    public function erreur(string $cle, array $parametres = []): void
    {
        $this->ajouter('erreurs', $cle, $parametres);
    }

     // getFlashBag: the "bag" of flash messages for the session; add(type, message)
     // adds a message of this type to the list (see example 20)
    private function ajouter(string $type, string $cle, array $parametres): void
    {
        $this->requetes->getSession()->getFlashBag()->add($type, new Message($cle, $parametres));
    }
}

Flash messages (example 20): a message placed in the session by an action, displayed by the next page, then discarded. This complements the Post/Redirect/Get pattern, which all forms in the application follow. There are two types: success messages are displayed at the top of the page, and error messages at the bottom.

  • Line 25: the request stack ([RequestStack]), a service of [Symfony] that knows the current request and, therefore, its session. A shared service cannot receive the request itself via its constructor: it is created once and may be used for multiple requests (a main request and its sub-requests);
  • lines 41–44: the “bag” of session flash messages ([getFlashBag]), for which [add(type, message)] completes the list of this type. This is what the [addFlash] method of [AbstractController] does (Example 20); making it a service allows a message to be placed outside a controller—such as the authenticator or listeners.

The [Message] objects are stored as-is in the session: [PHP] serializes the session data (Example 20) and reconstructs it on the next request. In the views, [app.flashes('erreurs')] renders the list of messages of this type and removes them from the session.

docs.title: 11.15.3. src/Web/Controleur.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/Controleur.php: the parent class of the application’s controllers. It
// inherits from AbstractController (see Example 03), and adds token verification
// anti-CSRF token for hand-coded forms (see Example 21).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpException;

abstract class Controleur extends AbstractController
{
     // the anti-CSRF token ID for hand-coded forms: a single
     // for the entire application (in views: csrf_token('rdvmedecins')). The
     // Form component forms each have their own
    public const CSRF = 'rdvmedecins';

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Missing or invalid anti-CSRF token: the page was likely displayed before
     // the session—which contained the token—expired. Error 419, the (unofficial
     // official but commonly used) for an expired page: the listener PageErreur displays
     // "The page has expired: reload it, then try again."
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    protected function verifierCsrf(Request $request): void
    {
        if (! $this->isCsrfTokenValid(self::CSRF, $request->request->getString('_token'))) {
            throw new HttpException(419, 'jeton anti-CSRF invalide');
        }
    }
}

The parent class for controllers. Forms written manually in the views (login, logout, deletions, reservations, etc.) include an anti-CSRF token (Example 21) with the identifier [rdvmedecins]: a single identifier is sufficient here, since all these actions already require a logged-in user or a CAPTCHA. Each form in the Form component has its own token, which is validated by the component.

A missing or invalid token stops the action with a 419 error (lines 27–32), the (unofficial but widely used) code for a page that has expired: the token is stored in the session, and a page displayed before the end of the session contains a token that the server no longer recognizes. The [PageErreur] listener then displays “The page has expired: reload it, then try again.” [HttpException] is the generic exception HTTP: its constructor receives the code and a message (intended for the log, not for the user).

docs.title: 11.15.4. src/Web/Outils.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Web/Outils.php: small utility functions for the web layer:
//    - dates: "yyyy-mm-dd", days "Wednesday, September 23, 2026";
//    - input: reading a positive integer or a date sent by the browser;
//    - user: the logged-in user and their patient (Client entity).
// The STATIQUES methods are called without an object (Tools::iso($jour)); the others
// require services (the current request, security, etc.): the class is a
// service, which controllers receive via their constructor.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Web;

use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Securite\SessionInvalide;
use App\Securite\UtilisateurConnecte;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use IntlDateFormatter;
use Symfony\Bundle\SecurityBundle\Security;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;

class Outils
{
     // Security: Symfony’s security service, which knows the user of
     // current request (the one established by the authenticator)
    public function __construct(
        private RequestStack $requetes,
        private Security $securite,
        private ApplicationModel $application,
    ) {
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- dates

     // the date, if [$texte] is a valid date in the yyyy-mm-dd format; null otherwise.
     // createFromFormat accepts "2026-02-30" (which becomes March 2): we verify
     // so that the reconstructed date is written exactly as the received text
    public static function dateValide(mixed $texte): ?DateTimeImmutable
    {
        if (! is_string($texte) || ! preg_match('/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/', $texte)) {
            return null;
        }
         // "!Y-m-d": the exclamation point sets the time to midnight
        $date = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('!Y-m-d', $texte);
        return $date !== false && $date->format('Y-m-d') === $texte ? $date : null;
    }

    public static function iso(DateTimeImmutable $jour): string
    {
        return $jour->format('Y-m-d');
    }

     // "Wednesday, September 23, 2026" / "mercredi 23 septembre 2026," depending on the language
     // from the query (see Example 16). The pattern ICU: EEEE for the day of the week in
     // spelled out, d for the day, MMMM the month spelled out, y for the year
    public function formaterJour(DateTimeImmutable $jour): string
    {
        $langue = $this->requetes->getCurrentRequest()?->getLocale() ?? 'fr';
        return (new IntlDateFormatter($langue, IntlDateFormatter::NONE, IntlDateFormatter::NONE,
            pattern: 'EEEE d MMMM y'))->format($jour);
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- input

     // "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", "+2", null -> null
    public static function entierPositif(mixed $valeur): ?int
    {
        if (! is_string($valeur) || ! preg_match('/^\d{1,9}$/', $valeur)) {
            return null;
        }
        $n = (int) $valeur;
        return $n > 0 ? $n : null;
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- user

     // the logged-in user. Protected actions are only called if the user exists;
     // As a precaution, its absence is treated as an expired session
    public function utilisateur(): UtilisateurConnecte
    {
        $utilisateur = $this->securite->getUser();
        return $utilisateur instanceof UtilisateurConnecte ? $utilisateur : throw new SessionInvalide();
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // The patient (Client entity) corresponding to the logged-in user.
    //
     // The token JWT contains only the ID of COMPTE (users.id). For a role USER,
     // the corresponding client is identified using the clients.user column.
    //
     // If there is no match, it means the account has been deleted since the login
     // even though its token is still valid: it is treated as an expired session
     // expired session (see SessionInvalide).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function patientConnecte(): Client
    {
        return $this->application->getClientByUserId($this->utilisateur()->userId)
            ?? throw new SessionInvalide();
    }
}

Some utility functions. The static methods are called without an object ([Outils::iso($jour)]); the others require services: the class is therefore also a service, which the controllers receive via their constructor.

  • Lines 38–46: the date of a parameter [aaaa-mm-jj] or [null]. Two checks: the format (a regular expression), then the existence of the date. [createFromFormat] is tolerant: February 30 becomes March 2. We then re-read the resulting date and verify that it is written exactly as the received text. The [!] in the format sets the time to midnight (without it, the time would be the current time). [mixed]: any type;
  • lines 56–61: “Saturday, September 26, 2026” or “Saturday 26 September 2026,” depending on the language of the request. [IntlDateFormatter] (example 16), with a pattern rather than a style: the codes are those from the ICU library, [EEEE] for the day of the week spelled out, [d] for the day, [MMMM] for the month spelled out, and [y] for the year. The parameter [pattern] is passed by name: the parameters that precede it in the signature—and for which no value is provided—retain their default values;
  • lines 66–73: A request parameter can be a string, such as [null], or even an array ([?idMedecin[]=1], example 10). Only digits are accepted (up to nine: to avoid exceeding capacity), and the number must be strictly positive;
  • lines 79–83: the logged-in user, determined by the authenticator, which is returned by the [Security] service of [Symfony]. Protected actions are called only for an authenticated user, but the user’s absence is still handled as an expired session. [throw] is an expression ([PHP] 8): it can appear in the operator [? :];
  • lines 95–99: the patient (the [Client]) of the logged-in user. The token contains only the account ID; the client is identified by the [clients.user] column. If it does not exist, the account has been deleted since the user logged in: [SessionInvalide].

docs.title: 11.15.5. src/Twig/VuesExtension.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Twig/VuesExtension.php: a Twig extension (see Example 16), which adds
// functions to views that TOUTES pages require:
//    - user() : the logged-in user (or null), for the navigation bar;
//    - titles(     ) : possible titles for a person (Mr., Mrs., Ms.).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Twig;

use App\Form\ChampsPersonneType;
use App\Securite\AuthService;
use App\Securite\UtilisateurConnecte;
use Symfony\Bundle\SecurityBundle\Security;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;
use Twig\Extension\AbstractExtension;
use Twig\TwigFunction;

class VuesExtension extends AbstractExtension
{
    public function __construct(
        private Security $securite,
        private RequestStack $requetes,
        private AuthService $auth,
    ) {
    }

    public function getFunctions(): array
    {
        return [
            new TwigFunction('utilisateur', $this->utilisateur(...)),
            new TwigFunction('titres', fn () => ChampsPersonneType::TITRES),
        ];
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the user established by the firewall. A 404 or 405 error page is
     // generated by the firewall (routing, which fails, occurs before it; see
     // example 24): the user is then read directly from the token, so that
     // the navigation bar on the error page is complete
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public function utilisateur(): ?UtilisateurConnecte
    {
        $utilisateur = $this->securite->getUser();
        if ($utilisateur instanceof UtilisateurConnecte) {
            return $utilisateur;
        }
        $jeton = $this->requetes->getMainRequest()?->cookies->getString(AuthService::COOKIE);
        return $jeton ? $this->auth->utilisateur($jeton) : null;
    }
}

An extension of [Twig] (Example 16), which adds two functions to the views that all pages need:

  • [utilisateur()]: the logged-in user, or [null], for the navigation bar. Usually, this is the one from the [Security] service (line 44). However, a 404 or 405 error page is generated before the firewall has examined the request: the routing, which fails, takes precedence over it (Example 24). The user is then retrieved directly from the token (lines 48–49) so that the navigation bar on the error page is complete. [getMainRequest] makes the main request; the operator [?->] returns [null] without calling the method if the object is [null];
  • [titres()]: the possible titles for a person ([Mr], [Mme], [Melle]), a constant in the person form class (see below).

[$this->utilisateur(...)] (line 31) is the syntax for first-class functions ([PHP] 8.1): it creates a function that calls the [utilisateur] method of that object. The extension is automatically declared as [Twig], just like in Example 16: the container recognizes a class that inherits from [AbstractExtension].

docs.title: 11.16. Dictionaries
docs.text:
The interface texts are the same as those in other versions of the application, which stored them in nested JSON files:

{
  "LOGIN": {
    "TITLE": "Connexion",
    "USERNAME": "Login"
  }
}

The [Flask] version “flattened” them at startup: [LOGIN.TITLE] referred to the text [Connexion]. The YAML dictionaries from [Symfony] do the same (example 22): nested keys are separated by periods. We therefore simply converted the JSON files to YAML, and replaced the [{{nom}}] parameters in the other versions with those of the ICU syntax, [{nom}] (the [+intl-icu] suffix in the filenames, example 22):

APP:
    TITLE: 'RdvMedecins'
    LOGOUT: 'Se déconnecter'
MEDECINS:
    ADDED: 'Le médecin {nom} a été ajouté (login : {login}).'
ERRORS:
    TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS: 'Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.'

The files [translations/messages+intl-icu.fr.yaml] and [messages+intl-icu.en.yaml] are not reproduced here. A key is represented by [{{ 'APP.LOGOUT'|trans }}] in a view, and a parameterized text by [{{ 'MEDECINS.ADDED'|trans({nom: ..., login: ...}) }}]. A key missing from the dictionary is displayed as-is, which immediately flags an omission (and the command [php bin/console debug:translation fr] lists the keys used by the views that are missing from the dictionary). ICU enables something that previous versions could not do: the plural (“1 minute,” “15 minutes”), using the format [plural] (example 22). A text entry has been added: [ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED], the message on page 419, which is not present in other versions.

Form error messages are also keys in these dictionaries ([ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED]...): the validation component translates them into the [messages] domain, using the line [translation_domain: messages] from [framework.yaml]. Their parameters correspond to the constraints: [{limit}], for the minimum password length.

docs.title: 11.17. Forms
docs.text: "Person" forms are forms from the Form component (examples 18 and 19): a type class describes the fields and their constraints; the action creates the form ([createForm]), passes the request to it ([handleRequest]), and then checks whether it has been submitted and is valid ([isSubmitted], [isValid]). An invalid form is redisplayed, showing the user’s input and error messages below the fields (excluding passwords: a [PasswordType] field is never redisplayed). The anti-CSRF token for each form is verified by the component itself.

docs.title: 11.17.1. src/Form/ChampsPersonneType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Form/ChampsPersonneType.php: the fields in the “person” forms and their
// constraints (see examples 18 and 19). Three forms share the same
// identity fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//    ChampsPersonneTyp         e title, first name, last name
//     ├─ PersonneTy           pe + login / password FACULTATIFS, version
//                                 │ (ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor/client)
//     ├─ InscriptionTy        pe + login / password / confirmation OBLIGATOIRES
//                                 │ (a patient creates an account)
//     └─ MonCompteTy          pe + username, optional new password,
//                                  ACTUEL password required, version
//                                  (a patient modifies their account)
//
// The child classes HÉRITENT of this one (in the sense of PHP): their buildForm first calls
// first calls the mother’s class, then adds its own fields.
//
// Forms do not have a data class (data_class, see Example 19): the
// validated input is an associative array, which the données() method transforms into
// DonneesPersonne for the business layer.
//
// Labels, tooltips, and error messages are CLÉS from the
// dictionaries: the Form component translates labels and tooltips, while the
// Validator component translates the error messages (see config/packages/framework.yaml).
// Sequentially: Constraints are checked in order, and the validation
// stops at the first constraint that is not met—only one message per field.
// The maximum lengths are those of the columns SQL.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Form;

use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;
use Symfony\Component\Form\AbstractType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\CallbackTransformer;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\ChoiceType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\TextType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\OptionsResolver\OptionsResolver;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

abstract class ChampsPersonneType extends AbstractType
{
    public const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

     // login: lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore—30 characters maximum
    public const FORMAT_LOGIN = '/^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/';

     // Minimum length for a patient’s password CHOISI
    public const MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6;

    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        $builder
             // array_combine: ['Mr' => 'Mr', ...], the label and value of each
             // option; choice_translation_domain false: the titles are not translated
            ->add('titre', ChoiceType::class, [
                'label' => 'PERSONNES.TITLE_LABEL',
                'choices' => array_combine(self::TITRES, self::TITRES),
                'choice_translation_domain' => false,
                'invalid_message' => 'ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE',
                'constraints' => [new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE')],
            ])
            ->add('prenom', TextType::class, [
                'label' => 'PERSONNES.FIRSTNAME_LABEL',
                'attr' => ['maxlength' => 20],
                'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                    new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED'),
                    new Assert\Length(max: 20, maxMessage: 'ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG'),
                ])],
            ])
            ->add('nom', TextType::class, [
                'label' => 'PERSONNES.LASTNAME_LABEL',
                'attr' => ['maxlength' => 20],
                'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                    new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED'),
                    new Assert\Length(max: 20, maxMessage: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG'),
                ])],
            ]);
    }

     // common options: an invalid form is sent back to the browser as-is,
     // without validation by the browser itself (see example 19: the SERVEUR
     // is the authoritative version); a message with an invalid anti-CSRF token
    public function configureOptions(OptionsResolver $resolver): void
    {
        $resolver->setDefaults([
            'attr' => ['novalidate' => 'novalidate'],
            'csrf_message' => 'ERRORS.PAGE_EXPIRED',
        ]);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the login field, which is common to all child forms. A login is always in
     // all lowercase: a TRANSFORMATEUR (CallbackTransformer) converts the input AVANT
     // its validation. Its first function transforms the form value into
     // displayed text (in this case, no action required), and the second function transforms the input into the form value
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    protected static function ajouterLogin(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        $builder->add('login', TextType::class, ['label' => 'PERSONNES.LOGIN_LABEL', 'required' => false,
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 30, 'autocomplete' => 'off'], ...$options]);
        $builder->get('login')->addModelTransformer(new CallbackTransformer(
            fn (?string $login) => $login,
            fn (?string $login) => $login === null ? null : mb_strtolower($login)));
    }

     // the validated input—the data expected by the business layer. Empty fields
     // are set to null (the Form component converts them this way)
    public static function donnees(array $saisie): DonneesPersonne
    {
        $motDePasse = $saisie['password'] ?? null;
        return new DonneesPersonne($saisie['titre'], $saisie['nom'], $saisie['prenom'],
            $saisie['login'] ?? null, $motDePasse === '' ? null : $motDePasse,
            isset($saisie['version']) && ctype_digit((string) $saisie['version']) ? (int) $saisie['version'] : null);
    }
}

Three forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name): the administrator form (for a doctor or a client), the client account creation form, and “Manage My Account.” Their common parent class is abstract; each of its child classes extends these fields. None of these forms has a data class (the [data_class] option from Example 19): their data consists of an associative array, with one element per field.

  • lines 44–50: the input rules, in the form of constants, which are also read by the views (the list of titles, by function [titres()] from extension [Twig]);
  • lines 57–63: the title, a list ([ChoiceType], Example 18). [array_combine] generates the array [['Mr' => 'Mr', ...]]: the label for each option and its value. [choice_translation_domain: false]: The titles are not translation keys. [invalid_message]: The message for a value that is not part of the list (a manually constructed query);
  • Lines 64–79: first name and last name. The constraint [Sequentially] (example 09) checks its constraints in order and stops at the first one that is not met: only one message per field. [Length(max: 20)]: 20 characters maximum; the column length is SQL; the attribute HTML [maxlength] prevents more characters from being entered. Spaces at the beginning and end of an entry are removed by the Form component itself (the [trim] option for a text field is set to [true]), and an empty entry becomes [null]; a field with the option [PasswordType], on the other hand, is not cleaned: spaces can be part of a password;
  • Lines 85–91: common options. [novalidate] disables browser validations ([required], [maxlength]...) when the form is submitted: the server performs the validation, and its result is final (example 19). [csrf_message]: the message for a invalid anti-CSRF token, the one from the 419 page;
  • lines 99–106: the login, common to all three girls, to which each adds her own options (the operator [...] adds elements from one array to another; a key present in both takes on the last value). A login is always in lowercase: a transformer converts the input before it is validated. A model transformer ([addModelTransformer]) has two functions: the first transforms the form data into a displayed value (in this case, no action is required), and the second transforms the entered value into form data. [CallbackTransformer] creates a transformer based on these two functions;
  • Lines 110–116: The validated input is converted to [DonneesPersonne] for the business layer: the business layer is not aware of the forms. An empty password is [null] (unchanged, or the default value); the version (the hidden field of the optimistic lock, e.g., 28) is an integer, or [null].

docs.title: 11.17.2. src/Form/PersonneType.php, InscriptionType.php, MonCompteType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Form/PersonneType.php: a form for a doctor or a client (ADMIN):
// login and password FACULTATIFS (see src/Metier/DonneesPersonne.php).

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\HiddenType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\OptionsResolver\OptionsResolver;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class PersonneType extends ChampsPersonneType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        parent::buildForm($builder, $options);
        $creation = $options['creation'];
         // An empty field is accepted: the constraints apply only to a value that is entered
        self::ajouterLogin($builder, [
            'help' => $creation ? 'PERSONNES.LOGIN_HELP_CREATE' : 'PERSONNES.LOGIN_HELP_EDIT',
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Regex(self::FORMAT_LOGIN, message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN')],
        ]);
        $builder->add('password', PasswordType::class, [
            'label' => 'PERSONNES.PASSWORD_LABEL',
            'required' => false,
            'help' => $creation ? 'PERSONNES.PASSWORD_HELP_CREATE' : 'PERSONNES.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT',
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 72, 'autocomplete' => 'new-password'],
             // Maximum of 72 characters: beyond that, bcrypt ignores the rest
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Length(max: 72, maxMessage: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG')],
        ]);
         // modification: the version of the displayed record, in a hidden field (the
         // optimistic lock)
        if (! $creation) {
            $builder->add('version', HiddenType::class);
        }
    }

     // an option of our own (see example 28): create or update form
    public function configureOptions(OptionsResolver $resolver): void
    {
        parent::configureOptions($resolver);
        $resolver->setDefaults(['creation' => true]);
    }
}

The administrator form. [parent::buildForm] (line 17) adds the fields from the parent class; next come the username and password, which are optional: a constraint applies only to a value that is entered (except for [NotBlank]), so an empty field is accepted. [Regex] validates the login format; [Length(max: 72)] limits the password length: [bcrypt] considers only the first 72 bytes (Example 25). The option [creation] (lines 40–44), an option we devised, declared with its default value (example 28), distinguishes between creation and modification: the tooltips differ (“by default, the name is in lowercase,” “leave blank to keep it unchanged”), and only the modification has the hidden version field.

<?php
// src/Form/InscriptionType.php: “Create a customer account”: username, password, and
// confirmation OBLIGATOIRES.

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\RepeatedType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class InscriptionType extends ChampsPersonneType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        parent::buildForm($builder, $options);
        self::ajouterLogin($builder, [
            'required' => true,
            'help' => 'INSCRIPTION.LOGIN_HELP',
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 30, 'autocomplete' => 'username'],
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED'),
                new Assert\Regex(self::FORMAT_LOGIN, message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN'),
            ])],
        ]);
        $builder->add('password', RepeatedType::class, self::motDePasseRepete(true));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the password and its confirmation: a field RÉPÉTÉ (see Example 19), where
     // both entries must be identical (otherwise: invalid_message). Common to
     // the registration (required) and the patient’s account (optional).
     // {limit}: in the message PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT, the minimum length;
     // help_translation_parameters: the help text parameters
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static function motDePasseRepete(bool $obligatoire): array
    {
        $longueur = new Assert\Length(min: self::MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, max: 72,
            minMessage: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT', maxMessage: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG');
        return [
            'type' => PasswordType::class,
            'required' => $obligatoire,
            'invalid_message' => 'ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER',
            'first_options' => [
                'label' => $obligatoire ? 'PERSONNES.PASSWORD_LABEL' : 'MON_COMPTE.NEW_PASSWORD_LABEL',
                'help' => $obligatoire ? 'INSCRIPTION.PASSWORD_HELP' : 'PERSONNES.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT',
                'help_translation_parameters' => ['min' => self::MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN],
            ],
            'second_options' => ['label' => 'COMPTE.CONFIRMATION_LABEL'],
            'options' => ['attr' => ['maxlength' => 72, 'autocomplete' => 'new-password']],
            'constraints' => $obligatoire
                ? [new Assert\Sequentially([new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED'), $longueur])]
                : [$longueur],
        ];
    }
}

Creating a customer account: login and password are required, and the password must be confirmed. The password is a repeated field ([RepeatedType], example 19): two [PasswordType] fields, whose entries must be identical (otherwise, the message [invalid_message] is displayed below the first one). Its options are generated by a static method, shared with “Manage My Account” (lines 36–55):

  • [first_options] and [second_options]: the options for each of the two fields; [options]: the options they have in common;
  • [help_translation_parameters]: the parameters for the help text, “At least {min} characters.”;
  • the minimum length is required only for the password chosen by a patient (6 characters). The message [ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT] contains [{limit}], the parameter that the constraint [Length] provides to its message;
  • [autocomplete="new-password"]: The browser offers to generate a password instead of filling in the field with the saved password.
<?php
// src/Form/MonCompteType.php: "Manage My Account" (one patient): login required,
// new password optional, password ACTUEL required.

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\HiddenType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\RepeatedType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class MonCompteType extends ChampsPersonneType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $builder, array $options): void
    {
        parent::buildForm($builder, $options);
        self::ajouterLogin($builder, [
            'required' => true,
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 30, 'autocomplete' => 'username'],
            'constraints' => [new Assert\Sequentially([
                new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED'),
                new Assert\Regex(self::FORMAT_LOGIN, message: 'ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN'),
            ])],
        ]);
         // optional: blank = password unchanged
        $builder->add('password', RepeatedType::class, InscriptionType::motDePasseRepete(false));
         // the password ACTUEL, required for any account changes; mapped
         // false: it is not part of the form data; it is read separately
        $builder->add('current_password', PasswordType::class, [
            'label' => 'MON_COMPTE.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL',
            'help' => 'MON_COMPTE.CURRENT_PASSWORD_HELP',
            'mapped' => false,
            'attr' => ['maxlength' => 72, 'autocomplete' => 'current-password'],
            'constraints' => [new Assert\NotBlank(message: 'ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED')],
        ]);
        $builder->add('version', HiddenType::class);
    }
}

“Manage My Account”: the new password is optional (empty: unchanged), the current password is required. [mapped: false] (line 33): the current password is not part of the form data ([getData()] does not contain it); the action reads it separately, via [$formulaire->get('current_password')->getData()]. It is not validated here, but by the action: an incorrect password must be counted by the attempt limiter as a failed login. ([Symfony] has a constraint, [UserPassword], which compares the entered password to the logged-in user’s password; this constraint is not applicable here: our logged-in user, [UtilisateurConnecte], does not contain the hash of their password.)

docs.title: 11.18. View Templates
docs.text:
The [src/Vues] folder contains the view templates: objects created by an action, which the view simply reads. The rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. Actions prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; the views place this data into the HTML. All these classes are of type [readonly] and have only properties, which are initialized by their constructor. The folder is excluded from the services ([config/services.yaml]): these are data, not services.

<?php
// src/Views/OptionVue.php: an option from a drop-down list (doctor, patient).
//
// The src/Views folder contains the "view models": objects
// constructed once by an action, which the view simply reads. Rule
// followed by all pages: no logic in the views. The actions
// prepare formatted data DÉJÀ (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,”
// "8:00 - 8:20", selection = true...) and already filtered according to the user’s
// the user; the views simply place them in the HTML.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class OptionVue
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $id,
        public string $libelle,
        public bool $selectionne,
    ) {
    }
}

An option in a drop-down list: the ID, the label, and whether the option is selected?

<?php
// src/Views/LigneAgenda.php: a row in the displayed calendar (a time slot).

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class LigneAgenda
{
    public function __construct(
        public int $idCreneau,
        public string $horaire,      // "8:00 - 8:20"
        public bool $libre,
         // displayed name for a booked slot; null = “Reserved”
        public ?string $patient,

        public string $urlReserver,
         // filled in only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
        public ?int $idRv,
    ) {
    }
}

A calendar entry: a time slot, and what the logged-in user is authorized to view and do with it. [patient] is populated only if the user has permission to see the patient’s name; [reservable] indicates whether to display the “Book” button; [idRv] indicates whether to display the “Cancel” button.

The displayed calendar and the booking window: for the administrator and doctors, the list of patients to choose from; for a patient, their own name. <?php
// src/Views/ClesPersonnes.php: translation keys specific to each type of
// person (doctors or clients), for the common people/list views and
// "People/Form" views.

namespace App\Vues;

readonly class ClesPersonnes

        public string $titre,                 // "Doctors"

     // the eight keys of a dictionary section ("MEDECINS", "CLIENTS")
