docs.title: 11.19. The web layer: routes and controllers
11.19.1. Routes
docs.text:
Routes are described by the [#[Route]] attributes of controllers (Example 02), which are loaded by the [config/routes.yaml] file. The [debug:router] command lists them all, along with their names, methods, and paths:

$ php bin/console debug:router
 ----------------------- ---------- --------------------------
  Name                    Method     Path
 ----------------------- ---------- --------------------------
  agenda                  GET        /agenda
  agenda_reserver         POST       /agenda/reserver
  agenda_annuler          POST       /agenda/annuler
  accueil                 GET        /
  login                   GET        /login
  connexion               POST       /login
  logout                  POST       /logout
  clients_liste           GET        /clients
  clients_ajout           GET|POST   /clients/ajouter
  clients_modification    GET|POST   /clients/{id}/modifier
  clients_supprimer       POST       /clients/{id}/supprimer
  espace                  GET        /mon-espace
  espace_annuler          POST       /mon-espace/annuler
  compte                  GET|POST   /mon-compte
  compte_supprimer        POST       /mon-compte/supprimer
  inscription_acces       POST       /inscription/acces
  inscription             GET|POST   /inscription
  langue                  GET        /langue/{code}
  medecins_liste          GET        /medecins
  medecins_ajout          GET|POST   /medecins/ajouter
  medecins_modification   GET|POST   /medecins/{id}/modifier
  medecins_supprimer      POST       /medecins/{id}/supprimer
 ----------------------- ---------- --------------------------

The URL files correspond to other versions of the application: modifying and deleting a doctor are POST requests ([/medecins/{id}/modifier], [/medecins/{id}/supprimer]), not PUT and DELETE as in Example 28. The code always generates the URL based on the route names ([redirectToRoute('login')], [path('agenda')] in the views, Example 04): changing a URL requires modifying only its [#[Route]] attribute.

Access rules are not in the controllers, but in the [access_control] rules of [config/packages/security.yaml], as shown above: one rule per URL prefix ([^/(medecins|clients)] for the administrator, [^/mon-] for patients...), and a final rule that requires an authenticated user for all other URL. The application’s URL routes were chosen for this purpose: all pages within the same role begin the same way. A URL route that does not match any route returns a 404 page, even to an anonymous visitor; a request for GET directed at a URL that exists only as POST ([/logout]) results in a 405 page, presented as a "page not found" (handler [PageErreur]).

docs.title: 11.19.2. src/Controller/LangueController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/LangueController.php: GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: both
// FR / EN buttons on the navigation bar. Public route: users should be able to
// change the language before logging in.
//
// The selection is stored in a cookie: with each subsequent request, the listener
// FixerLangue re-reads it and sets the request language. Then you return to the
// page you came from (see Example 22).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\EventListener\FixerLangue;
use App\Web\Controleur;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Cookie;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class LangueController extends Controleur
{
    public function __construct(#[Autowire(env: 'bool:COOKIE_SECURE')] private bool $cookieSecure)
    {
    }

     // {code} is limited to supported languages (requirements): /language/de returns a 404 page
     #[Route('/langue/{code}', name: 'langue', requirements: ['code' => 'fr|en'], methods: ['GET'])]
    public function changer(Request $request, string $code): Response
    {
        $reponse = $this->redirect($this->pageDOrigine($request));
        $reponse->headers->setCookie(Cookie::create(FixerLangue::COOKIE, $code)
            ->withExpires(new \DateTimeImmutable('+1 year'))
            ->withSecure($this->cookieSecure)
            ->withHttpOnly(true)
            ->withSameSite(Cookie::SAMESITE_LAX));
        return $reponse;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the previous page, based on the "Referer" header HTTP sent by the browser.
     // We only keep the path (/agenda?...): redirect to an address
     // provided by the request would allow the user to be sent to a
     // different site (a vulnerability known as an “open redirect”).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function pageDOrigine(Request $request): string
    {
        $referer = $request->headers->get('Referer');
        $url = $referer ? parse_url($referer) : false;
        $chemin = $url['path'] ?? '';
         // "//site.com/..." would be interpreted by the browser as a URL on a
         // AUTRE site: also rejected
        if (! isset($url['scheme']) || ! str_starts_with($chemin, '/') || str_starts_with($chemin, '//')
            || str_starts_with($chemin, '/langue/')) {
            return '/';
        }
        return isset($url['query']) ? "$chemin?{$url['query']}" : $chemin;
    }
}

The FR / EN buttons on the navigation bar: the language selection is stored in a cookie for one year (example 22), then the browser returns to the page it came from. The cookie is [HttpOnly]: the [JavaScript] on the page does not need to read it. It is unsigned: the listener [FixerLangue] verifies its value, and an unknown value results in French (see the chapter on ranges).

  • Line 29: [requirements: ['code' => 'fr|en']] accepts only these two values for the parameter [{code}]: [/langue/de] does not correspond to any route (404 page);
  • Lines 47–59: The previous page is specified by the header HTTP ***[Referer], which the browser sends with the request. This data is provided by the client and is therefore suspect: redirecting to a full URL from the request would allow an attacker to send the user to their own site via a link to ***[/langue/fr] that includes a fake ***[Referer] (the so-called “open redirect”* vulnerability). Therefore, we retain only the path and parameters ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&...]), extracted by the function [parse_url] from [PHP]*, which splits a URL into its parts ([scheme], [host], [path], [query]...). A path starting with [//] is also rejected: a browser interprets [//site.com/page] as an address on *another site. Finally, we cannot return to [/langue/...]: a loop.

docs.title: 11.19.3. src/Controller/AgendaController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/AgendaController.php: the appointment calendar page: selecting a doctor and
// selecting a day, that doctor’s schedule for that day, booking and canceling
// appointments.
//
//    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-2             3 the page
//    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7     the same page, with the
//                                                           booking window
//                                                           for time slot 7 is open
//    POST /calendar/book                                   creates an appointment
//    POST /calendar/canc                                  el cancels an appointment
//
// The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, mark it as a
// bookmark, or use the browser’s “Back” button—without a single line of
// JavaScript.
//
// What everyone sees and can do:
//
//    | rol         e | displayed re           served slot           | Reserve | Cancel |
//   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
//    | ADMIN, DOCTOR | patient name                         | for     a patient | yes |
//                  |                                    |            | selected from list | |
//    | USER (patient)| “Reserved,” or SON name if it i s | for himself, if he| no (*) |
//                  | | his own            appointment          | does not already have an appointment| |
//                  |                                                         | | upcoming | |
//
//    (*) The patient cancels their appointment from their "My Account" page.
//
// CONFIDENTIALITÉ: For a patient, the names of the AUTRES patients are not
// simply hidden by the view—it is never passed to the view. The HTML sent
// to the browser therefore does not contain it, even if hidden (a simple "View Source"
// "View Source" would reveal it otherwise).
//
// No past reservations: the “Reserve” button only appears for
// today and the following days (and the business layer would reject it outright
// case).
//
// Security: all URL /calendar operations require an authenticated user, and
// /calendar/cancel the role ADMIN or DOCTOR (see config/packages/security.yaml).
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Domain\AgendaMedecinJour;
use App\Entity\Client;
use App\Entity\Personne;
use App\Entity\Role;
use App\Metier\Dates;
use App\Metier\MetierException;
use App\Vues\AgendaVue;
use App\Vues\LigneAgenda;
use App\Vues\OptionVue;
use App\Vues\ReservationVue;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use App\Web\Controleur;
use App\Web\Flash;
use App\Web\Message;
use App\Web\Outils;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\BadRequestHttpException;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route('/agenda')]
class AgendaController extends Controleur
{
    public function __construct(
        private ApplicationModel $application,
        private Outils $outils,
        private Flash $flash,
    ) {
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /agenda
     // The parameters of URL are read in raw format ($request->query), to distinguish a
     // ABSENT parameter (null) from a VIDE parameter (?idMedecin=).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('', name: 'agenda', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function afficher(Request $request): Response
    {
        $erreur = null;
        $utilisateur = $this->outils->utilisateur();
        $droits = $this->droits();

         // the day: the one from URL if it is valid, otherwise today
        $jour = Dates::aujourdhui();
        $jourBrut = $request->query->get('jour');
        if ($jourBrut !== null) {
            $jourDemande = Outils::dateValide($jourBrut);
            if ($jourDemande !== null) {
                $jour = $jourDemande;
            } else {
                $erreur = 'ERRORS.INVALID_DATE';
            }
        }
        $jourReservable = $jour >= Dates::aujourdhui();

         // the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
        $idMedecinBrut = $request->query->get('idMedecin');
        $idMedecin = Outils::entierPositif($idMedecinBrut);
        if ($idMedecinBrut === null && $utilisateur->role === Role::DOCTOR) {
            $idMedecin = $this->application->getMedecinByUserId($utilisateur->userId)?->getId();
        }

         // the drop-down list of doctors
        $medecins = array_map(fn (Personne $m) => self::option($m, $m->getId() === $idMedecin),
            $this->application->getAllMedecins());

         // the calendar, if a doctor is selected (and the date is valid)
        $agenda = null;
        if ($idMedecin !== null && $erreur === null) {
            $agendaMedecin = $this->application->getAgendaMedecinJour($idMedecin, $jour);
            if ($agendaMedecin === null) {
                $erreur = 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND';
            } else {
                $agenda = $this->agendaVue($agendaMedecin, $droits, $jourReservable);
            }
        }

         // the booking window: only if the requested time slot is bookable
         // by this user. array_find: the first element that checks the
         // condition (null if there is none)
        $reservation = null;
        $idCreneau = Outils::entierPositif($request->query->get('reserver'));
        if ($agenda !== null && $idCreneau !== null) {
            $ligne = array_find($agenda->lignes,
                fn (LigneAgenda $l) => $l->idCreneau === $idCreneau && $l->reservable);
            if ($ligne !== null) {
                $reservation = new ReservationVue(
                    $ligne->idCreneau,
                    $ligne->horaire,
                    $droits['gestionnaire']
                        ? array_map(fn (Client $c) => self::option($c, false), $this->application->getAllClients())
                        : [],
                    $droits['patient']?->libelle());
            }
        }

        return $this->render('agenda.html.twig', [
            'titrePage' => 'AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE',
            'erreur' => $erreur ? new Message($erreur) : null,
            'medecins' => $medecins,
            'idMedecin' => $idMedecin,
            'jour' => Outils::iso($jour),
            'agenda' => $agenda,
            'reservation' => $reservation,
             // the displayed calendar, without the reservation window
            'urlRetour' => $idMedecin !== null ? $this->urlAgenda($idMedecin, $jour) : $this->generateUrl('agenda'),
            'info' => $this->infoPatient($droits, $agenda),
        ]);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /calendar/boo  k fields: idMedecin, day, idCreneau, idClient
    //
     // For a patient (USER), the field idClient is IGNORÉ: he always makes a reservation
     // for himself. Trusting a field sent by the browser
     // would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name.
    //
     // "Post/Redirect/Get" pattern: regardless of the result, we do not generate
     // a page here—we display a flash message and redirect to the calendar
     // (see example 20).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/reserver', name: 'agenda_reserver', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function reserver(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->verifierCsrf($request);
        [$idMedecin, $jour] = $this->agendaDemande($request);
        $idCreneau = Outils::entierPositif($request->request->get('idCreneau'));
        if ($idMedecin === null || $idCreneau === null) {
             // -> "invalid request" page (see src/EventListener/PageErreur.php)
            throw new BadRequestHttpException('agenda ou créneau invalide');
        }
        $utilisateur = $this->outils->utilisateur();

        if ($utilisateur->estPatient()) {
            $client = $this->outils->patientConnecte();
        } else {
            $idClient = Outils::entierPositif($request->request->get('idClient'));
            if ($idClient === null) {
                 // No patient selected: the booking window reopens
                $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT');
                return $this->redirect($this->urlAgenda($idMedecin, $jour, $idCreneau));
            }
            $client = $this->application->getClientById($idClient);
        }

        $creneau = $this->application->getCreneauById($idCreneau);
        if ($client === null) {
            $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND');
        } elseif ($creneau === null || $creneau->getMedecin()->getId() !== $idMedecin) {
            $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND');
        } else {
            try {
                 // the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
                 // patient, available time slot) are verified by the business layer
                $this->application->ajouterRv($jour, $creneau, $client);
                $this->flash->succes('AGENDA.BOOKED');
            } catch (MetierException $e) {
                 // same rule, but a message to the second person when it is the
                 // patient themselves who is making the appointment (“You already have...” rather than
                 // “This patient…”). The other exceptions (true anomalies) are
                 // are not caught: 500 error.
                if ($e->cle === 'ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT' && $utilisateur->estPatient()) {
                    $this->flash->erreur('AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO');
                } else {
                    $this->flash->erreur($e->cle, $e->parametres);
                }
            }
        }
        return $this->redirect($this->urlAgenda($idMedecin, $jour));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /agenda/canc  el fields: idRv, idMedecin, day
     // (a patient cancels SON an appointment from "My Account," not from here)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/annuler', name: 'agenda_annuler', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function annuler(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->verifierCsrf($request);
        [$idMedecin, $jour] = $this->agendaDemande($request);
        $idRv = Outils::entierPositif($request->request->get('idRv'));
        if ($idMedecin === null || $idRv === null) {
            throw new BadRequestHttpException('agenda ou rendez-vous invalide');
        }
        $rv = $this->application->getRvById($idRv);
        if ($rv === null) {
             // already canceled (by someone else, or by double-clicking)
            $this->flash->erreur('ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND');
        } else {
            $this->application->supprimerRv($rv);
            $this->flash->succes('AGENDA.CANCELLED');
        }
        return $this->redirect($this->urlAgenda($idMedecin, $jour));
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // Who is logged in, and what permissions do they have on this page?
        // administrator: ADMIN or DOCTOR;
        // patient: the logged-in client (role USER), otherwise null;
        // patientPeutReserver: a USER with no upcoming appointments.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function droits(): array
    {
        if (! $this->outils->utilisateur()->estPatient()) {
            return ['gestionnaire' => true, 'patient' => null, 'patientPeutReserver' => false];
        }
        $patient = $this->outils->patientConnecte();
        $rvAVenir = $this->application->getRvAVenirClient($patient->getId());
        return ['gestionnaire' => false, 'patient' => $patient, 'patientPeutReserver' => $rvAVenir === []];
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the doctor’s calendar, formatted for display—and filtered according to permissions
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function agendaVue(AgendaMedecinJour $agendaMedecin, array $droits, bool $jourReservable): AgendaVue
    {
        $idMedecin = $agendaMedecin->medecin->getId();
        $jour = $agendaMedecin->jour;
        $lignes = [];
        foreach ($agendaMedecin->creneauxMedecinJour as $cmj) {
            $creneau = $cmj->creneau;
            $rv = $cmj->rv;
            $libre = $rv === null;
             // the appointment for the connected patient?
            $moi = $rv !== null && $droits['patient'] !== null
                && $rv->getClient()->getId() === $droits['patient']->getId();
            $lignes[] = new LigneAgenda(
                idCreneau: $creneau->getId(),
                horaire: $creneau->horaire(),
                libre: $libre,
                 // LE privacy setting: a patient only sees the name of
                 // SON appointment; for others, null (the view displays “Reserved”)
                patient: $rv !== null && ($droits['gestionnaire'] || $moi) ? $rv->getClient()->libelle() : null,
                moi: $moi,
                reservable: $libre && $jourReservable && ($droits['gestionnaire'] || $droits['patientPeutReserver']),
                urlReserver: $this->urlAgenda($idMedecin, $jour, $creneau->getId()),
                idRv: $rv !== null && $droits['gestionnaire'] ? $rv->getId() : null);
        }
        return new AgendaVue($agendaMedecin->medecin->libelle(), $this->outils->formaterJour($jour), $lignes);
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- Utility functions

     // the hidden fields idMedecin / day in the forms POST; [null, null] if
     // are invalid
    private function agendaDemande(Request $request): array
    {
        $idMedecin = Outils::entierPositif($request->request->get('idMedecin'));
        $jour = Outils::dateValide($request->request->get('jour'));
        return $idMedecin === null || $jour === null ? [null, null] : [$idMedecin, $jour];
    }

     // /calendar?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23[&reserver=7]: generateUrl adds at the end
     // from URL the parameters that are not path parameters (see Example 16)
    private function urlAgenda(int $idMedecin, DateTimeImmutable $jour, ?int $reserver = null): string
    {
        $parametres = ['idMedecin' => $idMedecin, 'jour' => Outils::iso($jour)];
        if ($reserver !== null) {
            $parametres['reserver'] = $reserver;
        }
        return $this->generateUrl('agenda', $parametres);
    }

    private static function option(Personne $p, bool $selectionne): OptionVue
    {
        return new OptionVue($p->getId(), $p->libelle(), $selectionne);
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     // the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment
     // (why there is no "Book" button), or null. Irrelevant if SON
     // appointment appears in the displayed calendar (in blue): this is the case just
     // after it has just been booked, in which case the message would be moved.
     // array_any: Does at least one element satisfy the condition?
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function infoPatient(array $droits, ?AgendaVue $agenda): ?string
    {
        if ($droits['patient'] === null || $droits['patientPeutReserver']) {
            return null;
        }
        $rvAffiche = $agenda !== null && array_any($agenda->lignes, fn (LigneAgenda $l) => $l->moi);
        return $rvAffiche ? null : 'AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO';
    }
}

The application’s main page. The header comment summarizes what each user sees and can do. The [#[Route('/agenda')]] attribute of the class (line 66) specifies the start of the path for all its routes (example 02): the route [''] is [/agenda] itself.

docs.title: 11.19.3.1. The URL on the page
docs.text: The entire page is described by its URL: [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-26] displays Doctor 1’s schedule for that day; [&reserver=4] also opens the booking window for slot 4. You can reload the page, bookmark it, or use the browser’s Back button without a single line of [JavaScript]. The form at the top of the page (for selecting the doctor and the day) is a GET form (example 17): it reloads the page with new parameters. The appointment booking window is opened by a simple link and closed by a link to the same page without the [reserver] parameter.

docs.title: 11.19.3.2. GET /calendar
docs.text:
Lines 81–154:

  • the parameters of URL are read as-is ([$request->query->get('jour')]), without validation by [Symfony]: a missing parameter ([null]) is not an error (the system defaults to today or “no doctor”); an invalid date is an error, displayed at the bottom of the page (the doctor and day selections remain visible, but the calendar is not displayed); a doctor or time slot number that is not a positive integer is simply ignored;
  • a logged-in user who has not selected a doctor sees their schedule: their doctor is retrieved via their account ([getMedecinByUserId]). [?->getId()]: the nullsafe operator returns [null] if the object is [null], instead of raising an error;
  • the drop-down list of doctors: [array_map] converts each doctor to [OptionVue];
  • the calendar, formatted and filtered according to the user’s permissions ([agendaVue], below);
  • the booking window, only if the requested time slot is bookable by that user: a patient who attempts to generate the URL [&reserver=2] for a booked time slot would get nothing. [array_find] (example 06) returns the first element of an array that satisfies a condition, or [null]. The list of patients is provided only to the administrator and doctors; a patient receives only their own name;
  • the view receives its variables ([render], example 13), including [titrePage] and [erreur], which are read by the template.

docs.title: 11.19.3.3. POST /agenda/reserve
docs.text:
Lines 167–215:

  • the anti-CSRF token, followed by the hidden fields from the booking form (doctor, day, time slot). Since these are invalid, this must be a manually crafted request: [BadRequestHttpException], the “invalid request” page (400);
  • For a patient, the field [idClient] is ignored: the patient always makes an appointment for themselves ([Outils::patientConnecte]). Relying on a field sent by the browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation on behalf of someone else. For the administrator and doctors, a patient must have been selected; otherwise, the reservation window reopens with a message;
  • the time slot must belong to the doctor listed on the page;
  • the business rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment, available time slot) are verified by the business logic layer. A [MetierException] becomes a flash error message; its public properties [cle] and [parametres] provide the message. The same rejection—“one upcoming appointment”—is phrased in the second person for the patient themselves (“You already have…”). Any other exception is not intercepted: this is a true error (500 page);
  • in all cases, the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (example 20): a pop-up message and a redirect to the calendar.

docs.title: 11.19.3.4. POST /calendar/cancel
docs.text: Lines 221–239: Cancellation of an appointment by the administrator or a doctor (rule [^/agenda/annuler$] derived from [security.yaml]). An appointment that no longer exists (already canceled by someone else, or due to a double-click) is not an error: it’s just a message.

docs.title: 11.19.3.5. Permissions, the formatted calendar, and utility functions
docs.text:
• lines 247–255: what the user is authorized to do on the page, in an associative array: is the user an administrator (ADMIN or DOCTOR)? a patient (and which one)? can this patient make a reservation (no upcoming appointments)?
  • Lines 260–285: The doctor’s schedule, converted into rows for the view. The privacy consideration is on line 278: a patient sees only the name associated with their own appointment. For the others, the property [patient] is set to [null], and the view displays “Reserved.” The name is not hidden by the view: it is never passed to the view, and therefore does not appear in the page’s source code, where it would be easy to read it. The “Book” button is displayed for an available time slot, on a day that has not yet passed, to an administrator or a patient who can make a reservation; the “Cancel” button is displayed only to administrators. The named arguments ([idCreneau: $creneau->getId()]) make the construction of an object with eight properties readable;
  • lines 291–296: the hidden fields of the POST forms. [[$idMedecin, $jour] = ...] (lines 171 and 225) breaks down the rendered array into two variables;
  • lines 300–307: the URL for a doctor’s schedule on a given day. [generateUrl('agenda', [...])] adds the values that are not path parameters to the end of URL as query parameters: [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-26];
  • lines 321–328: the message explaining to a patient why there is no “Book” button (they already have an upcoming appointment), unless that appointment is in the displayed calendar (immediately after booking it, the message would be moved). [array_any] ([PHP] 8.4): Does at least one element satisfy the condition?

docs.title: 11.19.4. src/Controller/PersonnesController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// =========================================================================
// src/Controller/PersonnesController.php: the management of doctors and that of
// clients (reserved for the ADMIN) are IDENTIQUES: same list, same form,
// same rules. Rather than writing the same actions twice, we write them once
// time in this class ABSTRAITE; MedecinsController and ClientsController
// inherit from it and specify only what distinguishes them: the section name
// (doctors or clients), the translation keys, and the methods for
// which ApplicationModel method to call.
//
// The #[Route] attributes of the actions are also inherited: the #[Route]
// from the child class CHAQUE gives them the start of their path (/doctors or
// /clients) and their name (medecins_ or clients_). This results in the following for each one:
//
//    GE T /doctor                  s                      list medecins_liste
//    GE T /doctors/add            empty fo          rm medecins_ajout
//    POST /doctors/add            cr                 eation medecins_ajout
//    GE T /doctors/{id}/edit      pre-filled form     medecins_modification
//    POST /doctors/{id}/edit      edit               medecins_modification
//    POST /doctors/{id}/delete     deletion                medecins_supprimer
//
// (and the same URL under /clients). The views are also shared:
// templates/people/liste.html.twig and people/formulaire.html.twig.
//
// SÉCURITÉ: the rule access_control ^/(doctors|clients) from
// config/packages/security.yaml reserves all of these URL for the ADMIN—including those
// that might be added later.
// =========================================================================

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Personne;
use App\Form\ChampsPersonneType;
use App\Form\PersonneType;
use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;
use App\Metier\MetierException;
use App\Vues\ClesPersonnes;
use App\Web\ApplicationModel;
use App\Web\Controleur;
use App\Web\Flash;
use App\Web\Message;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

abstract class PersonnesController extends Controleur
{
     // the form fields affected by each business "data entry" error (a
     // duplicate entry): these are highlighted in red, with the message at the bottom of the page
    public const CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER = [
        'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN' => ['login'],
        'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS' => ['prenom', 'nom'],
        'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS' => ['prenom', 'nom'],
    ];

    public function __construct(protected ApplicationModel $application, protected Flash $flash)
    {
    }

     // ---- what each type of person must provide

     // "doctors" or "clients": the beginning of the street names
    abstract protected function section(): string;

    abstract protected function cles(): ClesPersonnes;

     /** @return list<Person> */
    abstract protected function lister(): array;

    abstract protected function trouver(int $id): ?Personne;

    abstract protected function creer(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne;

    abstract protected function mettreAJour(int $id, DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne;

    abstract protected function effacer(int $id): void;

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors (or /clients)
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('', name: 'liste', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function liste(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('personnes/liste.html.twig', ['titrePage' => $this->cles()->titre,
            'cles' => $this->cles(), 'section' => $this->section(), 'personnes' => $this->lister()]);
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors/add: the empty form; POST: creation
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/ajouter', name: 'ajout', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function ajout(Request $request): Response
    {
        $formulaire = $this->createForm(PersonneType::class, ['titre' => 'Mr']);
        $formulaire->handleRequest($request);
        if ($formulaire->isSubmitted() && $formulaire->isValid()) {
            try {
                $personne = $this->creer(ChampsPersonneType::donnees($formulaire->getData()));
            } catch (MetierException $e) {
                return $this->erreurMetier($e, $formulaire, null);
            }
            $this->flash->succes($this->cles()->ajoute, self::parametres($personne));
            return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_liste');
        }
        return $this->page($formulaire, null);
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     // GET /doctors/{id}/edit: the pre-filled form; POST: the edit.
     // {id<\d+>} : a parameter consisting of digits (see example 02):
     // /doctors/abc/edit does not correspond to any route (404 page)
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/{id<\d+>}/modifier', name: 'modification', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function modification(Request $request, int $id): Response
    {
        $personne = $this->trouver($id) ?? throw $this->createNotFoundException();
         // the form, pre-filled with the person’s information (the
         // password is never displayed)
        $formulaire = $this->createForm(PersonneType::class, [
            'titre' => $personne->getTitre(), 'prenom' => $personne->getPrenom(),
            'nom' => $personne->getNom(), 'login' => $personne->getCompte()->getLogin(),
            'version' => $personne->getVersion(),
        ], ['creation' => false]);
        $formulaire->handleRequest($request);
        if ($formulaire->isSubmitted() && $formulaire->isValid()) {
            try {
                $personne = $this->mettreAJour($id, ChampsPersonneType::donnees($formulaire->getData()));
            } catch (MetierException $e) {
                return $this->erreurMetier($e, $formulaire, $personne);
            }
            $this->flash->succes($this->cles()->modifie, self::parametres($personne));
            return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_liste');
        }
        return $this->page($formulaire, $personne);
    }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     // POST /doctors/{id}/delete
     // (a confirmation prompt asking “Are you sure?” appears before the form is submitted;
     // see public/js/app.js)
    // -------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[Route('/{id<\d+>}/supprimer', name: 'supprimer', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function supprimer(Request $request, int $id): Response
    {
        $this->verifierCsrf($request);
        $personne = $this->trouver($id);
        try {
            $this->effacer($id);
            $this->flash->succes($this->cles()->supprime, self::parametres($personne));
        } catch (MetierException $e) {
            $this->flash->erreur($e->cle, $e->parametres);
        }
        return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_liste');
    }

     // ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

     // $personne null: creation form; otherwise: modification form.
     // A form was rejected (invalid input or business rule): code 422
    private function page(FormInterface $formulaire, ?Personne $personne, ?Message $erreur = null,
        array $champsInvalides = []): Response
    {
        $cles = $this->cles();
        $refuse = $erreur !== null || ($formulaire->isSubmitted() && ! $formulaire->isValid());
        return $this->render('personnes/formulaire.html.twig', [
            'titrePage' => $personne === null ? $cles->ajouter : $cles->modifier,
            'formulaire' => $formulaire,
            'erreur' => $erreur,
            'champsInvalides' => $champsInvalides,
            'urlListe' => $this->generateUrl($this->section().'_liste'),
        ], new Response(status: $refuse ? 422 : 200));
    }

     // A business rule rejected the write operation: the form is redisplayed, with
     // the user’s input (without the password), the business layer message
     // business layer (at the bottom of the page), and the relevant fields, if any, highlighted in
     // red so the user can immediately see what to correct
    private function erreurMetier(MetierException $e, FormInterface $formulaire, ?Personne $personne): Response
    {
        if (in_array($e->cle, ['ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND', 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND'], true)) {
             // which has since been deleted by another ADMIN: return to the list
            $this->flash->erreur($e->cle, $e->parametres);
            return $this->redirectToRoute($this->section().'_liste');
        }
        return $this->page($formulaire, $personne, new Message($e->cle, $e->parametres),
            self::CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER[$e->cle] ?? []);
    }

     // {name} and {login} for "added / modified / deleted" messages
    private static function parametres(?Personne $personne): array
    {
        return $personne === null ? ['nom' => '', 'login' => '']
            : ['nom' => "{$personne->getPrenom()} {$personne->getNom()}",
                'login' => $personne->getCompte()->getLogin()];
    }
}

The management of doctors and clients is identical: same list, same form, same rules. The actions are written once, in an abstract class; [MedecinsController] and [ClientsController] inherit from it. Each must provide what sets it apart: this is the role of the abstract methods in lines 64–77, declared without code; a child class that does not implement them would be rejected by [PHP]. This is the design pattern known as the “template method”: the parent class defines the algorithm, and the child classes provide the details.

The [#[Route]] attributes of the actions are also inherited. [Symfony] ignores the abstract class but examines the methods of each of the child classes, including inherited ones; the [#[Route]] attribute of the child class specifies the start of their path and name: the action [liste] becomes the routes [medecins_liste] ([/medecins]) and [clients_liste] ([/clients]). To add an action to the doctor management or client management modules, simply write it here.

  • Lines 51–55: the fields affected by each business-logic input error: a duplicate login affects the “login” field; a name match affects the “first name” and “last name” fields. These fields will be highlighted in red;
  • line 57: the constructor, inherited by the child classes. Its properties are [protected]: visible to the child classes;
  • Lines 82–87: the list. This view is common to both sections: it receives the translation keys for the section ([cles]) and its name ([section]), which is used to generate the road names ([section ~ '_ajout'] in the view);
  • Lines 92–107: Adding. A single action for GET (the empty form, with the title [Mr] selected) and POST (creation), as in Example 19. An invalid entry reloads the form. A valid entry proceeds to the business layer, which may reject the write operation (e.g., a namesake, a login already in use); otherwise, a success message appears and the user returns to the list (schema PRG);
  • lines 114–136: the update, for an existing person: [?? throw $this->createNotFoundException()] (the 404 page; [throw] is an expression that can be used to the right of [??]). [{id<\d+>}] (line 114) accepts only digits for the parameter [{id}] (example: 02). The form is pre-filled with the person’s values and their version; [handleRequest] replaces them with the entered data, resulting in POST;
  • lines 143–155: deletion. The form requested confirmation in the browser (example 21). The person’s information is retrieved before deletion to generate the success message (“Doctor Paul TATOU has been deleted.”);
  • lines 161–173: the form, either for creation ([$personne] equals [null]) or modification. A rejected form (invalid input or business rule violation) is returned with status code 422 (example 19). The view receives the form itself ([render] converts it into a “form view,” example 18);
  • lines 179–188: the business layer rejected the write operation. If a person has been deleted in the meantime (by another administrator), the user is returned to the list. Otherwise, the form is redisplayed directly (without redirection), as in the case of an input error: it already contains the user’s input. Added to this are the message from the business layer (displayed at the bottom of the page, in the error area) and the fields to be highlighted in red. Note that the entity manager is closed after the exception (the business layer, as mentioned above): the action now only displays;
  • lines 191–196: the parameters [{nom}] and [{login}] for the success messages.

<?php
// src/Controller/MedecinsController.php: doctor management (role ADMIN
// only). All actions are written by PersonnesController: there is

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Entity\Personne;
use App\Metier\DonneesPersonne;

use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

// the start of the path and the name of all routes inherited from PersonnesController
#[Route('/medecins', name: 'medecins_')]
class MedecinsController extends PersonnesController
{
    protected function section(): string
    {
        return 'medecins';
    }

     // MEDECINS.TITLE, MEDECINS.ADD... (see translations)
    protected function cles(): ClesPersonnes
    {
        return ClesPersonnes::de('MEDECINS');
    }

    protected function lister(): array
    {
        return $this->application->getAllMedecins();
    }

    protected function trouver(int $id): ?Personne
    {
        return $this->application->getMedecinById($id);
    }

    protected function creer(DonneesPersonne $donnees): Personne
    {

    {
