├── templates/
│   ├── calcul/
│   │   └── resultat.html.twig
│   ├── erreur.html.twig
│   └── layout.html.twig
└── ...

The application has only one action, which calculates the square of an integer: [/carre/7]. Depending on URL, it either succeeds or fails in various ways. Messages are written to the server console by the [error_log] function in [PHP], which the development server ([php -S]) displays.

docs.title: 7.1.1. Before and after everything else: src/EventListener/Journal.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/EventListener/Journal.php: a listener for DEUX events. It sees
// every request from AVANT to the rest of the application (including routing), and the response
// APRÈS everything else

namespace App\EventListener;

use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\RequestEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ResponseEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;

class Journal
{
     // priority 100: before Symfony routing (priority 32)
     #[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::REQUEST, priority: 100)]
    public function avant(RequestEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $requete = $evenement->getRequest();
         // error_log: a message in the development server console
        error_log('--- '.$requete->getMethod().' '.$requete->getRequestUri());
        error_log('1. Journal, kernel.request (avant le routage)');
    }

     // priority -100: after the other listeners for kernel.response
     #[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::RESPONSE, priority: -100)]
    public function apres(ResponseEvent $evenement): void
    {
        error_log('7. Journal, kernel.response (code '.$evenement->getResponse()->getStatusCode().')');
    }
}

A single class can listen for multiple events: the [#[AsEventListener]] attribute is then applied to each of the relevant methods.

  • lines 16–23: message #1, with the request ([getRequestUri()]: the path and parameters). Priority 100 places the listener before routing: nothing has happened yet in [Symfony];
  • Lines 26–30: Message No. 7, once everything else has been completed. A priority of -100 places the listener after those of the application and [Symfony] (most of which have a priority between -10 and 10). [getStatusCode()] is the response code.

Such a listener does not know the chosen route, since routing has not yet taken place. It is used for processing that applies to all requests: logging, handling a proxy (the case study mentions this in relation to the clients’ IP address)...

docs.title: 7.1.2. After routing: src/EventListener/Bloquer.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/EventListener/Bloquer.php: a listener for kernel.request, executed on APRÈS on
// routing: it knows the selected route

namespace App\EventListener;

use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\RequestEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\AccessDeniedHttpException;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;

// priority 0 (default): after routing (priority 32)
#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::REQUEST)]
class Bloquer
{
    public function __invoke(RequestEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $requete = $evenement->getRequest();
         // the _route attribute of the request: the name of the route selected by the routing process
        error_log('2. Bloquer, kernel.request (route : '.$requete->attributes->get('_route').')');
        if ($requete->query->has('bloquer')) {
             // an exception: the next step (Chrono, the action) is not executed
            throw new AccessDeniedHttpException('accès bloqué');
        }
    }
}
  • line 13: the default priority, 0: the listener is called after routing;
  • line 20: message #2. Routing has stored the name of the selected route in the [_route] attribute of the request (and its parameters in the attributes of the same name, example 12);
  • Lines 21–24: The [?bloquer] parameter of URL ([has] checks for its presence) causes a 403 error (Forbidden, access denied): the [AccessDeniedHttpException] exception terminates processing.

docs.title: 7.1.3. Before the action: src/EventListener/Chronometre.php and Chrono.php
docs.text:
We want to time only certain actions—those that require it. All we need to do is mark them with a custom attribute, [PHP]:

<?php
// src/EventListener/Chronometre.php: a ATTRIBUT PHP of our own design, to be placed
// on the actions whose duration we want to measure (see the Chrono earpiece)

namespace App\EventListener;

use Attribute;

// #[Attribute]: this class is an attribute; TARGET_METHOD: it is applied to a method
#[Attribute(Attribute::TARGET_METHOD)]
class Chronometre
{
}

An attribute is an ordinary class, itself marked with the attribute [#[Attribute]]; [Attribute::TARGET_METHOD] indicates that it is applied to a method. This attribute carries no information: its mere presence is what matters.

<?php
// src/EventListener/Chrono.php: a listener for three events, which only acts
// for actions marked with the #[Chronometre] attribute: AVANT the action, APRÈS
// it, and finally APRÈS sending the response (kernel.terminate)

namespace App\EventListener;

use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ControllerEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ResponseEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\TerminateEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;

class Chrono
{
     // kernel.controller: the action has been selected, but it has not yet been called
     #[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::CONTROLLER)]
    public function avant(ControllerEvent $evenement): void
    {
         // getAttributes: the attributes PHP of a given class, carried by the action
        if ($evenement->getAttributes(Chronometre::class) === []) {
            return;
        }
        error_log('3. Chrono, kernel.controller (avant l\'action)');
         // the start time (hrtime: a precise clock, in nanoseconds), stored
         // in the query attributes (query scope; see Example 12)
        $evenement->getRequest()->attributes->set('debut', hrtime(true));
    }

     #[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::RESPONSE)]
    public function apres(ResponseEvent $evenement): void
    {
        if ($evenement->getRequest()->attributes->has('debut')) {
            error_log('6. Chrono, kernel.response (code '.$evenement->getResponse()->getStatusCode().')');
        }
    }

     // kernel.terminate: at the very end, APRÈS sends the response to the browser;
     // the response can no longer be changed
     #[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::TERMINATE)]
    public function fin(TerminateEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $debut = $evenement->getRequest()->attributes->get('debut');
         // The measurement has not started if the action has not been completed
        if ($debut !== null) {
            $ms = round((hrtime(true) - $debut) / 1e6);
            error_log("8. Chrono, kernel.terminate (fin, $ms ms)");
        }
    }
}
  • Lines 17–28: the [kernel.controller] event. The event’s [getAttributes] method returns the [PHP] attributes of a given class carried by the action (and by its class): an empty list means the action is not marked, and the listener does nothing. Otherwise, message #3, and the start time, stored in the request attributes (example 12). [hrtime(true)] is a precise clock, in nanoseconds, designed to measure durations;
  • lines 30–36: message #6, regarding [kernel.response], with the response code, if the measurement has started. The default priority, 0, places this listener before that of [Journal] (-100);
  • lines 40–49: the [kernel.terminate] event, published after the response is sent: message #8, containing the elapsed time since message #3. The check on line 45 verifies that the measurement has started: the event is published for all requests, even those that did not reach the action.

This is how [Symfony] itself implements some of its attributes: [#[IsGranted]], which we will discuss in the next chapter, is read by a listener of [kernel.controller_arguments], which denies access to the action if the user does not have the requested permission.

docs.title: 7.1.4. The action’s arguments: src/Liaison/EntierResolver.php and the controller
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Liaison/EntierResolver.php: an argument resolver (see Example 12): the
// route parameter converted to an integer, or to null if it is not a number
// integer (in which case the action decides)

namespace App\Liaison;

use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Controller\ValueResolverInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\ControllerMetadata\ArgumentMetadata;

class EntierResolver implements ValueResolverInterface
{
    public function resolve(Request $request, ArgumentMetadata $argument): iterable
    {
        $valeur = $request->attributes->get($argument->getName());
        error_log("4. EntierResolver, les arguments de l'action (valeur reçue : \"$valeur\")");
        $n = filter_var($valeur, FILTER_VALIDATE_INT);
        return [$n === false ? null : $n];
    }
}

An argument resolver (Example 12), which writes message #4. It accepts any text and converts it to an integer, or to [null] if it is not one ([filter_var] returns [false]): unlike a constraint such as [requirements] (Example 02), which would return a 404 page for [/carre/abc]; here, the action will determine the outcome.

<?php
// src/Controller/CalculController.php: a timed action

namespace App\Controller;

use App\EventListener\Chronometre;
use App\Liaison\EntierResolver;
use DomainException;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Attribute\ValueResolver;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\BadRequestHttpException;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class CalculController extends AbstractController
{
     // $n: the route parameter {n}, provided by our resolver EntierResolver;
     // #[Chronometre]: the Chrono listener measures the duration of this action
     #[Route('/carre/{n}', name: 'carre', methods: ['GET'])]
     #[Chronometre]
    public function carre(#[ValueResolver(EntierResolver::class)] ?int $n): Response
    {
        error_log("5. action carre($n)");
        if ($n === null) {
            throw new BadRequestHttpException('pas un entier');    // Error 400: see PageErreur
        }
        if ($n === 13) {
            throw new DomainException('13 porte malheur');    // an “unexpected” error
        }
        return $this->render('calcul/resultat.html.twig', ['n' => $n, 'carre' => $n * $n]);
    }
}
  • line 20: the action is marked with our attribute [#[Chronometre]];
  • line 21: the parameter [$n] is provided by our resolver (attribute [#[ValueResolver]], example 12);
  • lines 24–26: a parameter that is not an integer: error 400 (Bad Request), caused by the exception [BadRequestHttpException];
  • lines 27–29: the number 13 causes an “unexpected” error. [DomainException] is an exception class from the standard library of [PHP];
  • line 30: the normal case. The [calcul/resultat.html.twig] view simply displays the result.

docs.title: 7.1.5. Error handling: src/EventListener/PageErreur.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/EventListener/PageErreur.php: a listener for kernel.exception, which replaces
// Symfony’s error pages with ours

namespace App\EventListener;

use DomainException;
use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\ExceptionEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;
use Twig\Environment;

// priority -10: after the Symfony listener that logs the exception (0),
// before the one that generates its error page (-128)
#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::EXCEPTION, priority: -10)]
class PageErreur
{
     // Environment: the Twig engine itself, to generate a page outside of a controller
    public function __construct(private Environment $twig)
    {
    }

    public function __invoke(ExceptionEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $e = $evenement->getThrowable();
        if ($e instanceof HttpExceptionInterface) {
             // Errors HTTP (403, unknown page -> 404...): HttpExceptionInterface
             // is the interface for all HTTP exceptions; they carry their own code
            error_log("x. PageErreur, kernel.exception (HTTP {$e->getStatusCode()})");
            $code = $e->getStatusCode();
        } elseif ($e instanceof DomainException) {
             // an "unexpected" exception of a given type: DomainException and its subclasses
            error_log("x. PageErreur, kernel.exception (DomainException : {$e->getMessage()})");
            $code = 500;
        } else {
            return;    // all others: the Symfony error page
        }
         // the event’s response replaces the exception (subsequent listeners are
         // called); it will then pass through kernel.response, like a regular response
        $evenement->setResponse(new Response(
            $this->twig->render('erreur.html.twig', ['code' => $code]), $code));
    }
}
  • lines 15–17: the listener for [kernel.exception], with priority -10. [Symfony] registers two listeners for this event: the first, with priority 0, logs the exception; the second, with priority -128, generates the error page from [Symfony]. Ours falls between the two: the exception is logged, then we display the page;
  • line 21: the listener is not a controller and does not have the [render] method from [AbstractController]: it receives the [Twig] engine itself (the [Twig\Environment] class), whose [render] method returns the rendered page as a string;
  • lines 28–32: all HTTP errors: a URL with no route (404), a method denied (405), and the exceptions [AccessDeniedHttpException] (403) and [BadRequestHttpException] (400)... implement the [HttpExceptionInterface] interface and carry their code ([getStatusCode()]). This single test therefore replaces all [Symfony] error pages with ours;
  • lines 33–36: an exception of class [DomainException] (or its subclasses; see Example 08): an “unexpected” error, converted into a “custom” error page, with status code 500 (Internal Server Error). The exception message is displayed in the console, but not on the page: it may contain internal details that are not relevant to the user;
  • lines 37–39: the other exceptions are handled by [Symfony];
  • lines 42–43: [setResponse] provides the response, which replaces the exception and stops the event from propagating: subsequent listeners (the error page for [Symfony]) are not called.

The error page receives the error code and displays an appropriate message:

{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{# the error page; its template: the error code #}

{% block contenu %}
  <div class="alert alert-danger">
    <h1 class="h4">Erreur {{ code }}</h1>
    {# an associative array, indexed by the code; ??: the default value #}
    <p class="mb-0">{{ {400: 'Requête incorrecte.', 403: 'Accès refusé.', 404: 'Page introuvable.'}[code] ?? 'Erreur interne du serveur.' }}</p>
  </div>
{% endblock %}
  • Line 8: an associative array defined in the view ([{clé: valeur, ...}]), from which the element with index [code] is retrieved; the operator [??] provides a default value when this element does not exist.

There is another, even simpler way to replace error pages without writing a listener: a view named [templates/bundles/TwigBundle/Exception/error404.html.twig] replaces the 404 error page, and similarly for each code ([error.html.twig] for all others). These views are only used in production; debug mode retains its detailed pages (you can preview them in debug mode at [/_error/404], provided you have imported the routes [@FrameworkBundle/Resources/config/routing/errors.php]). A listener, on the other hand, allows for any type of handling (a response at JSON, a redirect, etc.) in all modes.

docs.title: 7.1.6. Execution
docs.text:
Normal case, [/carre/7]:

The server console displays the eight steps in order (the dates that [php -S] places at the beginning of the lines have been removed):

--- GET /carre/7
1. Journal, kernel.request (avant le routage)
[info] Matched route "carre".
2. Bloquer, kernel.request (route : carre)
3. Chrono, kernel.controller (avant l'action)
4. EntierResolver, les arguments de l'action (valeur reçue : "7")
5. action carre(7)
6. Chrono, kernel.response (code 200)
7. Journal, kernel.response (code 200)
8. Chrono, kernel.terminate (fin, 2 ms)
127.0.0.1:51612 [200]: GET /carre/7

The line [[info]] comes from the routing of [Symfony]: this is its log (log). Without a logging library (the most commonly used is [Monolog], installed by [composer require logger]), [Symfony] uses a minimal log, which writes to the console. The last line is the development server log, written once the request is complete. A blocked access, [/carre/7?bloquer]:

--- GET /carre/7?bloquer
1. Journal, kernel.request (avant le routage)
[info] Matched route "carre".
2. Bloquer, kernel.request (route : carre)
[error] Uncaught PHP Exception Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\AccessDeniedHttpException: "accès bloqué" at Bloquer.php line 23
x. PageErreur, kernel.exception (HTTP 403)
7. Journal, kernel.response (code 403)

The listener [Bloquer] raised an exception: the action was not selected, its arguments were not calculated, and it was not called. The exception was logged by [Symfony], then converted into a response by our listener; this response passed through [kernel.response]. The event [kernel.terminate] was published, but [Chrono] did not display anything, as the measurement had not started. A parameter that is not an integer, [/carre/abc]:

--- GET /carre/abc
1. Journal, kernel.request (avant le routage)
[info] Matched route "carre".
2. Bloquer, kernel.request (route : carre)
3. Chrono, kernel.controller (avant l'action)
4. EntierResolver, les arguments de l'action (valeur reçue : "abc")
5. action carre()
[error] Uncaught PHP Exception Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\BadRequestHttpException: "pas un entier" at CalculController.php line 25
x. PageErreur, kernel.exception (HTTP 400)
6. Chrono, kernel.response (code 400)
7. Journal, kernel.response (code 400)
8. Chrono, kernel.terminate (fin, 1 ms)

This time, the action was called with [null] (which is rendered as an empty string: [carre()]), and it was this action that raised error 400. An “unexpected” error, [/carre/13]:

--- GET /carre/13
1. Journal, kernel.request (avant le routage)
[info] Matched route "carre".
2. Bloquer, kernel.request (route : carre)
3. Chrono, kernel.controller (avant l'action)
4. EntierResolver, les arguments de l'action (valeur reçue : "13")
5. action carre(13)
[critical] Uncaught PHP Exception DomainException: "13 porte malheur" at CalculController.php line 28
x. PageErreur, kernel.exception (DomainException : 13 porte malheur)
6. Chrono, kernel.response (code 500)
7. Journal, kernel.response (code 500)
8. Chrono, kernel.terminate (fin, 1 ms)

The exception was handled by our listener: the user sees the “custom” error page, not the detailed page, even though debug mode is active. It was still logged, with the level [critical] (an error HTTP is simply a [error]): Like [Laravel], [Symfony] distinguishes between logging an exception in the log and the response it generates. Finally, a URL that does not correspond to any route, [/inconnu]:

--- GET /inconnu
1. Journal, kernel.request (avant le routage)
[error] Uncaught PHP Exception Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\NotFoundHttpException: "No route found for "GET http://localhost:8000/unknown"" at RouterListener.php line 156
x. PageErreur, kernel.exception (HTTP 404)
7. Journal, kernel.response (code 404)

Routing failed: no listener after it, no action. The 404 page is ours:

curl http://localhost:8000/unknown

...
      <div class="alert alert-danger">
    <h1 class="h4">Erreur 404</h1>
        <p class="mb-0">Page introuvable.</p>
  </div>
...

Let’s focus on the essentials. Kernel event listeners are the right place for checks common to many actions (is the user logged in? Do they have permission to access this action?): they form the basis of the security component in [Symfony], which the next chapter uses for authentication. The event listeners for [kernel.exception] and the error views ensure that the user never sees a technical page, regardless of the error: the case study takes advantage of this.

docs.title: 4. The View and Its Model
docs.text:
Up to this point, actions generated their own responses: text, JSON, and a few HTML tags written as a string. In a MVC application, this is the role of a view: a file that describes the page HTML, with placesholders for the data passed to it by the action—the view’s model.

[Symfony] uses the [Twig] view engine, created by the same team. A [Twig] view is a file whose name ends with [.html.twig] (the output format, followed by the engine), stored in the application’s [templates] folder. It is a text file—in this case, HTML—in which three types of tags are interpreted on the server:

  • [{{ expression }}]: the value of an expression, inserted into the page;
  • [{% instruction %}]: an instruction (tag); a condition ([{% if %}]); loop ([{% for %}]), template inheritance ([{% extends %}], [{% block %}]), inclusion ([{% include %}])...;
  • [{# commentaire #}]: a comment, which does not appear on the generated page.

Everything else is copied as-is. The expressions are not written in [PHP], but in the language of [Twig], which is simpler and safer: [modele.titre] refers to the property [titre] of the object [modele] (or its method [getTitre()], or the key [titre] of an array: [Twig] looks it up itself); filters transform a value ([nom|upper] capitalizes a name); functions perform calculations ([path('accueil')] generates a URL). [Twig] thus resembles [Jinja2] ([Flask]), from which it drew inspiration, or the engine of [Django]; it differs from [Blade] ([Laravel]) and [Razor] ([ASP.NET Core]), which combine HTML with host language code. A [Twig] view cannot execute arbitrary [PHP] code: it can only display the data provided to it. This is by design: the application logic remains within the classes. A view is not interpreted with every request: when it is first used, [Twig] compiles it into a [PHP] class, stored in the [var/cache/dev/twig] folder, which it then reuses as long as the view remains unchanged. We’ll see what this file looks like.

docs.title: 4.1. Example 13: A First View
docs.text:

├── config/
│   ├── packages/

docs.title: 4.1.1. The configuration: config/bundles.php and config/packages/twig.yaml
docs.text:
[Twig] is integrated into [Symfony] via a bundle, TwigBundle, which must be added to the application’s bundle list (Example 01):

<?php
// config/bundles.php: the application's bundles; TwigBundle includes the
// the Twig view engine
return [
    Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\FrameworkBundle::class => ['all' => true],
    Symfony\Bundle\TwigBundle\TwigBundle::class => ['all' => true],
];

and configure:

# config/packages/twig.yaml: the configuration for TwigBundle
twig:
     # the views directory
    default_path: '%kernel.project_dir%/templates'

The only key specifies the views folder: [templates], located in the project folder. This is also the default value. In a standard project, these two files are created by [Symfony Flex] when you install [Twig] ([composer require twig], see introduction).

docs.title: 4.1.2. The view template: src/Modele/PageModele.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Model/PageModele.php: the view model, the data that the action passes to the view

namespace App\Modele;

readonly class PageModele
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $titre,
        public string $message,
        public string $heure,
    ) {
    }
}

The view model is a simple immutable class (see Example 03): the three pieces of information that the view will display. There is no requirement to define a view’s model as a class: three separate variables could be passed to the view. However, a class documents what the view expects and allows the editor to verify the action’s code. This is the approach the case study will follow, where each important view has its own model class.

docs.title: 4.1.3. The controller: src/Controller/VuesController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/VuesController.php: actions that return a VUE

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Modele\PageModele;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route(methods: ['GET'])]
class VuesController extends AbstractController
{
     // render: the Twig engine generates the page from the view
     // templates/views/index.html.twig and the variables passed in the array (here
     // just one, [modele]); the generated page is the body of the response
     #[Route('/', name: 'index')]
    public function index(): Response
    {
        $modele = new PageModele(
            'Ma première vue',
            'Cette page a été fabriquée par Twig, sur le serveur.',
            date('H:i:s'));
        return $this->render('vues/index.html.twig', ['modele' => $modele]);
    }

     // the same view with a different template; or a different view, with a 404 error
     #[Route('/bonjour/{nom}', name: 'bonjour')]
    public function bonjour(string $nom): Response
    {
        if ($nom === 'inconnu') {
             // the third parameter of `render`: the response to be populated, here with the code 404
            return $this->render('vues/inconnu.html.twig', ['nom' => $nom],
                new Response(status: Response::HTTP_NOT_FOUND));
        }
        $modele = new PageModele(
            "Bonjour $nom",
            "Cette fois, le titre de la page vient de l'URL.",
            date('H:i:s'));
        return $this->render('vues/index.html.twig', ['modele' => $modele]);
    }
}
  • Lines 20–23: The action builds the view template. The function [date], derived from [PHP], formats the current time: [H] formats the hours, [i] formats the minutes, and [s] formats the seconds;
  • Line 24: The [render] method of [AbstractController] instructs [Twig] to generate the page. The first parameter is the name of the view: the file path, relative to the [templates] folder. The second parameter is an associative array, where each key becomes a variable in the view—in this case, a single one: [modele]. [render] returns an object [Response], whose body is the generated page (of type [text/html]);
  • lines 31–35: another view, with another variable ([nom]). The third parameter of [render] is a response to be populated: in this case, a 404 response for a custom error page. [new Response(status: ...)] passes the code via a named parameter, while the other parameters retain their default values;
  • Lines 36–40: the same view as the [index] action, but with a different template. This is the benefit of separating actions from views: a single view can be used by multiple actions.

docs.title: 4.1.4. The view: templates/views/index.html.twig
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  {# {{ ... }}: the value of an expression, inserted into the page #}
  <title>{{ modele.titre }}</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>{{ modele.titre }}</h1>
  <p>{{ modele.message }}</p>
  <p>Page fabriquée à {{ modele.heure }}.</p>
</body>
</html>
  • line 5: a comment [Twig];
  • line 6: [{{ modele.titre }}] inserts the value of the [titre] property of the [modele] variable. The period is the access operator for [Twig], where [PHP] writes [$modele->titre].

Everything inserted by [{{ }}] is escaped: the characters [<], [>], [&], ["], and ['] are replaced by their entities HTML. This is the role that function [htmlspecialchars] played in Example 09, but this time it is automatic: a view therefore cannot inadvertently insert the HTML provided by a user into the page.

docs.title: 4.1.5. The view: templates/views/inconnu.html.twig
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Inconnu</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Personne ne s'appelle [{{ nom }}] ici.</h1>
</body>
</html>

A view is not required to receive an object: the variable [nom] is a string.

docs.title: 4.1.6. Execution
docs.text:
The displayed time corresponds to the time zone configured in [PHP] (the [date.timezone] directive in the [php.ini] file), which is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) in this case; the case study will show how to set it for the application. The raw response shows the work done by [Twig]: the [{{ }}] tags have been replaced with their values, and the comment has been removed.

curl -i http://localhost:8000/

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
    <title>Ma première vue</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Ma première vue</h1>
  <p>Cette page a été fabriquée par Twig, sur le serveur.</p>
  <p>Page fabriquée à 09:31:47.</p>
</body>
</html>

The “home” error page, followed by a name containing HTML ([<b>martin], encoded in URL):

curl -i http://localhost:8000/hello/unknown
curl http://localhost:8000/hello/%3Cb%3Emartin

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Inconnu</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Personne ne s'appelle [inconnu] ici.</h1>
</body>
</html>
...
    <title>Bonjour <b>martin</title>
...
  <h1>Bonjour <b>martin</h1>
  <p>Cette fois, le titre de la page vient de l'URL.</p>
...

The tag [<b>] was escaped, even though neither the action nor the view had anything to do with it (the apostrophe was also escaped: [']). Here, finally, is the view compiled by [Twig], as found in the [var/cache/dev/twig] folder (under a generated name, such as [9e/9e42179990bdaebfeb73b2435744b0e7.php]), stripped down to the essentials:

/* views/index.html.twig */
class __TwigTemplate_aa4414ddec1d8b74a5b0f81e8faede95 extends Template
{
    ...
    protected function doDisplay(array $context, array $blocks = []): iterable
    {
         // line 1
        yield "<!doctype html>
<html lang=\"fr\">
<head>
  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">
  ";
         // line 6
        yield "  <title>";
        yield (string) $this->escaper->escape(CoreExtension::getAttribute($this->env, $this->source,
            ... $context["modele"] ..., "titre", ...), "html", null, true);
        yield "</title>
...

The view has become a class named [PHP], whose method [doDisplay] generates the page piece by piece ([yield]). Each [{{ modele.titre }}] has become a call to [CoreExtension::getAttribute] (which looks up the property, method, or key [titre]), passed to the method [escape] (escaping). A [Twig] view is therefore simply a safer and more readable way to write a [PHP] file that generates HTML.

docs.title: 4.2. Example 14: The Twig Language
docs.text: This example combines the main constructs of [Twig] into a single view.

docs.title: 4.2.1. The Template and the Action
docs.text:
The view’s template is defined by three immutable classes, each in its own file ([PHP] does not require one class per file, but the class loader in [Composer] looks for the class [App\Modele\Produit] in the file [src/Modele/Produit.php]):

<?php
// src/Template/Produit.php: a product

namespace App\Modele;

readonly class Produit
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $nom,
        public float $prix,
        public bool $enStock,
    ) {
    }
}

<?php
// src/Template/Adresse.php: an address

namespace App\Modele;

readonly class Adresse
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $rue,
        public string $ville,
    ) {
    }
}

<?php
// src/Template/BasesModele.php: the view template for Example 14

namespace App\Modele;

readonly class BasesModele
{
    /**
     * @param list<Produit> $produits
     * @param list<Produit> $panier
     */
    public function __construct(
        public string $titre,
        public string $nom,
        public ?string $surnom,
        public string $html,
        public bool $connecte,
        public string $devise,
        public array $produits,
        public array $panier,
        public Adresse $adresse,
    ) {
    }
}

The model contains values of various types: strings, [null], Booleans, arrays of objects, empty arrays, and objects containing other objects. The prices here are of type [float], to simplify calculations in the view (Example 06 showed why we prefer whole cents).

<?php
// src/Controller/BasesController.php: a view that uses the main Twig constructs

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Modele\Adresse;
use App\Modele\BasesModele;
use App\Modele\Produit;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class BasesController extends AbstractController
{
     #[Route('/', name: 'index', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function index(): Response
    {
        $modele = new BasesModele(
            titre: 'Les bases de Twig',
            nom: 'Martin',
            surnom: null,
            html: '<b>ceci est du HTML</b>',
            connecte: true,
            devise: '€',
            produits: [
                new Produit('Clavier', 25, true),
                new Produit('Souris', 12.5, false),
                new Produit('Écran', 149, true),
            ],
            panier: [],
            adresse: new Adresse('12 rue des Lilas', 'Angers'));
        return $this->render('bases/index.html.twig', ['modele' => $modele]);
    }
}

The action builds the model using named parameters (see Example 02): each value is preceded by the name of the parameter it is intended for, which makes the call readable despite the number of parameters.

docs.title: 4.2.2. The view: templates/bases/index.html.twig
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>{{ modele.titre }}</title>
</head>
<body>
  {# set: a view variable; the `reduce` filter sums the prices, and the `length` filter counts the products #}
  {% set total = modele.produits|reduce((somme, p) => somme + p.prix, 0) %}
  {% set nombre = modele.produits|length %}
  <h1>{{ modele.titre }}</h1>
  {# 1. Display a value from the model; `null` is displayed as an empty string;
     le filtre default remplace une valeur vide. Ce commentaire Twig n'apparaît
     pas dans la page produite #}
  <p>1. Nom : {{ modele.nom }} - surnom : [{{ modele.surnom }}] [{{ modele.surnom|default('aucun') }}]</p>
  {# 2. {{ }} escapes the HTML; the raw filter inserts it as-is #}
  <p>2a. {{ modele.html }}</p>
  <p>2b. {{ modele.html|raw }}</p>
  {# 3. a condition #}
  {% if modele.connecte %}
    <p>3. Vous êtes connecté.</p>
  {% else %}
    <p>3. Vous n'êtes pas connecté.</p>
  {% endif %}
  {# 4. a loop: the loop variable describes the state of the loop #}
  <p>4. Nos produits :</p>
  <ul>
    {% for produit in modele.produits %}
      <li>n° {{ loop.index0 }} : {{ produit.nom }}, {{ produit.prix }} {{ modele.devise }}
        {{ produit.enStock ? '(en stock)' : '(épuisé)' }}
        {% if loop.first %} - le premier{% endif %}
        {% if loop.last %} - le dernier, vu par {{ modele.nom }}{% endif %}
      </li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>
  {# 5. the empty list: the else block of a for loop #}
  <p>5. Votre panier :
    {% for p in modele.panier %}<span>{{ p.nom }}</span>{% else %} il est vide.{% endfor %}
  </p>
  {# 6. calculated expressions, set variables, and the number_format filter #}
  <p>6. {{ nombre }} produits, pour un total de {{ total }} {{ modele.devise }} ;
    prix moyen : {{ (total / nombre)|number_format(2, ',', ' ') }} {{ modele.devise }}</p>
  {# 7. An object within an object, and a filter that capitalizes text #}
  <p>7. Adresse : {{ modele.adresse.rue }}, {{ modele.adresse.ville|upper }}</p>
  {# 8. verbatim: text that Twig outputs as-is without interpreting it #}
  <p>8. Des accolades affichées telles quelles : {% verbatim %}{{ modele.nom }}{% endverbatim %}</p>
</body>
</html>
  • Lines 9–10: The [{% set %}] statement creates a variable in the view. The total price is calculated by the filter [reduce], which reduces an array to a single value (like [array_reduce], example 06): its function receives the accumulated value and the current element; [(somme, p) => somme + p.prix] is an arrow function of [Twig]. The filter [length] returns the number of elements in an array (or characters in a string). These calculations should be reserved for presentation purposes: the calculation normally belongs to the action;
  • line 15: a [null] value is displayed as an empty string. The [default] filter replaces an empty (or missing) value with a default value;
  • lines 17–18: [{{ }}] escapes HTML (2a); the filter [raw], on the other hand, inserts the value as-is, without escaping it (2b). [raw] is reserved for HTML generated by the application itself, never for user input;
  • Lines 20–24: a condition: [{% if %}], [{% elseif %}], [{% else %}], [{% endif %}]. Each block is closed by a [{% end... %}] statement;
  • Lines 28–34: a loop [{% for ... in ... %}] ... [{% endfor %}]. Within the loop, the special variable [loop] describes the loop’s state: [loop.index0] (the iteration number, starting at 0), [loop.index] (starting at 1), [loop.first], [loop.last] (true on the first and last iterations), [loop.length] (the number of elements). Variables outside the loop ([modele.nom]) remain accessible;
  • line 30: the ternary operator [condition ? a : b] ([Twig] also accepts [condition ? a], which returns an empty string if the condition is false);
  • line 38: a loop [for] can have a block [{% else %}], which is executed if the list is empty. This is simpler than a [{% if %}] that would check the length of the list;
  • lines 41–42: calculated expressions ([total / nombre]) and the variables from [set]. The filter [number_format] formats a number: two decimal places, a comma as the decimal separator, and a space as the thousands separator. In Example 16, we’ll see a much better way to format numbers and amounts;
  • line 44: the period passes through objects ([modele.adresse.ville]), and the filter [upper] capitalizes a string (while correctly handling accented characters);
  • line 46: the [{% verbatim %}] instruction copies its content without interpreting it: this is useful when a page contains curly braces intended for a [JavaScript] framework.

[Twig] has about fifty filters ([lower], [capitalize], [trim], [join], [split], [slice], [sort], [date], [json_encode], [escape]...), about fifteen functions ([range], [min], [max], [random]...) and tests ([is defined], [is empty], [is null], [is iterable], [is even]...); the bundles for [Symfony] add some ([path], [asset], [form_row], [is_granted]...), and the application can write its own (Example 16).

docs.text:
The generated page:

<html lang="fr">
<head>

  <title>Les bases de Twig</title>
</head>
<body>
        <h1>Les bases de Twig</h1>
    <p>1. Nom : Martin - surnom : [] [aucun]</p>
    <p>2a. <b>ceci est du HTML</b></p>
  <p>2b. <b>ceci est du HTML</b></p>
        <p>3. Vous êtes connecté.</p>
      <p>4. Nos produits :</p>
  <ul>
          <li>n° 0 : Clavier, 25 €
        (en stock)
         - le premier              </li>
          <li>n° 1 : Souris, 12.5 €
        (épuisé)
                      </li>
          <li>n° 2 : Écran, 149 €
        (en stock)
                 - le dernier, vu par Martin      </li>
      </ul>
    <p>5. Votre panier :
     il est vide.  </p>
    <p>6. 3 produits, pour un total de 186.5 € ;
    prix moyen : 62,17 €</p>
    <p>7. Adresse : 12 rue des Lilas, ANGERS</p>
    <p>8. Des accolades affichées telles quelles : {{ modele.nom }}</p>

The comments and instructions have disappeared, but they leave behind their spaces: [Twig] removes the line break that follows a tag, but not the indentation that precedes it. This has no effect: the browser ignores these spaces. (A hyphen inside a tag—such as [{%- ... -%}] or [{{- ... -}}]—would remove the whitespace surrounding it.) A number [float] inserted into the page is written with a decimal point ([12.5]); [number_format] uses the French comma.

docs.title: 4.3. Example 15: Templates, fragments, static files
docs.text:
The pages of a website usually share the same structure: a header, a navigation bar, a footer, and the same style sheets. Rather than repeating this structure in every view, it is written once in a template (layout), which the pages extend. This example also uses [Bootstrap], the most widely used CSS framework, for the layout.

15-gabarit/
├── config/
│   ├── packages/
│   │   └── twig.yaml
│   └── services.yaml
├── public/
│   └── css/
│       └── styles.css
├── src/
│   ├── Controller/
│   │   └── PagesController.php
│   ├── Modele/
│   │   └── Membre.php
│   └── Kernel.php
├── templates/
│   ├── fragments/
│   │   └── navbar.html.twig
│   ├── layout.html.twig
│   ├── macros.html.twig
│   └── pages/
│       ├── accueil.html.twig
│       ├── brute.html.twig
│       └── equipe.html.twig
└── ...

docs.title: 4.3.1. Static Files
docs.text:
A HTML page references other files: style sheets, [JavaScript] scripts, and images. These files, which the server sends as-is, are called static files. With [Symfony], they are stored in the [public] folder, which the web server serves as-is (example 01): The file [public/css/styles.css] is available at URL [/css/styles.css], without [Symfony] being involved.

/* a few additional Bootstrap settings */
body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

/* the template's footer */
.pied {
  margin-top: 2rem;
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  color: #6c757d;
}

/* error messages at the bottom of the page on a light pink background */
.zone-erreur {
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef;
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

A few additional CSS rules in addition to [Bootstrap]: a light gray background, the footer style, and the style for an error area that will be used in the following examples.

[Bootstrap] is used in examples 15 through 28. Rather than placing a copy in each user’s [public] folder, the examples share it: it is located in the [exemples/commun/bootstrap] folder. This folder is not served by the web server: a controller, shared by all these examples, serves its files. This is the file [exemples/commun/BootstrapController.php]:

<?php
// common/BootstrapController.php: a controller that serves the Bootstrap files,
// shared by examples 15 through 28 (the examples/common/bootstrap folder), under
// the URL /bootstrap/... Each of these examples declares it in its
// config/services.yaml

namespace Commun;

use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\BinaryFileResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\NotFoundHttpException;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Requirement\Requirement;

class BootstrapController
{
     #[Route('/bootstrap/{file}', name: 'bootstrap', requirements: ['fichier' => Requirement::CATCH_ALL],
        methods: ['GET'])]
    public function servir(string $fichier): BinaryFileResponse
    {
        $dossier = realpath(__DIR__.'/bootstrap');
         // realpath: the absolute path of the requested file, excluding . and ..;
         // false if the file does not exist
        $chemin = realpath($dossier.'/'.$fichier);
         // a file that exists, and that is indeed DANS the directory (no ../ to exit it)
        if ($chemin === false || ! str_starts_with($chemin, $dossier.DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR) || ! is_file($chemin)) {
            throw new NotFoundHttpException("fichier inconnu : $fichier");
        }
         // a response that returns the contents of a file; its type, based on its extension
        $reponse = new BinaryFileResponse($chemin);
        $types = ['css' => 'text/css', 'js' => 'text/javascript', 'map' => 'application/json'];
        $reponse->headers->set('Content-Type', $types[pathinfo($chemin, PATHINFO_EXTENSION)] ?? 'application/octet-stream');
        return $reponse;
    }
}
  • line 7: the class is in the [Commun] namespace, which the file [exemples/composer.json] associates with the folder [exemples/commun] (see introduction): the class loader in [Composer] therefore finds it, regardless of the example;
  • Lines 16–17: a route whose parameter [{fichier}] accepts any path ending, including slashes (example 02): the URL [/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css] refers to the [css/bootstrap.min.css] file in the folder. The route is named [bootstrap];
  • Lines 20–27: Serving files designated by URL requires caution: a URL such as [/bootstrap/..%2F..%2F15-gabarit%2F.env] (where [/] is encoded as [%2F]) must not grant access to a file located outside the folder. The [realpath] function of [PHP] calculates the absolute path of a file, stripping away its [.] and [..] components, or returns [false] if the file does not exist. We verify that the resulting path begins with the folder path ([str_starts_with]) and that it refers to a file ([is_file]); otherwise, a 404 error is returned. [DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR] is the system’s path separator: [\] under [Windows], [/] elsewhere;
  • lines 29–32: a [BinaryFileResponse] object is a response that sends the contents of a file. The content type is determined based on the file extension (provided by [pathinfo]), so that a stylesheet is correctly declared as [text/css]: a browser will reject a stylesheet declared as something else.

Each example that uses [Bootstrap] declares this controller as a service in its [config/services.yaml] file:

# config/services.yaml: the application’s services (see Example 06)
services:
    _defaults:
        autowire: true
        autoconfigure: true

    App\:
        resource: '../src/'

     # the controller that serves Bootstrap, common to examples 15 through 28 (see example 15)
    Commun\BootstrapController: ~
  • line 11: the [Commun\BootstrapController] service, with no specific configuration ([~] is the value of [null] in [YAML]): it receives the ones from [_defaults], and [autoconfigure] turns it into a controller, whose route joins those of the application (example 02).

docs.title: 4.3.2. The template: templates/layout.html.twig
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
{# the page template: the pages use ÉTENDENT and fill its blocks #}
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  {# block: a placeholder that the page can fill; here with default content #}
  <title>{% block titre %}Accueil{% endblock %} - {{ nom_site }}</title>
  {# path(): the URL of the route named [bootstrap]; asset(): the URL of a file in public/ #}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ path('bootstrap', {fichier: 'css/bootstrap.min.css'}) }}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('css/styles.css') }}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3">
    {# Insertion of the file fragments/navbar.html.twig #}
    {% include 'fragments/navbar.html.twig' %}
    <main>
      {# The content of the page requested by the action is inserted here #}
      {% block contenu %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {# app: the variable that Symfony assigns to all views (the current request...);
       nom_site : une variable globale (cf. config/packages/twig.yaml) #}
    <footer class="pied">Page [{{ app.request.pathInfo }}] - © {{ 'now'|date('Y') }} {{ nom_site }}</footer>
  </div>
</body>
</html>
  • line 6: the [viewport] tag instructs mobile browsers to display the page at the screen’s width, which is what [Bootstrap] expects;
  • line 8: the [{% block %}] directive marks a named slot, which pages that extend the template can fill by defining a block with the same name. The content written between [{% block titre %}] and [{% endblock %}] is the default content for the placeholder, used by a page that does not define this block. [nom_site] is a global variable, present in all views (see [config/packages/twig.yaml], below);
  • lines 10–11: the function [path] generates the URL for a named route (example 04), using the values of its parameters, which are provided in an associative array of [Twig] ([{fichier: '...'}], the equivalent of [['fichier' => '...']] in [PHP]). The [asset] function generates the URL from a file in the [public] folder. Writing the URL files manually ([/css/styles.css]) would also work, but [path] and [asset] will work if the application is installed under the URL prefix;
  • line 16: [{% include %}] inserts the content of another view, in this case the navigation bar. The included view has access to the variables of the view that includes it;
  • line 19: the space that each page fills with its own content;
  • line 23: the variable [app] is present in all views: [Symfony] stores the current request ([app.request]), the session ([app.session]), the logged-in user ([app.user], see the section on security), the route name ([app.current_route])... [app.request.pathInfo] is the path to the requested URL. The filter [date] formats a date; the string ['now'] denotes the current time.

The [container] class of [Bootstrap] centers the content and limits its width; [py-3] adds an inner vertical margin (padding): [Bootstrap] provides hundreds of classes of this type, which are combined in the [class] attribute. The global variable [nom_site] is declared in the configuration of [Twig]:

# config/packages/twig.yaml: the configuration for TwigBundle
twig:
    default_path: '%kernel.project_dir%/templates'
     # GLOBALES variables, present in all views
    globals:
        nom_site: 'Mon site'

Variables under the key [globals] are added to all views without the need for actions to provide them. A global variable can also be a service (['@App\Service\...']), whose methods will be called by the views.

docs.title: 4.3.3. The navigation bar: templates/fragments/navbar.html.twig
docs.text:
{# a fragment: a section of a page, inserted via `include` #}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand bg-light rounded mb-3 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand">{{ nom_site }}</span>
  <div class="navbar-nav">
    {# path(): the URL of a route, designated by its name #}
    <a class="nav-link" href="{{ path('accueil') }}">Accueil</a>
    <a class="nav-link" href="{{ path('equipe') }}">Équipe</a>
    <a class="nav-link" href="{{ path('brute') }}">Page sans gabarit</a>
  </div>
</nav>

A fragment: a piece of a page that has no meaning on its own. The classes [navbar], [navbar-brand], and [nav-link] are those of the navigation bar for [Bootstrap]. The links are generated by [path], based on the road names.

docs.title: 4.3.4. A macro: templates/macros.html.twig
docs.text:
{# MACROS: page fragments that have parameters, like functions #}

{# a Bootstrap map, with a name and a function #}
{% macro carte(nom, fonction = '') %}
  <div class="card">
    <div class="card-body">
      <h5 class="card-title">{{ nom }}</h5>
      <p class="card-text">{{ fonction }}</p>
    </div>
  </div>
{% endmacro %}
  • Line 4: A macro is a section of a page that has parameters; this is the function of [Twig]. It is declared by [{% macro nom(paramètres) %}] ... [{% endmacro %}]; a parameter can have a default value ([fonction = '']). A file can contain multiple macros. The map ([card]) is a component of [Bootstrap].

A macro can only access its own parameters (and global variables); it cannot access the variables of the view that calls it. This is what makes it reusable. (The [Symfony UX Twig Component] library offers more feature-rich components—[PHP] classes associated with a view—that are used as HTML tags: [<twig:Carte nom="..." />]; we won’t need them.)

docs.title: 4.3.5. The pages
docs.text:
{# this page ÉTEND is the template: it provides only the content of its blocks #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{# the macros in the file macros.html.twig, named m #}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1>Bienvenue</h1>
  <p>Cette page ne contient que son propre contenu : l'entête, la barre de
    navigation et le pied de page viennent du gabarit <code>layout.html.twig</code>.</p>
  {# the macro [carte], called with two parameters entered on the spot #}
  {{ m.carte('Une macro', 'appelée avec des paramètres écrits sur place') }}
{% endblock %}
  • line 2: the page extends the template: [Twig] generates the template page, replacing its blocks with those defined by the page. In a view that extends a template, all content must be within blocks: text written outside of them does not appear in the generated page;
  • line 4: [{% import %}] imports macros from a file under a name of your choice ([m]);
  • lines 6–12: the block [contenu], which fills the slot of the same name. The page does not define the block [titre]: the slot retains its default content, “Home”;
  • line 11: the call to the macro [carte], as a function: [m.carte(...)], within [{{ }}], since it produces text to be inserted. Its output is not escaped a second time: [Twig] knows that it is already safe from HTML (its parameters, however, were escaped within the macro).
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}

{% block titre %}Notre équipe{% endblock %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1>Notre équipe</h1>
  <div class="row g-3">
    {% for membre in membres %}
      <div class="col-md-4">
        {# the macro’s parameters are arbitrary expressions #}
        {{ m.carte(membre.nom, membre.fonction) }}
      </div>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}
  • line 4: the [titre] block, on a single line;
  • lines 8–15: one map per team member, in a grid of [Bootstrap] ([row], [col-md-4]: three columns on a medium or large screen, one column on a narrow screen);
  • line 12: the macro’s parameters are arbitrary expressions.

The controller contains no new features:

<?php
// src/Controller/PagesController.php: three pages

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Modele\Membre;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route(methods: ['GET'])]
class PagesController extends AbstractController
{
     #[Route('/', name: 'accueil')]
    public function accueil(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('pages/accueil.html.twig');
    }

     #[Route('/equipe', name: 'equipe')]
    public function equipe(): Response
    {
        $membres = [
            new Membre('Marie Pélissier', 'Directrice'),
            new Membre('Jacques Bromard', 'Développeur'),
            new Membre('Philippe Jandot', 'Graphiste'),
        ];
        return $this->render('pages/equipe.html.twig', ['membres' => $membres]);
    }

     #[Route('/brute', name: 'brute')]
    public function brute(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('pages/brute.html.twig');
    }
}

Finally, the third page does not use the template:

<!doctype html>
{# This view does not use a template: it is a full page #}
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Page brute</title>
</head>
<body>
  <p>Cette page n'utilise pas le gabarit : ni Bootstrap, ni barre de navigation.</p>
  <p><a href="{{ path('accueil') }}">Retour à l'accueil</a></p>
</body>
</html>

docs.title: 4.4. Example 16: Twig Extensions
docs.text:
A view often needs to format values: an amount with its currency, a date written out in full, or text in uppercase. This code does not belong in the action (which does not handle presentation), and [Twig] does not allow it to be written in the view (which cannot execute [PHP]; see the introduction to this chapter). It is written as [PHP], in an extension of [Twig]: a class that adds its own filters, functions, or tests to the view language. Libraries provide ready-made ones, such as [twig/intl-extra], installed with the examples, which formats dates and amounts according to the language. Finally, macros create pieces of HTML (Example 15).

16-extensions/
├── config/
│   └── services.yaml
├── src/
│   ├── Controller/
│   │   └── PagesController.php
│   ├── EventListener/
│   │   └── FixerLangue.php
│   ├── Modele/
│   │   └── Produit.php
│   ├── Twig/
│   │   └── FormatsExtension.php
│   └── Kernel.php
├── templates/
│   ├── fragments/
│   │   └── navbar.html.twig
│   ├── layout.html.twig
│   ├── macros.html.twig
│   └── pages/
│       ├── accueil.html.twig
│       └── produits.html.twig
└── ...

docs.title: 4.4.1. The extension: src/Twig/FormatsExtension.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Twig/FormatsExtension.php: a Twig module, which adds two filters
// to the view language: currency and date_longue

namespace App\Twig;

use DateTimeInterface;
use IntlDateFormatter;
use NumberFormatter;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RequestStack;
use Twig\Extension\AbstractExtension;
use Twig\TwigFilter;

class FormatsExtension extends AbstractExtension
{
     // the request stack, to determine the language of the current request
    public function __construct(private RequestStack $requetes)
    {
    }

     // the extension’s filters: their names in the views, and the method that implements them
    public function getFilters(): array
    {
        return [
            new TwigFilter('monnaie', $this->monnaie(...)),
            new TwigFilter('date_longue', $this->dateLongue(...)),
        ];
    }

     // an amount in cents, in a currency, formatted according to the language of the
     // request: 114990 -> "1,149.90 €" in French, "€1,149.90" in English.
     // The intl extension of PHP knows the conventions for each country
    public function monnaie(int $centimes, string $devise = 'EUR'): string
    {
        $formateur = new NumberFormatter($this->langue(), NumberFormatter::CURRENCY);
        return $formateur->formatCurrency($centimes / 100, $devise);
    }

     // a date written out in full, in the language of the query: "Sunday, September 27, 2026"
    public function dateLongue(DateTimeInterface $jour): string
    {
        $formateur = new IntlDateFormatter($this->langue(), IntlDateFormatter::FULL, IntlDateFormatter::NONE);
        return $formateur->format($jour);
    }

    private function langue(): string
    {
        return $this->requetes->getCurrentRequest()?->getLocale() ?? 'fr';
    }
}
  • Line 14: An extension of [Twig] inherits from the [AbstractExtension] class. It is a service, like every class in the [src] folder; [Symfony] recognizes it as an extension ([autoconfigure]) and passes it to [Twig];
  • Lines 17–19: The extension needs the language of the current request. It receives the request stack ([RequestStack]), a service from [Symfony] that knows the current request (there is a stack because one request can trigger another internally);
  • lines 22–28: The method [getFilters] returns the extension’s filters: for each one, its name in the views and the function that implements it. [$this->monnaie(...)] (with the ellipsis) does not call the method: it turns it into a value—a function that can be called later (a first-class callable). An extension can also provide functions ([getFunctions]) and tests ([getTests]);
  • lines 33–37: formatting an amount received in cents (see Example 06). This depends on the language: in French, [1 149,90 €] (space to separate thousands, decimal comma, symbol after the amount); in English, [€1,149.90]. The class [NumberFormatter], part of the [intl] extension of [PHP], supports the conventions of all countries (it uses data from the Unicode project CLDR): it is created for a language and a style (here, [CURRENCY], for amounts), and [formatCurrency] formats an amount, with the currency designated by its international code ([EUR], [USD]). The first parameter of the filter is the filtered value; the subsequent parameters are its properties in the view ([prix|monnaie('USD')]);
  • lines 40–44: formatting a date using class [IntlDateFormatter] from the [intl] extension: style [FULL] writes the date in full, including the day of the week ([dimanche 27 septembre 2026]); the style [NONE], for the time, does not include it. The type [DateTimeInterface] accepts all dates from [PHP];
  • lines 46–49: the language ([fr], [en]) of the current query, or French if there is no query (in a console command, for example). We’ll see who sets it.

docs.title: 4.4.2. The language of each request: src/EventListener/FixerLangue.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/EventListener/FixerLangue.php: the language of each request

namespace App\EventListener;

use Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\Attribute\AsEventListener;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Event\RequestEvent;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\KernelEvents;

// priority: the order of listeners for the same event (highest first);
// 20: after routing (32), before the Symfony listeners that use the language (16, 15)
#[AsEventListener(event: KernelEvents::REQUEST, priority: 20)]
class FixerLangue
{
     // the ?lang=en parameter in URL; otherwise, French
    public function __invoke(RequestEvent $evenement): void
    {
        $requete = $evenement->getRequest();
        $requete->setLocale($requete->query->get('lang') === 'en' ? 'en' : 'fr');
    }
}

Each request has a language (locale), which defaults to the language [default_locale] specified in the configuration ([en] if nothing is configured). Here, the parameter [?lang=en] of URL selects English; French is the default language. A listener for the [kernel.request] event (Example 12) sets this before each action using the [setLocale] method of the request. The [priority] parameter of the attribute sets the order of listeners for the same event: the highest-priority ones are processed first (default is 0). [Symfony] itself has several listeners of [kernel.request]: routing (priority 32), followed by those that prepare language-dependent services (16 and 15). Ours must run between the two: 20. The command [php bin/console debug:event-dispatcher kernel.request] displays all listeners for the event, in order. The language set in this way applies only to the current request: the next one will revert to the default language. The chapter on internationalization will use this same language to translate the texts.

docs.title: 4.4.3. The configuration: config/services.yaml
docs.text:
# config/services.yaml: the application’s services (see Example 06)
services:
    _defaults:
        autowire: true
        autoconfigure: true

    App\:
        resource: '../src/'

     # the controller that serves Bootstrap, common to examples 15 through 28 (see example 15)
    Commun\BootstrapController: ~

     # the Twig Intl extension (twig/intl-extra library): the filters
     # format_currency, format_date, format_number...
    Twig\Extra\Intl\IntlExtension: ~
  • Line 15: The filters for the [twig/intl-extra] library are provided by the [IntlExtension] extension. Its class is not in the [src] folder: it is declared as a service, and [Symfony] recognizes it as an extension of [Twig] ([autoconfigure]). (In a standard project, the [twig/extra-bundle] package, installed by [Symfony Flex], handles this itself.)

docs.title: 4.4.4. The controller: src/Controller/PagesController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/PagesController.php: two pages

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Modele\Produit;
use DateTimeImmutable;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route(methods: ['GET'])]
class PagesController extends AbstractController
{
     #[Route('/', name: 'accueil')]
    public function accueil(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('pages/accueil.html.twig', ['aujourdhui' => new DateTimeImmutable('today')]);
    }

     #[Route('/produits', name: 'produits')]
    public function produits(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('pages/produits.html.twig', ['produits' => [
            new Produit('clavier', 2500, 12),
            new Produit('souris', 1250, 0),
            new Produit('écran', 114990, 3),
        ]]);
    }
}

Actions pass raw values to the views: a date ([new DateTimeImmutable('today')], today’s date at midnight) and amounts in cents. Formatting is handled by the views. The [Produit] class combines a name, a price (in cents; see Example 06), and a stock level.

docs.title: 4.4.5. The views
docs.text:
{# a link in the navigation bar, which is assigned the class [active] if the page
   courante est sous le chemin [chemin]. app.request.pathInfo : le chemin de la
   requête en cours ; starts with : un test de Twig #}
{% macro lien(href, chemin, texte) %}
  <a class="nav-link{{ app.request.pathInfo starts with chemin ? ' active' }}" href="{{ href }}">{{ texte }}</a>
{% endmacro %}

{# a Bootstrap badge: green if the product is in stock, red otherwise #}
{% macro badge(stock) %}
  <span class="badge {{ stock > 0 ? 'text-bg-success' : 'text-bg-danger' }}">{{ stock > 0 ? stock ~ ' en stock' : 'épuisé' }}</span>
{% endmacro %}
  • lines 4–6: a macro that creates a link for the navigation bar. The link for the current page is assigned the class [active] from [Bootstrap], which highlights it. A macro accesses the global variable [app] (Example 15): [app.request.pathInfo] is the path of the current request; [starts with] is an operator of [Twig], which checks for the start of a string. The ternary operator without an “else” clause ([condition ? ' active']) returns an empty string if the condition is false (Example 14);
  • Lines 9–11: a badge from [Bootstrap], green ([text-bg-success]) or red ([text-bg-danger]) depending on inventory. The [~] operator of [Twig] concatenates two strings (the [.] of [PHP]).
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand bg-light rounded mb-3 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand">Extensions</span>
  <div class="navbar-nav">
    {# 1. a condition written in the view; app.current_route: the name of the current route #}
    <a class="nav-link{{ app.current_route == 'accueil' ? ' active' }}" href="{{ path('accueil') }}">Accueil</a>
    {# 2. the macro [lien] #}
    {{ m.lien(path('produits'), '/produits', 'Produits') }}
    {# 3. path() returns the URL of a named route; a parameter that is not a
         paramètre de la route s'ajoute à la fin de l'URL : /produits?lang=en #}
    <a class="nav-link" href="{{ path('produits', {lang: 'en'}) }}">Products (en)</a>
  </div>
</nav>
  • line 1: an included fragment (example 15) does not inherit imports from the view that includes it: it imports the macros it needs on its own;
  • line 6: the same as with the macro, written directly in the view, using the ternary operator. [app.current_route] is the name of the current request path. The macro avoids repeating the condition for each link;
  • line 8: the macro call;
  • line 11: a parameter of [path] that is not a route parameter is added to URL as a parameter: [/produits?lang=en].
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% block titre %}Accueil{% endblock %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1>Accueil</h1>
  {# our filter date_longue #}
  <p>Nous sommes le {{ aujourdhui|date_longue }}.</p>
  {# app.request.locale: the request language, set by the listener FixerLangue #}
  <p>Langue de formatage : {{ app.request.locale }}
    (<a href="{{ path('accueil', {lang: 'en'}) }}">en anglais</a>, <a href="{{ path('accueil') }}">en français</a>)</p>
{% endblock %}
  • line 7: our filter [date_longue];
  • line 9: [app.request.locale], the request language, set by the listener [FixerLangue].
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}
{% block titre %}Produits{% endblock %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1>Produits</h1>
  <table class="table table-sm w-auto">
    <thead><tr><th>Produit</th><th>Prix</th><th>Prix en dollars</th><th>Stock</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      {% for produit in produits %}
        <tr>
          {# a Twig filter (upper), then our currency filter—first without, then with a parameter #}
          <td>{{ produit.nom|upper }}</td>
          <td>{{ produit.prixCentimes|monnaie }}</td>
          <td>{{ produit.prixCentimes|monnaie('USD') }}</td>
          {# the [badge] macro generates the HTML for the badge #}
          <td>{{ m.badge(produit.stock) }}</td>
        </tr>
      {% endfor %}
    </tbody>
  </table>
  {# the format_currency filter from the Intl extension: an amount (here in units), a
     devise, et la langue de la requête #}
  <p>Total du stock : {{ (produits|reduce((s, p) => s + p.prixCentimes * p.stock, 0) / 100)|format_currency('EUR', locale: app.request.locale) }}</p>
{% endblock %}
  • line 13: a filter for [Twig];
  • Lines 14–15: our [monnaie] filter, first with its default motto, then with a parameter;
  • line 17: the call to the [badge] macro;
  • line 24: the [format_currency] filter from the Intl extension: an amount (here in euros: the total inventory, calculated by [reduce], divided by 100), a currency, and the query language, passed via a named parameter from [Twig] ([locale: ...]). This extension also provides [format_date], [format_datetime], [format_number], [country_name], [language_name]... Our filter [monnaie] therefore serves a dual purpose: we wrote it to demonstrate how to write an extension.

The template [layout.html.twig] is a simplified version of the one in Example 15; its attribute [lang] receives the language of the request ([<html lang="{{ app.request.locale }}">]).

docs.title: 4.5. Example 17: A GET form
docs.text:
A HTML form sends its fields to the server in one of two ways, depending on its [method] attribute:

  • [method="get"]: The fields are added to the URL as parameters ([/recherche?motCle=le&genre=roman]). This is the method used by a form that performs a query: a search or a filter. The URL containing the results can be bookmarked, shared, or reloaded safely;
  • [method="post"]: The fields are included in the request body (see Example 11). This is the method used by a form that modifies data: a registration, an addition, or a deletion.

This first form is a book search. It is hand-coded in HTML within the view; the following examples will use the Form component from [Symfony] for the forms.

docs.title: 4.5.1. The template: src/Modele/Livre.php and RechercheModele.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Template/Livre.php: a book

namespace App\Modele;

readonly class Livre
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $titre,
        public string $auteur,
        public string $genre,
    ) {
    }

docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/LivresController.php: a search form, submitted by GET

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Modele\Livre;
use App\Modele\RechercheModele;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class LivresController extends AbstractController
{
     // of class CONSTANTES: the data, written in the code for the example
    private const GENRES = ['roman', 'poésie', 'théâtre'];

     /** @return list<Book> */
    private static function livres(): array
    {
        return [
            new Livre('Le Rouge et le Noir', 'Stendhal', 'roman'),
            new Livre('Les Fleurs du mal', 'Baudelaire', 'poésie'),
            new Livre('Madame Bovary', 'Flaubert', 'roman'),
            new Livre('Alcools', 'Apollinaire', 'poésie'),
            new Livre('Le Cid', 'Corneille', 'théâtre'),
        ];
    }

     // GET / and GET/search?motCle=...&genre=...: the ET form and its results;
     // two ways to perform the same action: the #[Route] attribute can be repeated
     #[Route('/', name: 'livres_accueil', methods: ['GET'])]
     #[Route('/recherche', name: 'livres_recherche', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function recherche(Request $request): Response
    {
         // getString: the parameter, as a string ('' if absent)
        $motCle = $request->query->getString('motCle');
        $genre = $request->query->getString('genre');
        $mot = mb_strtolower($motCle);
        $resultats = array_values(array_filter(self::livres(), fn (Livre $livre) =>
            ($mot === '' || str_contains(mb_strtolower($livre->titre), $mot)
                || str_contains(mb_strtolower($livre->auteur), $mot))
            && ($genre === '' || $livre->genre === $genre)));
        return $this->render('livres/recherche.html.twig', [
            'modele' => new RechercheModele($motCle, $genre, self::GENRES, $resultats),
        ]);
    }
}
  • Line 16: A private class constant named [self::GENRES] ([self] refers to the current class). A constant cannot contain objects: the books are therefore provided by a static method (lines 19–28). In a real application, they would come from a database;
  • lines 32–33: two routes for the same action: the [#[Route]] attribute can be repeated. On the first visit ([/]), there are no parameters, and all books are displayed;
  • lines 37–38: The form fields are read as parameters for URL (example 07). The [getString] method returns the parameter as a string, empty if it is absent;
  • lines 40–43: filtering. The [array_filter] function retains the elements of an array for which the given function returns [true]: a book is selected if the keyword is empty or appears in its title or author (in lowercase on both sides; [mb_strtolower] correctly handles accented characters), and if the genre is empty or matches the book’s genre. [array_filter] retains the keys of the selected items (0, 2...): [array_values] renumbers them starting from 0;
  • lines 44–46: the view template.

{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1 class="h3">Recherche de livres</h1>
  {# method="get": the fields are sent in the URL (?motCle=...&genre=...) #}
  <form method="get" action="{{ path('livres_recherche') }}" class="row g-2 align-items-end mb-3">
    <div class="col-auto">
      <label class="form-label" for="motCle">Titre ou auteur</label>
      {# value: the field displays the entered value (escaped by {{ }}) #}
      <input class="form-control" id="motCle" name="motCle" value="{{ modele.motCle }}">
    </div>
    <div class="col-auto">
      <label class="form-label" for="genre">Genre</label>
      <select class="form-select" id="genre" name="genre">
        <option value="">(tous)</option>
        {% for genre in modele.genres %}
          {# the boolean "selected" attribute, set if the condition is true, omitted otherwise #}
          <option value="{{ genre }}"{{ genre == modele.genre ? ' selected' }}>{{ genre }}</option>
        {% endfor %}
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="col-auto">
      <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Rechercher</button>
    </div>
  </form>
  <p>{{ modele.resultats|length }} livre(s) trouvé(s).</p>
  <ul>
    {% for livre in modele.resultats %}
      <li><i>{{ livre.titre }}</i>, {{ livre.auteur }} ({{ livre.genre }})</li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>
{% endblock %}
  • Line 6: the [<form>] tag. The [action] attribute is the URL to which the form is submitted; [method="get"] places the fields in the URL. The classes of [Bootstrap] arrange the fields on a single line;
  • Line 8: a label. Its [for] attribute specifies the identifier ([id]) of the field it describes: clicking on the label places the cursor in the field, and screen readers read the label along with the field;
  • line 10: an input field. Its attribute [name] is the name of the parameter sent to the server: this is the link between the form and the action ([$request->query->getString('motCle')]). The attribute [value] is the displayed value: the previous entry, redisplayed (and escaped by [{{ }}], which is essential in an attribute: an entry containing a quotation mark ["] would otherwise close the attribute);
  • lines 14–20: a drop-down list. Each [<option>] has a value ([value]), sent to the server, and text, displayed. The first option, with an empty value, means “all genres”;
  • line 18: the option selected in the previous request is assigned the attribute [selected]. This is a Boolean attribute: its presence alone is sufficient; it has no value. The ternary operator without the “else” part writes it if the condition is true, and writes nothing otherwise. [==] is the equality of [Twig];
  • line 23: the submit button;
  • line 26: the number of results.

docs.title: 4.6. Example 18: Form Fields
docs.text:
This example presents all the field types in a HTML form, this time submitted by POST. It shows how to redisplay each field type with its current value, how the browser sends the values for each one, and how the server verifies that a received value is indeed one of the available options. Writing all of this by hand, as in Example 17, would be time-consuming and repetitive. [Symfony] delegates this task to its Form component: a form is described by a class, its type; [Symfony] generates the HTML, reads the submitted fields, converts them, validates them, and redisplays the form with the user’s input and any errors. This is the counterpart to [WTForms] in [Python].

namespace App\Service;

    public function titres(): array

The form’s dropdown lists (titles, countries, hobbies, languages) are provided by a service, following the model in Example 06: in a real application, they would come from a database. Each list is an associative array: the key is the displayed text, and the value is what is sent to the server (this is the order expected by the Form component).
