docs.title: 4.6.3. Form type: src/Form/FormulaireType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Form/FormulaireType.php: the DESCRIPTION of the form: its fields, their types, and their options

namespace App\Form;

use App\Service\ListesService;
use Symfony\Component\Form\AbstractType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\ChoiceType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\DateType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\HiddenType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\TextareaType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\TextType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints\NotBlank;

class FormulaireType extends AbstractType
{
     // A form type is a service: it receives the list service
    public function __construct(private ListesService $listes)
    {
    }

     // the form fields, in the order they are displayed
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $constructeur, array $options): void
    {
        $constructeur
             // radio buttons: a list of choices (ChoiceType), "expanded";
             // constraints: the field’s validation constraints (see example 08)
            ->add('titre', ChoiceType::class, [
                'choices' => $this->listes->titres(),
                'expanded' => true,
                'label_attr' => ['class' => 'radio-inline'],
                'constraints' => [new NotBlank(message: 'Le titre est obligatoire.')],
            ])
             // an input field; required => false: the field is not required
            ->add('nom', TextType::class, ['required' => false])
             // a password: never displayed on the page
            ->add('mot_de_passe', PasswordType::class, ['label' => 'Mot de passe', 'required' => false])
             // a date: an <input type="date"> field; the value is a string in the format yyyy-mm-dd
            ->add('naissance', DateType::class, [
                'label' => 'Date de naissance',
                'widget' => 'single_text',
                'input' => 'string',
                'required' => false,
            ])
             // checkboxes: a drop-down list of options, with options MULTIPLES
            ->add('loisirs', ChoiceType::class, [
                'choices' => $this->listes->loisirs(),
                'expanded' => true,
                'multiple' => true,
                'label_attr' => ['class' => 'checkbox-inline'],
                'required' => false,
            ])
             // drop-down list: a non-expanded list of options
            ->add('pays', ChoiceType::class, ['choices' => $this->listes->pays()])
             // multiple-select list, displayed on four lines
            ->add('langues', ChoiceType::class, [
                'label' => 'Langues parlées',
                'choices' => $this->listes->langues(),
                'multiple' => true,
                'attr' => ['size' => 4],
                'required' => false,
            ])
            ->add('commentaire', TextareaType::class, ['required' => false, 'attr' => ['rows' => 2]])
             // a hidden field
            ->add('jeton', HiddenType::class);
    }
}
  • line 17: a form type inherits from the [AbstractType] class. It is a service (located in the [src] folder): it can accept other services, in this case the list service (line 20);
  • line 25: the method [buildForm] describes the fields by adding them ([add]) to a form builder: for each field, its name, type, and options. The field name is also the name of the data it displays; its label, by default, is its name formatted as text ([nom] becomes “Name”);
  • Lines 30–35: A [ChoiceType] field is a drop-down list, defined by the [choices] option. With the [expanded] option, it becomes a group of radio buttons (a single-selection field). The option [label_attr] assigns a class to the group label: [radio-inline] specifies side-by-side buttons in the theme. The option [constraints] sets the field’s validation constraints (example 08): a title is required;
  • line 37: a [TextType] field is an input field. The option [required] defaults to [true]: [Symfony] then sets the attribute HTML to [required], which the browser checks (Example 19). It does not send any information to the server: it is a constraint ([NotBlank]) that makes a field required for the server;
  • line 39: a password ([PasswordType]), which is never returned to the page: its field is always empty when displayed;
  • lines 41–46: a date ([DateType]), displayed by a single field [<input type="date">] (option [widget]). Such a field exchanges its value with the server in the [aaaa-mm-jj] format, regardless of the format in which the browser displays it; the [input] option specifies that the data is a string (rather than a [DateTime] object, which is the default);
  • lines 48–54: a drop-down list with multiple choices ([multiple]): checkboxes;
  • line 56: a non-expanded multiple-choice list: a drop-down list;
  • lines 58–64: a non-expanded, multiple-choice list: a multi-select list, displayed across four lines (the attribute HTML [size], specified by the option [attr]);
  • line 65: a text box ([TextareaType]), spanning two lines;
  • line 67: a hidden field ([HiddenType]).

[Symfony] provides about thirty field types: [EmailType], [IntegerType], [MoneyType], [UrlType], [CheckboxType], [FileType], [CountryType], [RepeatedType] (example 19), [CollectionType] (a list of subforms)...

docs.title: 4.6.4. The controller: src/Controller/FormulaireController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/FormulaireController.php: a form that uses all field types

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Form\FormulaireType;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class FormulaireController extends AbstractController
{
     // GET: the form, with initial values; POST: the submitted fields
     // are read, validated, and then redisplayed by the same form
     #[Route('/formulaire', name: 'formulaire', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function formulaire(Request $request): Response
    {
         // the initial values (one per field, an array for a multi-value field)
        $initiales = ['titre' => 'Mme', 'pays' => 'fr', 'langues' => ['français'], 'jeton' => 'A7X2'];
         // createForm: the form, constructed based on its description
        $formulaire = $this->createForm(FormulaireType::class, $initiales);
         // handleRequest: if the request is a POST, the received fields are copied
         // in the form, then validated
        $formulaire->handleRequest($request);
        $modele = ['formulaire' => $formulaire];
        if ($formulaire->isSubmitted()) {
             // what the browser actually sent, field by field
            $recu = [];
            foreach ($request->request->all() as $nom => $valeur) {
                foreach ((array) $valeur as $cle => $v) {
                    $recu[] = "{$nom}[$cle] = [".implode(', ', (array) $v).']';
                }
            }
            $modele += [
                'recu' => implode("\n", $recu),
                'valide' => $formulaire->isValid(),
                 // getErrors(true): errors for all fields
                'erreurs' => $formulaire->getErrors(true),
                 // getData(): the form values, converted by each field
                'donnees' => $formulaire->getData(),
            ];
        }
        return $this->render('formulaire/formulaire.html.twig', $modele);
    }
}
  • line 16: a single action for both methods: GET displays the form, POST processes it. This is the standard way to write a form action with [Symfony];
  • line 20: the form’s initial values: an associative array, one value per field (an array for a multi-value field);
  • line 22: [createForm] creates the form—a [Form] object—based on its type and initial data;
  • line 25: [handleRequest] examines the request. For a GET, it does nothing. For a POST that contains the form fields, it copies them into the form: each field converts its value (the date, the lists, etc.), verifies that a selection is among those that were offered, and then the form validates the constraints and the anti-CSRF token;
  • line 27: [isSubmitted]: Was the form submitted?;
  • lines 29–34: for this example, the list of what the browser actually sent. The fields of a [Symfony] form are named after the form: [formulaire[nom]], [formulaire[loisirs][]]. [PHP] therefore organizes them into an array named [formulaire] (Example 10), which is then iterated over. [(array) $valeur] converts a single value into a one-element array (an array remains an array); [implode] combines the elements of an array into a string, separated by the first parameter;
  • lines 35–42: the view template receives what the server received: the validation result ([isValid]), the errors ([getErrors(true)]: those for all fields), and the form data ([getData]), converted by each field. The [+=] operator adds these keys to the [$modele] array;
  • line 44: the form is passed to the view, which will display it, along with the user’s input and any errors.

docs.title: 4.6.5. The view: templates/form/formulaire.html.twig
docs.text:
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1 class="h3">Un formulaire complet</h1>
  {# form_start: the <form> tag, here with the POST method and the URL from page #}
  {{ form_start(formulaire, {attr: {style: 'max-width: 40rem'}}) }}
    {# form_row: a complete field (label, input field, errors) #}
    {{ form_row(formulaire.titre) }}
    <div class="row g-2">
      <div class="col">{{ form_row(formulaire.nom) }}</div>
      <div class="col">{{ form_row(formulaire.mot_de_passe) }}</div>
      <div class="col">{{ form_row(formulaire.naissance) }}</div>
    </div>
    {{ form_row(formulaire.loisirs) }}
    <div class="row g-2">
      <div class="col">{{ form_row(formulaire.pays) }}</div>
      <div class="col">{{ form_row(formulaire.langues) }}</div>
    </div>
    {{ form_row(formulaire.commentaire) }}
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Envoyer</button>
  {# form_end: the remaining fields (the hidden field, the anti-CSRF token), followed by </form> #}
  {{ form_end(formulaire) }}

  {# is defined: true if the variable `recu` was passed to the view (form submitted) #}
  {% if recu is defined %}
    <h2 class="h5 mt-3">Ce que le serveur a reçu</h2>
    <pre class="bg-light p-2 border">{{ recu }}</pre>
    <p>Formulaire valide : {{ valide ? 'oui' : 'non' }}</p>
    <ul>
      {% for erreur in erreurs %}
        {# erreur.origin: the field with an error; erreur.message: the message #}
        <li>{{ erreur.origin.name }} : {{ erreur.message }}</li>
      {% endfor %}
    </ul>
    {% if valide %}
      <p>Les données du formulaire :</p>
      <ul>
        {# a loop over an associative array: the key and the value #}
        {% for cle, valeur in donnees %}
          <li>{{ cle }} : {{ valeur is iterable ? valeur|join(', ') : valeur }}</li>
        {% endfor %}
      </ul>
    {% endif %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}
  • line 6: the function [form_start] writes the tag [<form>]: the method POST and the URL of the current page, by default; the second parameter adds HTML attributes;
  • Line 8: The [form_row] function writes a complete field: its label, its input field (with its current value), and its errors, using the theme’s classes. [formulaire.titre] refers to the [titre] field in the form. You can also write the parts separately: [form_label], [form_widget], [form_errors];
  • lines 9–19: the other fields, arranged by the grid classes of [Bootstrap];
  • line 22: [form_end] writes the fields that have not yet been written (in this case, the hidden field [jeton] and the hidden field [_token], the anti-CSRF token), then closes the [</form>] tag;
  • line 25: the [is defined] check: the variable [recu] only exists after a submission;
  • lines 30–33: the errors. Each is a [FormError] object, where [origin] is the field containing the error;
  • Lines 39–41: A [for] loop on an associative array, which iterates over both the keys and the values. The [is iterable] test distinguishes between arrays (grouped by the [join] filter) and single values.

The entire form could have been written in a single line: [{{ form(formulaire) }}]. The functions [form_start], [form_row], and [form_end] allow you to arrange the fields as desired.

[Symfony] has written everything: the identifiers ([formulaire_titre_1]), the labels associated with their fields, the names ending in [[]] for multiple fields (example 10), the [checked] and [selected] attributes of common values, and the classes of [Bootstrap]. The last hidden field, [formulaire[_token]], contains the anti-CSRF token. A CSRF attack (Cross-Site Request Forgery) involves a malicious site tricking its victim’s browser into submitting a form to our application. The browser includes our application’s cookies in the request—and thus the logged-in user’s session—making the request appear legitimate. The countermeasure: every form in our application contains a random token linked to the user’s session, which the malicious site cannot know. The Form component adds this token to every form, and [handleRequest] rejects any form whose token is missing or incorrect: no form can omit it. (The [data-controller] attribute is used by an optional script for [Symfony], which enhances protection; it has no effect here.) Let’s fill out the form and submit it:

The page shows what the server received: one parameter per field, with multiple values for the checkboxes and the dropdown list; the password was sent but is not displayed again in its field. The hidden field [jeton] was returned as-is: this is the way to send information back and forth that the user cannot see (the case study uses this for a record’s version number). However, a hidden field is not a protected field: the user can modify it using their browser’s developer tools, and the server must validate it just like any other field. The anti-CSRF token is also included among the received fields; it is not part of the form data.

Now let’s send a form without a token, using [curl], and with a country that wasn’t listed as an option:

curl -g -d "formulaire[nom]=Martin&formulaire[pays]=xx" http://localhost:8000/form

...
    <h2 class="h5 mt-3">Ce que le serveur a reçu</h2>
    <pre class="bg-light p-2 border">formulaire[nom] = [Martin]
formulaire[pays] = [xx]</pre>
    <p>Formulaire valide : non</p>
    <ul>
                      <li>formulaire : Le jeton CSRF est invalide. Veuillez renvoyer le formulaire.</li>
                      <li>titre : Le titre est obligatoire.</li>
                      <li>pays : Le choix sélectionné est invalide.</li>
          </ul>
...

The form is invalid for three reasons: the anti-CSRF token is missing (the error is associated with the form itself), no title was submitted, and the country [xx] is not among the available options. This last check is performed by the [ChoiceType] field itself, without us having requested it: a malicious user could submit anything, not just what the page offered. The messages are in French: those from the Form component are translated by [Symfony], as are those from the validator (example 09). The response has status code 422 (Unprocessable Content): [render] selects it automatically when presented with a submitted, invalid form. Note the difference from other frameworks: [Symfony] does not reject the request before the action; it is the form that declares it invalid, and the action that decides how to proceed.

For the token to be accepted, [curl] must behave like a browser: first request the form, while retaining the session cookie (option [-c], which saves received cookies to a file), then resend the cookie (option [-b]) and the token read from the page. The option [--data-urlencode] encodes the token value itself:

curl -c cookies.txt http://localhost:8000/form
curl -b cookies.txt -g --data-urlencode "formulaire[_token]=fd1f4224ba.KXZM..." -d "formulaire[nom]=Martin&formulaire[pays]=xx" http://localhost:8000/form

...
    <ul>
                      <li>titre : Le titre est obligatoire.</li>
                      <li>pays : Le choix sélectionné est invalide.</li>
          </ul>
...

(the token is the one from the page received by the first command). Only the two input errors remain.

docs.title: 4.7. Example 19: Form Validation
docs.text:
A registration form, where each field has its own validation rules. If an error occurs, the form is redisplayed with the user’s input and a message below each field containing an error. This example uses the standard approach of [Symfony]: the form data is an object, whose class contains the constraints (Example 08); the form populates the object and then validates it.

19-validation-formulaire/
├── src/
│   ├── Controller/
│   │   └── InscriptionController.php
│   ├── Form/
│   │   └── InscriptionType.php
│   ├── Modele/
│   │   └── Inscription.php
│   └── Kernel.php
├── templates/
│   ├── inscription/
│   │   ├── bienvenue.html.twig
│   │   └── inscription.html.twig
│   └── layout.html.twig
└── ...

The files [config/packages/framework.yaml] and [config/packages/twig.yaml] are those from Example 18.

docs.title: 4.7.1. Data and Its Constraints: src/Modele/Inscription.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Template/Inscription.php: registration form data and its constraints

namespace App\Modele;

use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;

class Inscription
{
     #[Assert\NotBlank(message: 'Le nom est obligatoire.')]
     #[Assert\Length(max: 20, maxMessage: 'Le nom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.')]
    public ?string $nom = null;

     // Email: a valid address with a fully qualified domain name (e.g., exemple.fr, not “example”)
     #[Assert\NotBlank(message: "L'adresse électronique est obligatoire.")]
     #[Assert\Email(message: 'Adresse électronique invalide.')]
    public ?string $email = null;

     #[Assert\NotBlank(message: "L'âge est obligatoire.")]
     #[Assert\Range(notInRangeMessage: "L'âge doit être compris entre 18 et 120 ans.", min: 18, max: 120)]
    public ?int $age = null;

     #[Assert\NotBlank(message: 'Le mot de passe est obligatoire.')]
     #[Assert\Length(min: 6, minMessage: 'Le mot de passe doit comporter au moins 6 caractères.')]
    public ?string $motDePasse = null;
}
  • Line 8: a regular class whose properties are public and editable; the form will populate them one by one. All are initialized to [null]; the object is empty when first displayed;
  • lines 10–12: the name is required and must not exceed 20 characters. Each constraint is assigned its own message here, in French (example 09): [message] for [NotBlank], [maxMessage] for exceeding [Length];
  • lines 15–17: The constraint [Email] verifies that an address is valid and requires a fully qualified domain name ([exemple.fr], not [exemple]);
  • lines 19–21: age is an integer between 18 and 120 ([notInRangeMessage]: the message for [Range] when there is a minimum and a maximum). The form will have converted the input to an integer;
  • lines 23–25: The password must be at least 6 characters long.

docs.title: 4.7.2. The form: src/Form/InscriptionType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Form/InscriptionType.php: fields in the registration form

namespace App\Form;

use App\Modele\Inscription;
use Symfony\Component\Form\AbstractType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\EmailType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\IntegerType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\PasswordType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\RepeatedType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\TextType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\OptionsResolver\OptionsResolver;

class InscriptionType extends AbstractType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $constructeur, array $options): void
    {
        $constructeur
             // attr: additional HTML attributes on the input field (for
             // browser validation; see below)
            ->add('nom', TextType::class, ['attr' => ['maxlength' => 20]])
            ->add('email', EmailType::class, ['label' => 'Adresse électronique'])
             // IntegerType: an integer; an entry that is not a product
             // the error invalid_message
            ->add('age', IntegerType::class, [
                'label' => 'Âge',
                'attr' => ['min' => 18, 'max' => 120],
                'invalid_message' => 'Un nombre entier est attendu.',
            ])
             // RepeatedType: DEUX fields that must contain the same value (the word
             // password and its confirmation); a single value in the data
            ->add('motDePasse', RepeatedType::class, [
                'type' => PasswordType::class,
                'first_options' => ['label' => 'Mot de passe', 'attr' => ['minlength' => 6]],
                'second_options' => ['label' => 'Confirmation'],
                'invalid_message' => 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.',
            ]);
    }

     // form options: its data is a Registration object
    public function configureOptions(OptionsResolver $options): void
    {
        $options->setDefaults(['data_class' => Inscription::class]);
    }
}
  • line 23: the [attr] option adds HTML attributes to the input field: [maxlength] limits the input in the browser;
  • line 24: a [EmailType] field generates a [<input type="email">], which the browser can validate;
  • lines 27–31: a [IntegerType] field generates a [<input type="number">] and converts the input to an integer. An entry that is not an integer cannot be converted: this is a conversion error (not a validation error; see example 08), for which the error message is provided by the [invalid_message] option;
  • Lines 34–39: A [RepeatedType] field consists of two fields (here, two [PasswordType] fields), which must contain the same value: the password and its confirmation. Each has its own options ([first_options], [second_options]); if the two entries differ, the error is [invalid_message]. The data has only one value: the password;
  • lines 43–46: the method [configureOptions] sets the options for the form itself: [data_class] indicates that its data is a [Inscription] object. Each field reads and writes the property of the same name.

[Symfony] can also infer a field’s type based on the constraints and the property’s type: [->add('age')], which has no type, would produce a [IntegerType], with the attributes [min] and [max] inferred from [Range]. We’ve written this out explicitly for clarity.

docs.title: 4.7.3. The controller: src/Controller/InscriptionController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/InscriptionController.php: a form validated by the server

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Form\InscriptionType;
use App\Modele\Inscription;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Attribute\MapQueryParameter;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class InscriptionController extends AbstractController
{
     // GET /registration: the form; ?html5=true: let the browser
     // validate it before submission. POST /registration: the submitted form
     #[Route('/inscription', name: 'inscription', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function inscription(Request $request, #[MapQueryParameter] bool $html5 = false): Response
    {
        $inscription = new Inscription();
        $formulaire = $this->createForm(InscriptionType::class, $inscription);
        $formulaire->handleRequest($request);
         // isValid: the fields were successfully converted, and the Registration
         // meets its constraints
        if ($formulaire->isSubmitted() && $formulaire->isValid()) {
            return $this->render('inscription/bienvenue.html.twig', ['inscription' => $inscription]);
        }
         // the initial display, or an invalid form, redisplayed with the input
         // and errors (render then returns it with code 422)
        return $this->render('inscription/inscription.html.twig',
            ['formulaire' => $formulaire, 'html5' => $html5]);
    }
}
  • line 19: the parameter [?html5=true] enables browser validation (see below). [#[MapQueryParameter]] converts it to a Boolean (example 07);
  • lines 21–23: The empty object [Inscription] is passed to the form; [handleRequest] will populate it using the submitted fields;
  • lines 26–28: [isValid] is true if every field could be converted and if the [Inscription] object meets its constraints. The welcome page then receives the filled-in object (the following example will show that it is better to redirect after a successful POST);
  • lines 31–32: otherwise, the form is displayed: empty on the first display; after an invalid submission, it shows the input and errors, along with code 422 (example 18).

The invalid form is therefore redisplayed by the POST action itself, which retains the input and errors: this is the approach taken by [Symfony]. Other frameworks, such as [Laravel], instead respond by redirecting to the form page, while retaining the input and errors in the session for the next request.

{% block contenu %}

  {% if html5 %}
    <p>Validation par le navigateur <b>activée</b> - <a href="{{ path('inscription') }}">la désactiver</a></p>
  {% else %}
    <p>Validation par le navigateur <b>désactivée</b> - <a href="{{ path('inscription', {html5: 'true'}) }}">l'activer</a></p>
  {% endif %}

     le formulaire tel quel ; seul le serveur valide #}
  {{ form_start(formulaire, {attr: html5 ? {} : {novalidate: 'novalidate'}}) }}

    {{ form_widget(formulaire) }}

{% endblock %}

  • line 14: [form_widget(formulaire)], applied to the entire form, writes all its fields, each with its label, input, and error messages: the [Bootstrap] theme highlights an invalid field in red (class [is-invalid]) and displays its message below it (class [invalid-feedback]). We didn’t have to write any components for this;
  • lines 19–25: the [bas_de_page] block, defined by the template (see below). [formulaire.vars] contains the form data, calculated for the view: [submitted] (submitted?), [valid] (valid?), [value], [errors]... If the form has been submitted and is invalid, a general message appears in a field whose style is defined by [public/css/styles.css] (example 15). The [role="alert"] attribute flags this to screen readers.

{% block contenu %}

  <h1 class="h3">Bienvenue {{ inscription.nom }}</h1>

[inscription] is the object [Inscription], populated and validated: the name has had its spaces removed (see below), and the age is an integer.

docs.title: 4.7.5. Execution
docs.text:
Let’s submit a form full of errors: a name consisting of spaces, an address without a full domain, an age of 12, a password that’s too short, and a different confirmation:

The input has been retained (except for the passwords), and each error is flagged below its corresponding field. The name consisting of spaces is flagged as missing: the Form component removes the spaces surrounding each entry (field option [trim], set to true by default). The password, however, has only one error, which is in the confirmation: when the two entries differ, the [RepeatedType] field returns no value, and the length is not checked. URL is the form’s ID, and [/inscription] indicates that the page was displayed by the action in response to POST. With [curl], by providing the anti-CSRF token as in Example 18, you can also send something a browser would not send—a non-numeric age:

curl -i -b cookies.txt -g --data-urlencode "inscription[_token]=..." -d "inscription[nom]=Martin&inscription[email]=martin@exemple.fr&inscription[age]=abc&inscription[motDePasse][first]=abcdef&inscription[motDePasse][second]=abcdef" http://localhost:8000/registration

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content
...
<input type="number" id="inscription_age" name="inscription[age]" required="required" min="18" max="120" aria-describedby="inscription_age_error1" aria-invalid="true" class="form-control is-invalid" value="abc" />
<div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="inscription_age_error1">Un nombre entier est attendu.</div>
...

We see the input redisplayed, along with the attributes HTML5 ([required], [min], [max]), the class [is-invalid], the conversion message, and the attributes [aria-...], which link the field to its message for screen readers.

docs.title: 4.7.6. Browser validation
docs.text:
Let’s remove the [novalidate] attribute by following the “Enable” link (parameter [?html5=true]). The browser then checks the attributes [required], [type="email"], [min], [maxlength]... before submitting the form, and displays its own messages in a tooltip below the first field with an error (“Please fill in this field,” “The value must be greater than or equal to 18,” etc.): the form is not submitted as long as there is an error. [Symfony] automatically generates these attributes: [required] for any field (option [required], e.g., 18), [type="email"] and [type="number"] based on the field type; [maxlength], [min], [max], and [minlength] come from our [attr] options. They must remain consistent with the constraints.

This validation is convenient for the user: it’s immediate, with no back-and-forth with the server. But it does not replace server-side validation: a user can disable it, and a program like [curl] ignores it completely. The rule is absolute: the server always validates; browser-side validation is merely an added convenience.

A correct entry, at last. The name, entered with spaces on either side, was cleaned up by the form:

docs.title: 4.8. Example 20: The Post/Redirect/Get Pattern
docs.text:
When a POST action responds with a page, that page is the result of a POST. If the user reloads the page (presses [F5]), the browser sends the POST request, after displaying a warning that few people read: the command is sent twice, and the message is posted twice. The Post/Redirect/Get pattern (PRG) avoids this problem: a successful POST action does not return a page; it responds with a redirect (example 04) to a page GET, which the browser requests immediately. Reloading this page simply re-executes the GET action.

One problem remains: the GET page would like to display a message (“the task has been added”), but it is the POST action that knows this message, and it cannot pass a variable to a request that has not yet occurred. The solution: the flash message, placed in the session by the action POST, is retained until it is read, displayed, and then discarded.

docs.title: 4.8.1. Configuration: config/packages/framework.yaml
docs.text:
# config/packages/framework.yaml: the configuration for FrameworkBundle
framework:
    secret: '%env(APP_SECRET)%'
     # SESSION: its data is stored on the server, one file per session,
     # in the var/sessions/dev directory (handler_id: null: the files for PHP itself)
    session:
        handler_id: null
        save_path: '%kernel.project_dir%/var/sessions/%kernel.environment%'
     # VERROUS (Lock component): flocked files in the var/lock directory
    lock: 'flock://%kernel.project_dir%/var/lock'
  • Lines 6–8: the user’s session (chapter on scopes): browser-specific data, retained from one request to the next. It is stored on the server; the browser holds only an identifier for it, in a cookie. [handler_id: null] delegates the task of storing this data to [PHP] itself, which stores each session in a file; [save_path] selects the folder—[var/sessions/dev]—so that we can examine them. [%kernel.environment%] is the environment ([dev]);
  • line 10: the locks (the Lock component, described below), stored in the folder [var/lock].

docs.title: 4.8.2. The service: src/Service/TachesService.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Service/TachesService.php: the list of tasks, shared by all
// users. In PHP, objects are not retained after the request: the list is
// stored in the application’s CACHE (here, a file in the var/cache/dev/pools directory)

namespace App\Service;

use Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Lock\LockFactory;

class TachesService
{
    private const CLE = 'taches';

     // the application cache (the cache.app service) and the lock factory
    public function __construct(
        private CacheItemPoolInterface $cache,
        private LockFactory $verrous,
    ) {
    }

     /** @return list<string> */
    public function liste(): array
    {
         // the cache entry stored under the key [taches]; isHit: it exists
        $element = $this->cache->getItem(self::CLE);
        return $element->isHit() ? $element->get() : ['Lire le chapitre 3'];
    }

    public function ajouter(string $libelle): void
    {
         // multiple requests may be running EN MÊME TEMPS (the server
         // processes them in multiple processes): a lock ensures that only one at a
         // time reads, modifies, and rewrites the list
        $verrou = $this->verrous->createLock('taches');
         // acquire(true): wait for the lock to become available, then acquire it
        $verrou->acquire(true);
        try {
            $taches = $this->liste();
            $taches[] = $libelle;
             // the cache entry receives its new value, with no time limit
            $element = $this->cache->getItem(self::CLE);
            $this->cache->save($element->set($taches));
        } finally {
             // finally: the lock is released in all cases, even after an exception
            $verrou->release();
        }
    }
}

The task list is shared by all users and must persist from one request to the next. In [Java], [C#], or [Python], it would be kept in memory within a single service. In [PHP], this is impossible: as we saw in examples 01 and 06, nothing survives the request. The list must therefore be stored outside of [PHP]: in a database, a file... or in the application cache, which we are using here.

  • Lines 16–20: The service receives two services from [Symfony]. The first is the application cache (the [cache.app] service, from the Cache component), a store of key-value pairs, represented by the standardized interface [CacheItemPoolInterface] (the PSR-6 standard). By default, it stores its values in files within the [var/cache/dev/pools] folder; in production, a dedicated server is preferred, such as [Redis] (a configuration line). The second is the lock factory of the Lock component;
  • lines 23–28: [getItem] retrieves the cache item stored under a key; [isHit] checks if it exists, and [get] returns its value. Any value (in this case, an array of strings) can be stored: [Symfony] serializes it—that is, it converts it to text—using the function [serialize] from [PHP];
  • Lines 35–47: The development server, like a production server, can process multiple requests at the same time, across multiple processes (the environment variable [PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS] sets the number of processes to [php -S]). Two simultaneous additions could read the same list, each add its own task to it, and then write it back: the second write would overwrite the first task. A lock ensures that only one request at a time executes the code it protects: [createLock('taches')] creates a named lock; [acquire(true)] waits for it to become available, then acquires it; [release()] releases it. Here, the lock is a file in the [var/lock] folder, locked by the operating system (the [flock] function); alternatively, multiple servers would share a lock stored in [Redis] or in a database;
  • lines 38–47: the block [try] … [finally] ensures that the lock is released in all cases, even if an exception interrupts the code it protects;
  • lines 42–43: the cache element receives its new value ([set]), then it is saved ([save]). Without a specified lifetime, it is retained indefinitely ([expiresAfter(3600)] would retain it for one hour).

docs.title: 4.8.3. The controller: src/Controller/TachesController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/TachesController.php: the Post/Redirect/Get pattern

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Service\TachesService;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

class TachesController extends AbstractController
{
    public function __construct(private TachesService $taches)
    {
    }

     // GET /tasks: the list and the add form
     #[Route('/taches', name: 'taches', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function afficher(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('taches/taches.html.twig', ['taches' => $this->taches->liste()]);
    }

     // POST /tasks: the Post/Redirect/Get pattern
     #[Route('/taches', name: 'taches_ajouter', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function ajouter(Request $request): Response
    {
        $libelle = trim($request->request->getString('libelle'));
        if ($libelle === '' || mb_strlen($libelle) > 40) {
             // Invalid input: the page is reloaded without redirection
            return $this->render('taches/taches.html.twig', ['taches' => $this->taches->liste(),
                'libelle' => $libelle,
                'erreur' => 'Le libellé doit comporter de 1 à 40 caractères.']);
        }
        $this->taches->ajouter($libelle);
         // addFlash sets a "flash" message in the session: it will survive the
         // redirect, for the request SUIVANTE
        $this->addFlash('succes', "La tâche [$libelle] a été ajoutée.");
         // no page: a redirect to the page GET
        return $this->redirectToRoute('taches');
    }

     // POST /tasks/no-program: the counterexample (a page in response to POST)
     #[Route('/taches/sans-prg', name: 'taches_sans_prg', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function ajouterSansPrg(Request $request): Response
    {
        $this->taches->ajouter(trim($request->request->getString('libelle')) ?: '(sans titre)');
        return $this->render('taches/taches.html.twig', ['taches' => $this->taches->liste(), 'sansPrg' => true]);
    }
}
  • lines 29–35: The input is validated manually to keep the example concise ([trim] removes the surrounding spaces). An invalid entry is redisplayed without redirection: there is nothing to protect against a duplicate submission, since nothing has been modified;
  • line 39: the method [addFlash] of [AbstractController] places a flash message of type [succes] in the session (the type is arbitrary: it allows distinguishing between success and error messages, etc.);
  • line 41: the redirection to the page GET, named [taches] (example 04);
  • lines 45–50: the counterexample: a page in response to POST. The operator [?:] returns its left operand if it is “true” (here, a non-empty string), and the right operand otherwise.

  <title>Tâches</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ path('bootstrap', {fichier: 'css/bootstrap.min.css'}) }}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('css/styles.css') }}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
    {# flash messages [succes], at the top of the page: submitted AVANT the redirect;
       app.flashes les RETIRE de la session en les lisant #}
    {% for message in app.flashes('succes') %}
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ message }}</div>
    {% endfor %}
    <main>
      {% block contenu %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% if erreur is defined %}
      <div class="zone-erreur" role="alert">{{ erreur }}</div>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</body>
</html>
  • Lines 13–15: [app.flashes('succes')] returns the list of flash messages of type [succes] and removes them from the session: a flash message is displayed only once. The [alert alert-success] class of [Bootstrap] displays the message in a green frame;
  • lines 19–21: the error message, at the bottom of the page, when the action has generated one.
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h1 class="h3">Mes tâches</h1>
  <ol>
    {% for tache in taches %}
      <li>{{ tache }}</li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ol>
  <form method="post" action="{{ path('taches_ajouter') }}" class="d-flex gap-2">
    <input class="form-control" name="libelle" value="{{ libelle ?? '' }}" placeholder="Nouvelle tâche">
    <button class="btn btn-primary text-nowrap" type="submit">Ajouter</button>
    {# form submission: this button sends the MÊME form to another address #}
    <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary text-nowrap" type="submit" formaction="{{ path('taches_sans_prg') }}">Ajouter sans PRG</button>
  </form>
  {% if sansPrg is defined %}
    <p class="text-danger mt-2">Page affichée en réponse à un POST : appuyez sur F5 et la tâche sera ajoutée une seconde fois.</p>
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}
  • line 11: the operator [??] of [Twig] returns its right-hand operand if the left-hand operand does not exist (or is equal to [null]): the variable [libelle] exists only after an invalid entry;
  • Line 14: A button’s [formaction] attribute submits the form to an address different from that specified by its [action] attribute: a single form can thus trigger two different actions.

This hand-coded form lacks an anti-CSRF token: to keep the example simple, we’ll add it in the next example.

docs.title: 4.8.5. Where are flash messages stored?
docs.text:
Between the request POST and the subsequent request GET, the message must be stored somewhere: in the user’s session or on the server. Let’s examine this with [curl], while storing the cookies in a file (options [-c] and [-b], Example 18):

curl -i -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt -d "libelle=Faire%20les%20exercices" http://localhost:8000/tasks

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate, private
Location: /taches
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Expires: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 09:36:41 GMT
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=1e1f574eccd93268b1eb829dd714a029; path=/; httponly; samesite=lax
...

The response to POST is a redirect (status code 302, header [Location]), accompanied by the session cookie, [PHPSESSID] (the name that [PHP] assigns to this cookie), which contains the session ID: 32 random characters that are impossible to guess. This cookie is [httponly] (the [JavaScript] on the page cannot read it) and [samesite=lax] (the browser does not send it with a POST request originating from another site). The headers [Cache-Control] and [Expires] prevent the caching of a response that depends on a session. The identifier is also the name of the session file on the server: [var/sessions/dev/sess_1e1f574eccd93268b1eb829dd714a029]. Here is that file, following the request POST:

_symfony_flashes|a:1:{s:6:"succes";a:1:{i:0;s:49:"La tâche [Faire les exercices] a été ajoutée.";}}_sf2_meta|a:3:{s:1:"u";i:1790501801;s:1:"c";i:1790501801;s:1:"l";i:0;}

This is the serialization format for sessions in [PHP]: each piece of session data is written in the form [nom|valeur sérialisée]. [a:1:{...}] declares an array with 1 element, [s:6:"succes"] a 6-byte string... It contains flash messages ([_symfony_flashes]), sorted by type, and metadata from [Symfony] ([_sf2_meta]: the session’s creation and last-used dates). Let’s follow the redirect by sending the cookie back:

curl -i -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt http://localhost:8000/tasks

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
              <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">La tâche [Faire les exercices] a été ajoutée.</div>
...
          <li>Lire le chapitre 3</li>
          <li>Faire les exercices</li>
...

The message is displayed and removed from the session by [app.flashes]. The session, now empty, has even disappeared: [Symfony] does not store an empty session, and the file has been deleted. A new request, GET, would no longer display the message. The task list, however, is stored in a cache file, whose name is calculated based on the key ([var/cache/dev/pools/app/VT2eLxVxyZ/T/U/kAplxOBLatpb5XP0GkrA]):

0
taches
a:2:{i:0;s:18:"Lire le chapitre 3";i:1;s:19:"Faire les exercices";}

The first line is the value’s expiration date (0: never), the second is the key, and the third is the serialized list. As for the lock, it is an empty file, [var/lock/sf.taches.hngbec7.lock], which the system locks for the duration of a modification.

docs.title: 4.8.6. Execution
docs.text:
Adding a task: the browser followed the redirect; URL is the page corresponding to GET, which can be safely reloaded.

An invalid entry, redisplayed with its error message:

The counterexample: the page is the response to POST, and its URL is [/taches/sans-prg]. If you click on [F5], the browser asks if you want to resubmit the form; if you agree, the task is added a second time.

docs.title: 4.9. Example 21: Links, Buttons, and Confirmation
docs.text:
A principle of the HTTP protocol: a GET request does not change anything. Browsers, search engines, and tools that preload pages freely follow links without asking the user for permission. A “delete” link ([<a href="/contacts/2/supprimer">]) would therefore be dangerous: a bot crawling the site would delete everything. In a web application:

  • viewing is done via a link ([<a href>]), which sends a GET request;
  • editing (save, duplicate, delete) is done via a button placed in a form, protected by an anti-CSRF token.

This example manages a contact list and displays a confirmation window before each deletion.

docs.title: 4.9.1. Configuration: config/packages/framework.yaml
docs.text:
# config/packages/framework.yaml: the configuration for FrameworkBundle
framework:
    secret: '%env(APP_SECRET)%'
     # A form POST containing a field _method (DELETE, PUT...) is processed
     # as a request for this method
    http_method_override: true
     # the session (flash messages, anti-CSRF tokens), stored in var/sessions (see example 20)
    session:
        handler_id: null
        save_path: '%kernel.project_dir%/var/sessions/%kernel.environment%'
    csrf_protection: true
    lock: 'flock://%kernel.project_dir%/var/lock'
  • Line 6: A HTML form can only send GET and POST requests. However, the HTTP protocol provides for other methods: DELETE for deletion, and PUT and PATCH for modification. [Symfony] circumvents this limitation: with the [http_method_override] option, a POST form containing a hidden field [_method] with a value of [DELETE] (or [PUT], [PATCH]), is treated as a request for that method. This is method spoofing;
  • the other lines are those from examples 18 and 20: the session, CSRF protection, and locks.

docs.title: 4.9.2. The service: src/Service/ContactsService.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Service/ContactsService.php: contacts, shared by all, stored in
// the application cache (see Example 20)

namespace App\Service;

use App\Modele\Contact;
use Psr\Cache\CacheItemPoolInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Lock\LockFactory;

class ContactsService
{
    private const CLE = 'contacts';

    public function __construct(
        private CacheItemPoolInterface $cache,
        private LockFactory $verrous,
    ) {
    }

     /** @return array{contacts: list<Contact>, dernierId: int} */
    private function donnees(): array
    {
        $element = $this->cache->getItem(self::CLE);
        return $element->isHit() ? $element->get() : [
            'contacts' => [
                new Contact(1, 'Marie Durand', '01 23 45 67 89'),
                new Contact(2, 'Paul Martin', '06 12 34 56 78'),
                new Contact(3, 'Philippe Jandot', '02 98 76 54 32'),
            ],
            'dernierId' => 3,
        ];
    }

     // a data modification, under a lock: the function receives the data,
     // modifies it (&), and returns the result of the operation
    private function modifierDonnees(callable $operation): mixed
    {
        $verrou = $this->verrous->createLock('contacts');
        $verrou->acquire(true);
        try {
            $donnees = $this->donnees();
            $resultat = $operation($donnees);
            $this->cache->save($this->cache->getItem(self::CLE)->set($donnees));
            return $resultat;
        } finally {
            $verrou->release();
        }
    }

     /** @return list<Contact> */
    public function liste(): array
    {
        return $this->donnees()['contacts'];
    }

     // the contact, or null if it does not exist
    public function lire(int $id): ?Contact
    {
        return array_find($this->liste(), fn (Contact $c) => $c->id === $id);
    }

    public function modifier(int $id, string $nom, string $telephone): ?Contact
    {
        return $this->modifierDonnees(function (array &$donnees) use ($id, $nom, $telephone) {
            foreach ($donnees['contacts'] as $i => $contact) {
                if ($contact->id === $id) {
                     // A contact is immutable (read-only): a new one is created,
                     // which replaces the old one in the array
                    return $donnees['contacts'][$i] = new Contact($id, $nom, $telephone);
                }
            }
            return null;
        });
    }

    public function ajouter(string $nom, string $telephone): Contact
    {
        return $this->modifierDonnees(function (array &$donnees) use ($nom, $telephone) {
            $contact = new Contact(++$donnees['dernierId'], $nom, $telephone);
            $donnees['contacts'][] = $contact;
            return $contact;
        });
    }

    public function supprimer(int $id): ?Contact
    {
        return $this->modifierDonnees(function (array &$donnees) use ($id) {
            foreach ($donnees['contacts'] as $i => $contact) {
                if ($contact->id === $id) {
                     // array_splice removes element i from the array and renumbers the subsequent elements
                    array_splice($donnees['contacts'], $i, 1);
                    return $contact;
                }
            }
            return null;
        });
    }
}

The contacts are stored in the cache, just like the tasks in Example 20. Each contact is an immutable object [Contact] (an ID, a name, a phone number), stored in an array, with the most recently assigned ID. A few points about [PHP]:

  • lines 37–49: All modifications follow the same pattern: acquire the lock, read the data, modify it, write it back, and release the lock. This method writes to the array once; each modification passes it a function (of type [callable], “callable”), which receives the data and modifies it. The function must modify the array itself, not a copy: its parameter is declared as [array &$donnees], where [&] specifies a pass-by-reference (without [&], an array is copied; see Example 06). The keyword [use] in an anonymous function gives it access to variables in the containing function (line 65: [$id], [$nom], [$telephone]);
  • line 44: the calls follow one after another: [getItem] returns the element, [set] assigns a value to it and returns the element itself, [save] stores it;
  • lines 63–75: A contact is immutable: a new one is created, which replaces the old one in the array. An assignment is an expression whose value is the assigned value: [return $donnees['contacts'][$i] = new Contact(...)] replaces the contact and returns it;
  • line 80: [++] placed before a variable increments it by 1 and returns the new value;
  • line 92: [array_splice] removes an element from the array and renumbers the subsequent elements;
  • The methods return [null] for a nonexistent contact: it is up to the controller to decide on the response.

docs.title: 4.9.3. The form for the record: src/Form/ContactType.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Form/ContactType.php: the contact form, with DEUX submit buttons

namespace App\Form;

use Symfony\Component\Form\AbstractType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\SubmitType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\Extension\Core\Type\TextType;
use Symfony\Component\Form\FormBuilderInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints\NotBlank;

class ContactType extends AbstractType
{
    public function buildForm(FormBuilderInterface $constructeur, array $options): void
    {
        $constructeur
            ->add('nom', TextType::class, ['constraints' => [new NotBlank()]])
            ->add('telephone', TextType::class, ['label' => 'Téléphone', 'constraints' => [new NotBlank()]])
             // two submit buttons: the form will know which one was clicked
            ->add('enregistrer', SubmitType::class, ['attr' => ['class' => 'btn-primary']])
            ->add('dupliquer', SubmitType::class, ['attr' => ['class' => 'btn-outline-primary']]);
    }
}
  • lines 17–18: the two fields are required;

docs.title: 4.9.4. The controller: src/Controller/ContactsController.php
docs.text:
<?php
// src/Controller/ContactsController.php: links (GET) and buttons (POST, DELETE)

namespace App\Controller;

use App\Form\ContactType;
use App\Modele\Contact;
use App\Service\ContactsService;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\Form\SubmitButton;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\AccessDeniedHttpException;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;

#[Route('/contacts', name: 'contacts')]
class ContactsController extends AbstractController
{
    public function __construct(private ContactsService $contacts)
    {
    }

     // the contact, or a 404 response if it does not exist
    private function contactOu404(?Contact $contact): Contact
    {
        return $contact ?? throw $this->createNotFoundException('contact inconnu');
    }

     // a LIEN (<a href>): a GET request, which does not modify anything
     #[Route('', name: '', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function liste(): Response
    {
        return $this->render('contacts/liste.html.twig', ['contacts' => $this->contacts->liste()]);
    }

     // GET /contacts/2: the profile; POST /contacts/2: one of its two buttons
     #[Route('/{id<\d+>}', name: '_fiche', methods: ['GET', 'POST'])]
    public function fiche(Request $request, int $id): Response
    {
        $contact = $this->contactOu404($this->contacts->lire($id));
        $formulaire = $this->createForm(ContactType::class,
            ['nom' => $contact->nom, 'telephone' => $contact->telephone]);
        $formulaire->handleRequest($request);
        if ($formulaire->isSubmitted() && $formulaire->isValid()) {
            ['nom' => $nom, 'telephone' => $telephone] = $formulaire->getData();
            $dupliquer = $formulaire->get('dupliquer');
             // isClicked: the button that submitted the form
            if ($dupliquer instanceof SubmitButton && $dupliquer->isClicked()) {
                $copie = $this->contacts->ajouter("$nom (copie)", $telephone);
                $this->addFlash('succes', "Le contact [$copie->nom] a été créé.");
            } else {
                $this->contacts->modifier($id, $nom, $telephone);
                $this->addFlash('succes', "Le contact [$nom] a été modifié.");
            }
            return $this->redirectToRoute('contacts');
        }
        return $this->render('contacts/fiche.html.twig', ['contact' => $contact, 'formulaire' => $formulaire]);
    }

     // a request DELETE, simulated by a form POST (hidden field _method)
     #[Route('/{id<\d+>}', name: '_supprimer', methods: ['DELETE'])]
    public function supprimer(Request $request, int $id): Response
    {
         // the form's anti-CSRF token, specific to this contact
        if (! $this->isCsrfTokenValid("supprimer-contact-$id", $request->request->getString('_token'))) {
            throw new AccessDeniedHttpException('jeton anti-CSRF invalide');
        }
        $contact = $this->contactOu404($this->contacts->supprimer($id));
        $this->addFlash('succes', "Le contact [$contact->nom] a été supprimé.");
        return $this->redirectToRoute('contacts');
    }
}
  • line 16: the name prefix [contacts]: the route for the list, whose name is empty (line 30), is therefore called [contacts], and the one for the record is [contacts_fiche]...;
  • lines 24–27: a utility function: a nonexistent contact stops the action with a 404 response;
  • lines 30–34: the GET action in the list, which does not modify anything;
  • lines 37–58: a contact’s record. In GET, it displays the form, populated with the contact’s information; in POST, it processes it. The same URL and [/contacts/2] are thus used for both viewing and saving;
  • line 45: the form data, an unstructured associative array: [['nom' => $nom, 'telephone' => $telephone] = ...] stores each element in a variable;
  • lines 46–54: [get('dupliquer')] renders the [dupliquer] button on the form; [isClicked()] determines whether it was the one that submitted the form (the [instanceof SubmitButton] test confirms the object type to the editor). Depending on the button, the action either duplicates or saves the contact;
  • line 55: in both cases, the PRG schema (example 20), with a flash message;
  • lines 61–71: deletion, handled by a DELETE request (the same as URL, but using a different method). The delete form is hard-coded in the view: the action verifies its own anti-CSRF token using the [isCsrfTokenValid] method from [AbstractController]. A token is linked to an identifier (here, [supprimer-contact-2]): a form’s token is valid only for that form. A missing or invalid token stops the action with a 403 error (Forbidden). (The [#[IsCsrfTokenValid('...')]] attribute, set on the action, would perform the same validation.)

docs.title: 4.9.6. The confirmation window
docs.text:
The browser can display a confirmation dialog (functions [JavaScript] and [confirm]), but it is not very attractive, and its appearance depends on the browser. Here we use a modal window from [Bootstrap], displayed using a few lines of [JavaScript]. The window is a fragment included in the template and is therefore present—though hidden—on all pages:

{# a single window for the entire page, hidden (d-none) by default #}
<div id="modale-confirmation" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title">Confirmation</h5>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="modale-confirmation-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="non">Non, revenir</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="oui">Oui, confirmer</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 2: the [d-none] class from [Bootstrap] hides the element;
  • lines 3–4: the gray background, followed by the window, are rendered by the classes of [Bootstrap];
  • line 11: the message's position;
  • lines 14–15: the two buttons, of type [button] (not [submit]: they do not submit any form), distinguished by their [data-action] attribute.
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Contacts</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ path('bootstrap', {fichier: 'css/bootstrap.min.css'}) }}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ asset('css/styles.css') }}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 40rem">
    {% for message in app.flashes('succes') %}
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ message }}</div>
    {% endfor %}
    <main>
      {% block contenu %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
  </div>
  {# the confirmation window, present on all pages #}
  {% include 'fragments/confirmation.html.twig' %}
  {# the script, at the bottom of the page: the elements it looks for already exist #}
  <script src="{{ asset('js/app.js') }}"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • line 19: the window, included on all pages;
  • line 21: the script, placed at the end of the page: when it runs, the elements it searches for already exist. It is stored in the [public/js] folder.

The script [public/js/app.js]:

// Confirmation for forms with the data-confirmation="..." attribute
// Without JavaScript, these forms are simply submitted without confirmation.
(() => {
  const modale = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation');
  const message = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation-message');
  let enAttente = null; // The form to submit if confirmation is given

   // 1. We intercept the submission of forms requiring confirmation
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((formulaire) => {
    formulaire.addEventListener('submit', (evenement) => {
      evenement.preventDefault(); // The submission is suspended
      enAttente = formulaire;
      message.textContent = formulaire.dataset.confirmation;
      modale.classList.remove('d-none'); // the window appears
    });
  });

   // 2. The two buttons in the window
  modale.addEventListener('click', (evenement) => {
    const action = evenement.target.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'oui') {
      enAttente.submit(); // Submit, SANS trigger the 'submit' event again
    } else if (action === 'non') {
      modale.classList.add('d-none');
      enAttente = null;
    }
  });
})();
  • line 3: the code is enclosed in an anonymous function, which is executed immediately; its variables do not interfere with those of the other scripts on the page;
  • lines 4–6: the window, the message location, and the form awaiting confirmation;
  • lines 9–17: for each form that has a [data-confirmation] attribute, the [submit] event—triggered when the form is submitted—is intercepted. [preventDefault()] suspends submission; the form is put on hold, and its message ([dataset.confirmation], the value of the [data-confirmation] attribute) is displayed in the window, which appears;
  • lines 20–28: a single handler for clicks in the window: [evenement.target] is the element clicked; its attribute [data-action] specifies which button it is. "Yes" submits the pending form using the [submit()] method, which—unlike clicking a button—does not trigger the [submit] event (otherwise, the window would reappear); "No" hides the window.

Without [JavaScript], the form is simply submitted without confirmation: the page remains usable. This is incremental improvement: [JavaScript] adds convenience, but the application does not depend on it.

docs.title: 4.9.7. Execution

Clicking “Delete” displays the confirmation window:

After confirmation, the (simulated) query DELETE, the redirection, and the pop-up message:

A contact’s profile, with its two send buttons:

A request without an anti-CSRF token is rejected, and a nonexistent contact returns a 404 error:

curl -i -X POST -d "_method=DELETE" http://localhost:8000/contacts/3
curl -i http://localhost:8000/contacts/9

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Debug-Exception: jeton%20anti-CSRF%20invalide
...
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
X-Debug-Exception: contact%20inconnu
...

The error pages are still the detailed ones from the debug mode of [Symfony]. The chapter on the request lifecycle will show how to replace them with custom pages.
